p0.original: PART I. Of the Expense of Defence.

p1.original: The first duty of the sovereign, that of protecting the society from the violence and invasion of other independent societies, can be performed only by means of a military force. But the expense both of preparing this military force in time of peace, and of employing it in time of war, is very different in the different states of society, in the different periods of improvement.
p1.zh: 主权者的首要义务,即保护社会免遭暴力和其他独立社会的入侵,只能通过军事力量来履行。 但是,在和平时期准备这种军事力量,在战时使用这种军队,其代价在不同的社会状态,不同的改良时期,却大不相同.

p2.original: Among nations of hunters, the lowest and rudest state of society, such as we find it among the native tribes of North America, every man is a warrior, as well as a hunter. When he goes to war, either to defend his society, or to revenge the injuries which have been done to it by other societies, he maintains himself by his own labour, in the same manner as when he lives at home. His society (for in this state of things there is properly neither sovereign nor commonwealth) is at no sort of expense, either to prepare him for the field, or to maintain him while he is in it.
p2.zh: 在猎人民族中,社会最低和最粗鲁的状态,比如我们发现在北美的原住民部落中,每个人都是战士,也是猎人. 当他去打仗时,要么是为了保卫自己的社会,要么是为了报复其他社会对它造成的伤害,他依靠自己的劳动维持自己,就像他住在家中一样。 他的社会(因为在这个状态下,没有主权或联邦)是没有代价的,无论是准备他去田野,还是在田野期间维持他.

p3.original: Among nations of shepherds, a more advanced state of society, such as we find it among the Tartars and Arabs, every man is, in the same manner, a warrior. Such nations have commonly no fixed habitation, but live either in tents, or in a sort of covered waggons, which are easily transported from place to place. The whole tribe, or nation, changes its situation according to the different seasons of the year, as well as according to other accidents. When its herds and flocks have consumed the forage of one part of the country, it removes to another, and from that to a third. In the dry season, it comes down to the banks of the rivers; in the wet season, it retires to the upper country. When such a nation goes to war, the warriors will not trust their herds and flocks to the feeble defence of their old men, their women and children; and their old men, their women and children, will not be left behind without defence, and without subsistence. The whole nation, besides, being accustomed to a wandering life, even in time of peace, easily takes the field in time of war. Whether it marches as an army, or moves about as a company of herdsmen, the way of life is nearly the same, though the object proposed by it be very different. They all go to war together, therefore, and everyone does as well as he can. Among the Tartars, even the women have been frequently known to engage in battle. If they conquer, whatever belongs to the hostile tribe is the recompence of the victory; but if they are vanquished, all is lost; and not only their herds and flocks, but their women and children become the booty of the conqueror. Even the greater part of those who survive the action are obliged to submit to him for the sake of immediate subsistence. The rest are commonly dissipated and dispersed in the desert.
p3.zh: 在牧羊人的国家中,我们发现在鞑靼人和阿拉伯人中间,社会更加发达的状态,每个人都以同样的方式成为战士.这些国家通常没有固定住所,而是住在帐篷里,或者住在某种被覆盖的胡萝卜上,很容易从地方运送到地方。整个部落,或民族,根据当年的不同季节,以及其他事故,改变自己的处境.其畜群和羊群耗尽了全国某地的饲料后,便将它移到另一地,从那里移到三分之一.旱季时,降于河岸;湿季时,退居上乡.这样的民族去打仗的时候,武士们不会相信自己的群羊群,只能依靠老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵,老兵整个民族,除了习惯流浪的生活外,即使在和平时期,也很容易在战争时期夺取田地.无论是作为军队进军,还是作为牧民的连队移动,生活方式几乎相同,尽管它提出的物体非常不同. 因此,他们都一起参战,每个人都尽他所能。 在鞑靼人中,甚至连妇女也经常被人们称为参与战斗. 如果他们征服了,无论属于敌对部落的什么,都是胜利的回报;但是如果他们被打败,一切就都失去了;不仅他们的牧群和羊群,而且他们的妇女和儿童成为征服者的战利品.即使是在行动中幸存下来的大多数人也不得不为了立即生存而向他屈服。其余的通常散落于沙漠中.

p4.original: The ordinary life, the ordinary exercise of a Tartar or Arab, prepares him sufficiently for war. Running, wrestling, cudgel-playing, throwing the javelin, drawing the bow, etc. are the common pastimes of those who live in the open air, and are all of them the images of war. When a Tartar or Arab actually goes to war, he is maintained by his own herds and flocks, which he carries with him, in the same manner as in peace. His chief or sovereign (for those nations have all chiefs or sovereigns) is at no sort of expense in preparing him for the field; and when he is in it, the chance of plunder is the only pay which he either expects or requires.
p4.zh: 普通的生活,一个鞑靼人或阿拉伯人的正常行使,足以让他为战争做好准备.奔跑,摔跤,摇摆,扔下贾维林,画弓等,是露天生活的人们常见的消遣,都是战争的画面. 当一个鞑靼人或阿拉伯人真的去打仗时,他由自己的牧群和羊群来维持,他带着这些羊群和羊群,与平时一样. 他的酋长或君主(对于这些国家来说,他们都有酋长或君主)在为他准备战地方面是不会花费任何代价的;当他身处战地时,掠夺的机会是他所期望或要求的唯一报酬.

p5.original: An army of hunters can seldom exceed two or three hundred men. The precarious subsistence which the chace affords, could seldom allow a greater number to keep together for any considerable time. An army of shepherds, on the contrary, may sometimes amount to two or three hundred thousand. As long as nothing stops their progress, as long as they can go on from one district, of which they have consumed the forage, to another, which is yet entire; there seems to be scarce any limit to the number who can march on together. A nation of hunters can never be formidable to the civilized nations in their neighbourhood; a nation of shepherds may. Nothing can be more contemptible than an Indian war in North America; nothing, on the contrary, can be more dreadful than a Tartar invasion has frequently been in Asia. The judgment of Thucydides, that both Europe and Asia could not resist the Scythians united, has been verified by the experience of all ages. The inhabitants of the extensive, but defenceless plains of Scythia or Tartary, have been frequently united under the dominion of the chief of some conquering horde or clan; and the havock and devastation of Asia have always signalized their union. The inhabitants of the inhospitable deserts of Arabia, the other great nation of shepherds, have never been united but once, under Mahomet and his immediate successors. Their union, which was more the effect of religious enthusiasm than of conquest, was signalized in the same manner. If the hunting nations of America should ever become shepherds, their neighbourhood would be much more dangerous to the European colonies than it is at present.
p5.zh: 一支猎人军队很少能超过两三百人.钱财提供的不稳定的生计,很少能使更多的人能够维持任何相当长的时间。 相反,牧羊人的军队有时可能达到2或30万。 只要没有什么能阻止他们的进步,只要他们能够从一个他们已经消耗了饲料的区,到另一个已经完全完全的区,他们就可以继续前进;能够一起前进的人数似乎没有多少限制。 一个猎人的国家对邻近的文明国家来说永远不会强大;一个牧羊人的国家可能如此。 最可鄙的莫过于北美的印度战争;相反,最可怕的莫过于亚洲经常发生鞑靼人的入侵。Thucydides的判断,欧洲和亚洲都无法抵抗锡斯人联合,这些判断都得到了所有年龄层的经验的证实.斯cythia或Tartary这些大片、但毫无防御能力的平原的居民,经常在征服部落或部族的酋长的统治下团结起来;亚洲的破坏和破坏始终表明他们的联盟。阿拉伯荒漠中的居民,另一个伟大的牧羊国,从来没有统一过,而是在马霍梅及其直接的继任者之下统一过一次. 他们的结合,与其说是征服,不如说是宗教热情的效果,也是以同样的方式发出信号的. 如果美国的狩猎国成为牧羊人,那么他们的邻居对欧洲殖民地来说比现在危险得多.

p6.original: In a yet more advanced state of society, among those nations of husbandmen who have little foreign commerce, and no other manufactures but those coarse and household ones, which almost every private family prepares for its own use, every man, in the same manner, either is a warrior, or easily becomes such. Those who live by agriculture generally pass the whole day in the open air, exposed to all the inclemencies of the seasons. The hardiness of their ordinary life prepares them for the fatigues of war, to some of which their necessary occupations bear a great analogy. The necessary occupation of a ditcher prepares him to work in the trenches, and to fortify a camp, as well as to inclose a field. The ordinary pastimes of such husbandmen are the same as those of shepherds, and are in the same manner the images of war. But as husbandmen have less leisure than shepherds, they are not so frequently employed in those pastimes. They are soldiers but soldiers not quite so much masters of their exercise. Such as they are, however, it seldom costs the sovereign or commonwealth any expense to prepare them for the field.
p6.zh: 在一个更先进的社会状况中,在那些几乎没有对外商业的夫家国家中,除了那些粗俗的和家庭的制造品之外,其他的制造品几乎都是每个私人家庭为自己的使用作准备的,每个人以同样的方式,要么是一个战士,要么很容易成为战士。以农业为生的人一般在露天中通过一整天,暴露在季节的所有的内涵中. 他们平凡生活的硬性,使他们为战争的疲劳做好准备,对于其中的一些,他们必要的职业有很强的类比.必要地占领一个沟渠者,使他准备在壕沟里工作,并加固一个营地,以及封闭一个田地. 这种丈夫的普通消遣与牧羊人一样,也是战争的画面. 但是,由于丈夫比牧羊人闲得更少,因此在那些消遣中,他们没有那么频繁地受雇于人. 他们是士兵,但士兵们并不怎么精通他们的锻炼。 然而,尽管如此,主权或联邦很少花费任何费用来为实地做好准备。

p7.original: Agriculture, even in its rudest and lowest state, supposes a settlement, some sort of fixed habitation, which cannot be abandoned without great loss. When a nation of mere husbandmen, therefore, goes to war, the whole people cannot take the field together. The old men, the women and children, at least, must remain at home, to take care of the habitation. All the men of the military age, however, may take the field, and in small nations of this kind, have frequently done so. In every nation, the men of the military age are supposed to amount to about a fourth or a fifth part of the whole body of the people. If the campaign, too, should begin after seedtime, and end before harvest, both the husbandman and his principal labourers can be spared from the farm without much loss. He trusts that the work which must be done in the mean time, can be well enough executed by the old men, the women, and the children. He is not unwilling, therefore, to serve without pay during a short campaign; and it frequently costs the sovereign or commonwealth as little to maintain him in the field as to prepare him for it. The citizens of all the different states of ancient Greece seem to have served in this manner till after the second Persian war; and the people of Peloponnesus till after the Peloponnesian war. The Peloponnesians, Thucydides observes, generally left the field in the summer, and returned home to reap the harvest. The Roman people, under their kings, and during the first ages of the republic, served in the same manner. It was not till the seige of Veii, that they who staid at home began to contribute something towards maintaining those who went to war. In the European monarchies, which were founded upon the ruins of the Roman empire, both before, and for some time after, the establishment of what is properly called the feudal law, the great lords, with all their immediate dependents, used to serve the crown at their own expense. In the field, in the same manner as at home, they maintained themselves by their own revenue, and not by any stipend or pay which they received from the king upon that particular occasion.
p7.zh: 农业,即使处于最粗鲁和最低的状态,也认为是一个定居点,某种固定的居住区,这种居住区不能不遭受巨大损失而放弃。 因此,当一个只有丈夫的民族去打仗时,全体人民不能一起行动。老人、妇女和儿童至少必须留在家里,照顾住家。 然而,所有军事时代的人都可以攻占田野,在这种小国中,经常这样做。 在每一个国家,军事时代的男子应该相当于整个人民身体的大约四分之一或五分之一。 如果运动也应在种子时间之后开始,在收获前结束,丈夫和主要工人都可以免于农场损失。 他相信,在平时必须完成的工作,可以由老人、女人和孩子很好地完成。 因此,他并不不愿意在短短的竞选期间无偿服务;而且,在现场维持他,为他做好准备,往往要付出很少的代价。古希腊所有不同邦的公民似乎都以这种方式服役到第二次波斯战争之后;伯罗奔尼撒人民则服役到伯罗奔尼撒战争之后.伯罗奔尼撒人,Thucydides观察,一般在夏季离开田地,回到家乡收获收获.罗马人在其国王之下,在共和国的最初岁月里,也以同样的方式服役. 直到维伊之战,他们才开始为维持那些参战者做出贡献。 在建立于罗马帝国废墟之上的欧洲君主制中,无论是在之前还是之后的一段时间内,都建立了所谓封建法,大领主们都以所有直接的依附者为主,习惯于自费为皇冠服务.在外地,他们与家庭一样,依靠自己的收入维持自己,而不是依靠在那个特殊时刻从国王那里得到的任何津贴或报酬。

p8.original: In a more advanced state of society, two different causes contribute to render it altogether impossible that they who take the field should maintain themselves at their own expense. Those two causes are, the progress of manufactures, and the improvement in the art of war.
p8.zh: 在较先进的社会状态下,两个不同的原因使得那些占据这个领域的人完全无法自费地维持自己。 这两个原因是:制造的进步,以及战争艺术的改进。

p9.original: Though a husbandman should be employed in an expedition, provided it begins after seedtime, and ends before harvest, the interruption of his business will not always occasion any considerable diminution of his revenue. Without the intervention of his labour, Nature does herself the greater part of the work which remains to be done. But the moment that an artificer, a smith, a carpenter, or a weaver, for example, quits his workhouse, the sole source of his revenue is completely dried up. Nature does nothing for him; he does all for himself. When he takes the field, therefore, in defence of the public, as he has no revenue to maintain himself, he must necessarily be maintained by the public. But in a country, of which a great part of the inhabitants are artificers and manufacturers, a great part of the people who go to war must be drawn from those classes, and must, therefore, be maintained by the public as long as they are employed in its service.
p9.zh: 虽然丈夫应受雇于远征,但从种子开始,到收获结束,他的生意中断并不总是会使其收入出现任何大幅度的缩减。 如果没有他的劳动干预,大自然自己承担了有待完成的大部分工作。 但一瞬间,一个工匠,一个匠人,一个木匠,或者一个织工,比如说,他退出了工作室,他唯一的收入来源是完全干涸的.自然对他无济于事;他对自己无济于事。 当他攻下田地,因此,为了保卫公众,因为他没有收入可以维持自己,所以他必然要由公众来维持. 但是,在一个相当一部分居民是工匠和制造商的国家里,参战的很大一部分人必须从这些阶级中抽调出来,因此只要他们受雇于这个阶级,就必须得到公众的维护.

p10.original: When the art of war, too, has gradually grown up to be a very intricate and complicated science; when the event of war ceases to be determined, as in the first ages of society, by a single irregular skirmish or battle; but when the contest is generally spun out through several different campaigns, each of which lasts during the greater part of the year; it becomes universally necessary that the public should maintain those who serve the public in war, at least while they are employed in that service. Whatever, in time of peace, might be the ordinary occupation of those who go to war, so very tedious and expensive a service would otherwise be by far too heavy a burden upon them. After the second Persian war, accordingly, the armies of Athens seem to have been generally composed of mercenary troops, consisting, indeed, partly of citizens, but partly, too, of foreigners; and all of them equally hired and paid at the expense of the state. From the time of the siege of Veii, the armies of Rome received pay for their service during the time which they remained in the field. Under the feudal governments, the military service, both of the great lords, and of their immediate dependents, was, after a certain period, universally exchanged for a payment in money, which was employed to maintain those who served in their stead.
p10.zh: 当战争艺术也逐渐发展成非常复杂复杂的科学时;当战争事件不再像社会最初时代一样由单一的不规则冲突或战斗决定时;但当比赛一般通过若干不同的运动而爆发时,每一运动都持续到一年的较大时间;公众必须普遍维持那些在战争中为公众服务的人,至少当他们受雇于这一服务时。 无论在和平时期,对参战者的普通占领如何,否则,服务非常乏味和昂贵,对他们来说将负担太重。 因此,在第二次波斯战争之后,雅典的军队似乎一般都由雇佣兵组成,实际上部分由公民组成,但也部分由外国人组成;他们都平等受雇,以国家为代价支付报酬. 从围攻韦伊时起,罗马军队在留在战地期间获得服役报酬. 在封建政府之下,军务,既为大领主,亦为直系属民,在一定时期之后,普遍交换金钱,用以维持代役者.

p11.original: The number of those who can go to war, in proportion to the whole number of the people, is necessarily much smaller in a civilized than in a rude state of society. In a civilized society, as the soldiers are maintained altogether by the labour of those who are not soldiers, the number of the former can never exceed what the latter can maintain, over and above maintaining, in a manner suitable to their respective stations, both themselves and the other officers of government and law, whom they are obliged to maintain. In the little agrarian states of ancient Greece, a fourth or a fifth part of the whole body of the people considered the themselves as soldiers, and would sometimes, it is said, take the field. Among the civilized nations of modern Europe, it is commonly computed, that not more than the one hundredth part of the inhabitants of any country can be employed as soldiers, without ruin to the country which pays the expense of their service.
p11.zh: 能够参战的人数,按照全体人口的比例,在文明的状态下,一定比在粗鲁的社会状态下要小得多.在一个文明社会中,由于士兵完全由非士兵的劳动维持,因此前者的人数永远不能超过后者能够维持的,除了维持之外,以适合他们各自的驻地的方式,包括他们本人以及他们有义务维持的其他政府官员和法律官员。 在古希腊的小农业国中,整个人的第四或第五部分将自己视为士兵,有时,据说会夺取田地. 在现代欧洲的文明国家中,人们通常认为,任何一个国家的居民中不超过一百分之一的人可以被雇用为士兵,而不会给支付其服务费用的国家带来破坏。

p12.original: The expense of preparing the army for the field seems not to have become considerable in any nation, till long after that of maintaining it in the field had devolved entirely upon the sovereign or commonwealth. In all the different republics of ancient Greece, to learn his military exercises, was a necessary part of education imposed by the state upon every free citizen. In every city there seems to have been a public field, in which, under the protection of the public magistrate, the young people were taught their different exercises by different masters. In this very simple institution consisted the whole expense which any Grecian state seems ever to have been at, in preparing its citizens for war. In ancient Rome, the exercises of the Campus Martius answered the same purpose with those of the Gymnasium in ancient Greece. Under the feudal governments, the many public ordinances, that the citizens of every district should practise archery, as well as several other military exercises, were intended for promoting the same purpose, but do not seem to have promoted it so well. Either from want of interest in the officers entrusted with the execution of those ordinances, or from some other cause, they appear to have been universally neglected; and in the progress of all those governments, military exercises seem to have gone gradually into disuse among the great body of the people.
p12.zh: 在任何国家,军队为战地做准备的费用似乎都没有增加,直到在战地维持军队的费用完全移交给主权或联邦之后很久。 在古希腊的所有不同共和国中,学习他的军事演习,是国家强加给每个自由公民的教育的必要部分. 每个城市似乎都有一个公共领域,在公共地方法官的保护下,不同的主人对年轻人进行不同的练习。 在这个非常简单的体制中,任何希腊国家似乎都花费了全部费用,为本国公民备战。 在古罗马,Campus Martius的练习与古希腊的体操同样回答了目的. 在封建政府之下,许多关于每个区公民应当行箭的公开法令,以及其他几次军事演习,都是为了促进同样的目的,但似乎并没有很好地促进这一目的.无论是对负责执行这些法令的军官缺乏兴趣,还是出于其他原因,这些法令似乎被普遍忽视;在所有这些政府的进步中,军事演习似乎已逐渐在广大人民中失去用途。

p13.original: In the republics of ancient Greece and Rome, during the whole period of their existence, and under the feudal governments, for a considerable time after their first establishment, the trade of a soldier was not a separate, distinct trade, which constituted the sole or principal occupation of a particular class of citizens; every subject of the state, whatever might be the ordinary trade or occupation by which he gained his livelihood, considered himself, upon all ordinary occasions, as fit likewise to exercise the trade of a soldier, and, upon many extraordinary occasions, as bound to exercise it.
p13.zh: 在古希腊和罗马各共和国,在整个存续期间,以及在封建政府统治下,在他们第一次建立之后的相当长一段时间里,一个士兵的贸易并不是一个单独的,独特的贸易,它构成了某一类公民的唯一或主要的职业;国家的每一个主体,无论他赖以谋生的普通贸易或职业是什么,都认为自己在一切普通场合同样适合从事一个士兵的贸易,在许多特殊场合,也认为必须进行这种贸易.

p14.original: The art of war, however, as it is certainly the noblest of all arts, so, in the progress of improvement, it necessarily becomes one of the most complicated among them. The state of the mechanical, as well as some other arts, with which it is necessarily connected, determines the degree of perfection to which it is capable of being carried at any particular time. But in order to carry it to this degree of perfection, it is necessary that it should become the sole or principal occupation of a particular class of citizens; and the division of labour is as necessary for the improvement of this, as of every other art. Into other arts, the division of labour is naturally introduced by the prudence of individuals, who find that they promote their private interest better by confining themselves to a particular trade, than by exercising a great number. But it is the wisdom of the state only, which can render the trade of a soldier a particular trade, separate and distinct from all others. A private citizen, who, in time of profound peace, and without any particular encouragement from the public, should spend the greater part of his time in military exercises, might, no doubt, both improve himself very much in them, and amuse himself very well; but he certainly would not promote his own interest. It is the wisdom of the state only, which can render it for his interest to give up the greater part of his time to this peculiar occupation; and states have not always had this wisdom, even when their circumstances had become such, that the preservation of their existence required that they should have it.
p14.zh: 然而,战争艺术,因为它当然是所有艺术中最崇高的,所以在进步的过程中,它必然成为其中最复杂的之一.机械的状态,以及某些其他艺术,必然与它联系在一起,决定了它在特定时间能够携带的完美程度. 但是,为了达到这种完美的程度,它必须成为某一阶层公民的唯一或主要职业;分工是改进这一点所必需的,就像所有其他艺术一样。 在其他艺术中,劳动分工自然是由个人的谨慎性引入的,他们发现,通过将自身局限在某一特定行业中,而不是通过行使大量权利,他们可以更好地促进自己的私人利益. 但是,只有国家的智慧才能使士兵的贸易与所有其他贸易相分离和区别。私人公民,在深厚的和平时期,在没有公众任何特别鼓励的情况下,应该花更多的时间进行军事演习,毫无疑问,他们既能大大改善自己,又能很好玩;但他当然不会促进自己的利益。 只有国家的智慧,才能使他为了利益而放弃他的大部分时间来从事这种特殊的工作;而且各国并不总是有这种智慧,即使它们的情况已经如此,维持它们的生存需要它们拥有这种智慧。

p15.original: A shepherd has a great deal of leisure; a husbandman, in the rude state of husbandry, has some; an artificer or manufacturer has none at all. The first may, without any loss, employ a great deal of his time in martial exercises; the second may employ some part of it; but the last cannot employ a single hour in them without some loss, and his attention to his own interest naturally leads him to neglect them altogether. Those improvements in husbandry, too, which the progress of arts and manufactures necessarily introduces, leave the husbandman as little leisure as the artificer. Military exercises come to be as much neglected by the inhabitants of the country as by those of the town, and the great body of the people becomes altogether unwarlike. That wealth, at the same time, which always follows the improvements of agriculture and manufactures, and which, in reality, is no more than the accumulated produce of those improvements, provokes the invasion of all their neighbours. An industrious, and, upon that account, a wealthy nation, is of all nations the most likely to be attacked; and unless the state takes some new measure for the public defence, the natural habits of the people render them altogether incapable of defending themselves.
p15.zh: 牧羊人拥有大量的闲暇;丈夫在粗鲁的畜牧业状态下,拥有一些;艺术家或制造商完全没有.前者可能毫无损失地运用大量时间进行武术演习;后者可能利用一部分时间;但后者不能在武术演习中使用一个小时而不损失一些时间,而他对自身利益的注意自然导致他完全忽视了武术.畜牧业的这些改进也必然是艺术和制造业进步所引入的,这使丈夫像艺术家一样少有闲暇。军事演习受到该国居民和城镇居民的忽视,人民伟大的身体变得完全不像战争。 与此同时,这种财富总是随着农业和制造业的改善而来,事实上,这种财富只不过是这些改进的累积产物,它激起了所有邻国的入侵。 一个勤奋的国家,一个富裕的国家,是最可能遭到攻击的所有国家;除非国家采取一些新的措施进行公共防卫,人民的自然习惯使他们完全无法自卫。

p16.original: In these circumstances, there seem to be but two methods by which the state can make any tolerable provision for the public defence.
p16.zh: 在这种情况下,国家似乎只有两种方法可以为公共辩护作出任何可容忍的规定。

p17.original: It may either, first, by means of a very rigorous police, and in spite of the whole bent of the interest, genius, and inclinations of the people, enforce the practice of military exercises, and oblige either all the citizens of the military age, or a certain number of them, to join in some measure the trade of a soldier to whatever other trade or profession they may happen to carry on.
p17.zh: 首先,通过非常严格的警察,尽管人民的利益、才智和倾向都一丝不苟,但军事演习的实践是强制性的,它迫使所有军事时代的公民,或其中某些人,在某种程度上加入一个士兵的行业,从事他们可能发生的任何其他行业或职业。

p18.original: Or, secondly, by maintaining and employing a certain number of citizens in the constant practice of military exercises, it may render the trade of a soldier a particular trade, separate and distinct from all others.
p18.zh: 其次,通过保持和雇用一定数量的公民不断进行军事演习,它可能使士兵的贸易成为与所有其他贸易分开和不同的特定贸易。

p19.original: If the state has recourse to the first of those two expedients, its military force is said to consist in a militia; if to the second, it is said to consist in a standing army. The practice of military exercises is the sole or principal occupation of the soldiers of a standing army, and the maintenance or pay which the state affords them is the principal and ordinary fund of their subsistence. The practice of military exercises is only the occasional occupation of the soldiers of a militia, and they derive the principal and ordinary fund of their subsistence from some other occupation. In a militia, the character of the labourer, artificer, or tradesman, predominates over that of the soldier; in a standing army, that of the soldier predominates over every other character; and in this distinction seems to consist the essential difference between those two different species of military force.
p19.zh: 如果国家诉诸于上述两个捷径中的第一个,则其军事力量据说由民兵组成;如果至第二个,则据说由一支常备部队组成。举行军事演习是常备军队士兵的唯一或主要职业,国家为他们提供的维持或支付是维持生计的本金和普通资金。军事演习的做法只是偶尔占领民兵的士兵,他们从其他一些占领中获取维持生计的本金和普通资金。 在民兵中,工人、工匠或商人的性格凌驾于士兵的性格之上;在常备军中,士兵的性格凌驾于所有其他的性格之上;在这种区分中,这两类不同军事力量之间的根本区别似乎就在于此。

p20.original: Militias have been of several different kinds. In some countries, the citizens destined for defending the state seem to have been exercised only, without being, if I may say so, regimented; that is, without being divided into separate and distinct bodies of troops, each of which performed its exercises under its own proper and permanent officers. In the republics of ancient Greece and Rome, each citizen, as long as he remained at home, seems to have practised his exercises, either separately and independently, or with such of his equals as he liked best; and not to have been attached to any particular body of troops, till he was actually called upon to take the field. In other countries, the militia has not only been exercised, but regimented. In England, in Switzerland, and, I believe, in every other country of modern Europe, where any imperfect military force of this kind has been established, every militiaman is, even in time of peace, attached to a particular body of troops, which performs its exercises under its own proper and permanent officers.
p20.zh: 民兵有几种不同的类型。 在一些国家,准备保卫国家的公民似乎只是行使了权力,而我可以说,他们并没有被团团化;也就是说,没有被分成单独和不同的部队机构,每个部队都在自己的适当和永久军官的领导下进行演习。 在古希腊和罗马的共和国中,每个公民只要留在家中,似乎都单独独立地练习,或与他最喜欢的同等人一起练习;并且不附属于任何特定的部队,直到他被实际征召去战场为止. 在其他国家,民兵不仅行使,而且被团派。 在英国、瑞士,以及我相信在现代欧洲的每一个其他国家,任何不完善的这种军事力量都已经建立起来,即使在和平时期,每一个民兵都附属于一个特定的部队机构,在自己的适当和永久军官领导下进行演习。

p21.original: Before the invention of fire-arms, that army was superior in which the soldiers had, each individually, the greatest skill and dexterity in the use of their arms. Strength and agility of body were of the highest consequence, and commonly determined the fate of battles. But this skill and dexterity in the use of their arms could be acquired only, in the same manner as fencing is at present, by practising, not in great bodies, but each man separately, in a particular school, under a particular master, or with his own particular equals and companions. Since the invention of fire-arms, strength and agility of body, or even extraordinary dexterity and skill in the use of arms, though they are far from being of no consequence, are, however, of less consequence. The nature of the weapon, though it by no means puts the awkward upon a level with the skilful, puts him more nearly so than he ever was before. All the dexterity and skill, it is supposed, which are necessary for using it, can be well enough acquired by practising in great bodies.
p21.zh: 在发明火武器之前,这支军队是优越的,其中士兵们各自拥有使用武器的最大技巧和技巧。力量和身体的敏捷性是最大的后果,通常决定着战斗的命运。 但是,这种使用武器的技能与狡猾,只能像目前一样,通过练习,而不是在伟大的身体中,而每个人单独,在一个特定的学校里,在某个特定的主人之下,或者与自己特定的平等者和同伴一起获得. 然而,由于发明火武器、力量和身体的敏捷性,甚至使用武器方面的异常灵活和技巧,虽然远非无任何后果,但后果却较小。武器的性质,虽然它绝不是把尴尬放在一个高手的水平上,使他比以前更加接近。 所有精巧和技巧,都是应该的,是使用它所必须的,通过在伟大身体中练习,可以很好地获得.

p22.original: Regularity, order, and prompt obedience to command, are qualities which, in modern armies, are of more importance towards determining the fate of battles, than the dexterity and skill of the soldiers in the use of their arms. But the noise of fire-arms, the smoke, and the invisible death to which every man feels himself every moment exposed, as soon as he comes within cannon-shot, and frequently a long time before the battle can be well said to be engaged, must render it very difficult to maintain any considerable degree of this regularity, order, and prompt obedience, even in the beginning of a modern battle. In an ancient battle, there was no noise but what arose from the human voice; there was no smoke, there was no invisible cause of wounds or death. Every man, till some mortal weapon actually did approach him, saw clearly that no such weapon was near him. In these circumstances, and among troops who had some confidence in their own skill and dexterity in the use of their arms, it must have been a good deal less difficult to preserve some degree of regularity and order, not only in the beginning, but through the whole progress of an ancient battle, and till one of the two armies was fairly defeated. But the habits of regularity, order, and prompt obedience to command, can be acquired only by troops which are exercised in great bodies.
p22.zh: 在现代军队中,规律、秩序和迅速服从指挥是决定战斗命运的更重要的品质,而不是士兵使用武器时的狡猾和技巧。 但是,火武器的声音,烟雾,以及每个人每时每刻都感受到自己的隐形死亡,一旦进入大炮射击中,而且战斗经常需要很长时间才能被很好地说成是交战,因此即使在现代战斗开始时,也很难维持这种规律性,秩序和迅速的服从. 在古代的战役中,除了从人类的声音中产生的东西,没有噪音;没有烟雾,没有隐形的伤亡原因.每个人,直到某种凡人武器确实接近他,都清楚地看到没有这种武器靠近他。 在这种情况下,在对自己的技能有一定信心,在使用武器上有一定节制的军队中,不但在一开始,而且在一次古代战役的整个进步中,要保持一定的规律和秩序,一定不是一件好事情,直到两军之一被公平击败为止. 但是,规律、秩序和迅速服从指挥的习惯,只能由在伟大身体中行使的军队来获得。

p23.original: A militia, however, in whatever manner it may be either disciplined or exercised, must always be much inferior to a well disciplined and well exercised standing army.
p23.zh: 然而,民兵无论以何种方式受到纪律约束或行使权力,必须始终比纪律严明和表现良好的常备军低得多。

p24.original: The soldiers who are exercised only once a week, or once a-month, can never be so expert in the use of their arms, as those who are exercised every day, or every other day; and though this circumstance may not be of so much consequence in modern, as it was in ancient times, yet the acknowledged superiority of the Prussian troops, owing, it is said, very much to their superior expertness in their exercise, may satisfy us that it is, even at this day, of very considerable consequence.
p24.zh: 每周只锻炼一次,或每月锻炼一次的士兵,在使用武器方面从未像每天锻炼一次,或每隔一天那样如此精通;虽然这种情况在现代可能没有太大的后果,就像古代那样,然而,据说,由于普鲁士部队在锻炼中具有高级的专业知识,公认的优越性,可能使我们确信,即使在今天,它也会产生非常重大的后果。

p25.original: The soldiers, who are bound to obey their officer only once a-week, or once a-month, and who are at all other times at liberty to manage their own affairs their own way, without being, in any respect, accountable to him, can never be under the same awe in his presence, can never have the same disposition to ready obedience, with those whose whole life and conduct are every day directed by him, and who every day even rise and go to bed, or at least retire to their quarters, according to his orders. In what is called discipline, or in the habit of ready obedience, a militia must always be still more inferior to a standing army, than it may sometimes be in what is called the manual exercise, or in the management and use of its arms. But, in modern war, the habit of ready and instant obedience is of much greater consequence than a considerable superiority in the management of arms.
p25.zh: 兵士,必每服其官,只周一,或每月一,在一切其它时候,自由管理自己事务,不至于在他面前,不至于受同样的敬畏,决无同样的准备服从之意,与他每天指挥的一生和行为,甚至每天起身上床睡觉,或至少根据他的命令,退休到自己的住处去.民兵在所谓纪律中,或在随时服从的习惯中,必须始终比常备军更低级,有时可能比起所谓的手工操练,或管理和使用其武器. 但是,在现代战争中,随时服从和即时服从的习惯,其后果远远大于武器管理方面的相当优越性。

p26.original: Those militias which, like the Tartar or Arab militia, go to war under the same chieftains whom they are accustomed to obey in peace, are by far the best. In respect for their officers, in the habit of ready obedience, they approach nearest to standing armies. The Highland militia, when it served under its own chieftains, had some advantage of the same kind. As the Highlanders, however, were not wandering, but stationary shepherds, as they had all a fixed habitation, and were not, in peaceable times, accustomed to follow their chieftain from place to place; so, in time of war, they were less willing to follow him to any considerable distance, or to continue for any long time in the field. When they had acquired any booty, they were eager to return home, and his authority was seldom sufficient to detain them. In point of obedience, they were always much inferior to what is reported of the Tartars and Arabs. As the Highlanders, too, from their stationary life, spend less of their time in the open air, they were always less accustomed to military exercises, and were less expert in the use of their arms than the Tartars and Arabs are said to be.
p26.zh: 像鞑靼人或阿拉伯民兵一样,在他们习惯于和平服从的同一批酋长手下参战的民兵是迄今为止最好的。 对于他们的军官,以随时服从的习惯,他们接近常备军.高地民兵在自己首领手下服役时,也有一定优势. 然而,由于高地人不是流浪,而是固定的牧羊人,因为他们都有一个固定的居所,在平和的时代,他们并不习惯于从地方跟随他们的酋长;因此,在战时,他们不太愿意跟随他到任何相当远的地方,或者在野外的任何长时间继续. 当他们获得任何战利品时,他们渴望返回家园,他的权力很少足以拘留他们。 在服从方面,他们总是比塔塔尔人和阿拉伯人的报导低得多。 由于高地人也从固定生活开始,在露天度过的时间较少,所以他们总是不太习惯军事演习,在使用武器方面比塔塔尔人和阿拉伯人据说更不精通.

p27.original: A militia of any kind, it must be observed, however, which has served for several successive campaigns in the field, becomes in every respect a standing army. The soldiers are every day exercised in the use of their arms, and, being constantly under the command of their officers, are habituated to the same prompt obedience which takes place in standing armies. What they were before they took the field, is of little importance. They necessarily become in every respect a standing army, after they have passed a few campaigns in it. Should the war in America drag out through another campaign, the American militia may become, in every respect, a match for that standing army, of which the valour appeared, in the last war at least, not inferior to that of the hardiest veterans of France and Spain.
p27.zh: 然而,必须看到,在野外连续开展几次运动的民兵,在各个方面都成为了一支常备军。 这些士兵每天都在使用武器,而且经常在军官的指挥下,习惯于与常备军队一样的迅速服从。 他们攻下球场前的状态,并不重要. 他们必须在各方面成为一支常备军,在经过几次战役之后。 如果美国战争拖过另一场战役,美国民兵在各个方面都可能成为常备军的对手,至少在上一场战争中,英勇表现不逊于法国和西班牙最艰苦的老兵。

p28.original: This distinction being well understood, the history of all ages, it will be found, hears testimony to the irresistible superiority which a well regulated standing army has over a militia.
p28.zh: 这种区别是可以理解的,所有年龄的历史都将被找到,这可以证明,一支管理良好的常备军对民兵具有不可抗拒的优越性。

p29.original: One of the first standing armies, of which we have any distinct account in any well authenticated history, is that of Philip of Macedon. His frequent wars with the Thracians, Illyrians, Thessalians, and some of the Greek cities in the neighbourhood of Macedon, gradually formed his troops, which in the beginning were probably militia, to the exact discipline of a standing army. When he was at peace, which he was very seldom, and never for any long time together, he was careful not to disband that army. It vanquished and subdued, after a long and violent struggle, indeed, the gallant and well exercised militias of the principal republics of ancient Greece; and afterwards, with very little struggle, the effeminate and ill exercised militia of the great Persian empire. The fall of the Greek republics, and of the Persian empire was the effect of the irresistible superiority which a standing arm has over every other sort of militia. It is the first great revolution in the affairs of mankind of which history has preserved any distinct and circumstantial account.
p29.zh: 最早的常备军之一,我们在所有经过验证的历史中都有明确的说法,是马塞顿的菲利普. 他经常与特拉西亚人,伊利里安人,塞萨尔人,以及马塞顿街区的一些希腊城市展开战争,逐渐组建了他的部队,起初很可能是民兵,到一个常备军的精确纪律. 当他和平的时候,他很少,而且从未在一起很长时间,他很小心地不解散那支军队。 它在经过长期的暴力斗争之后,确实打败了古希腊各主要共和国的英勇和出色的民兵;随后,经过很少的战斗,大波斯帝国的精疲力竭的民兵被削弱和被削弱。 希腊共和国和波斯帝国的衰败是站立的军队对所有其他类型的民兵的不可抗拒的优越性的影响。 这是人类事务中第一次大革命,历史对此作了任何明确和间接的叙述。

p30.original: The fall of Carthage, and the consequent elevation of Rome, is the second. All the varieties in the fortune of those two famous republics may very well be accounted for from the same cause.
p30.zh: 迦太基的陷落, 以及罗马的崛起,是第二次。 这两个著名的共和国的财富中的所有品种都很可能来自同一事业。

p31.original: From the end of the first to the beginning of the second Carthaginian war, the armies of Carthage were continually in the field, and employed under three great generals, who succeeded one another in the command; Amilcar, his son-in-law Asdrubal, and his son Annibal: first in chastising their own rebellious slaves, afterwards in subduing the revolted nations of Africa; and lastly, in conquering the great kingdom of Spain. The army which Annibal led from Spain into Italy must necessarily, in those different wars, have been gradually formed to the exact discipline of a standing army. The Romans, in the meantime, though they had not been altogether at peace, yet they had not, during this period, been engaged in any war of very great consequence; and their military discipline, it is generally said, was a good deal relaxed. The Roman armies which Annibal encountered at Trebi, Thrasymenus, and Cannae, were militia opposed to a standing army. This circumstance, it is probable, contributed more than any other to determine the fate of those battles.
p31.zh: 从第一次到第二次迦太基战争开始,迦太基的军队不断地在野战,雇佣在三位大将之下,他们互相继承指挥权;阿米尔卡尔,他的女婿阿斯德鲁巴尔,和他的儿子安尼巴尔:首先惩罚他们自己的反叛奴隶,后来征服叛乱的非洲国家;最后征服西班牙的大王国. 安尼巴尔从西班牙率领的军队进入意大利,在这些不同的战争中,必然要逐渐形成一个正规军的纪律。在此期间,罗马人虽然还没有完全平息,但在此期间,他们并没有参与过任何具有非常巨大后果的战争;而且他们的军事纪律,一般说来,是相当放松的. 安尼拔在特雷比,Thrasymenus,和坎纳遇到的罗马军队是反对常备军的民兵. 这种情况很可能比任何其他情况更有助于确定这些战斗的命运。

p32.original: The standing army which Annibal left behind him in Spain had the like superiority over the militia which the Romans sent to oppose it; and, in a few years, under the command of his brother, the younger Asdrubal, expelled them almost entirely from that country.
p32.zh: 安尼拔留在西班牙的常备军,比罗马人派来反对的民兵有类似的优势;几年后,在他的弟弟阿斯德鲁巴尔的指挥下,几乎完全将他们赶出了这个国家.

p33.original: Annibal was ill supplied from home. The Roman militia, being continually in the field, became, in the progress of the war, a well disciplined and well exercised standing army; and the superiority of Annibal grew every day less and less. Asdrubal judged it necessary to lead the whole, or almost the whole, of the standing army which he commanded in Spain, to the assistance of his brother in Italy. In this march, he is said to have been misled by his guides; and in a country which he did not know, was surprised and attacked, by another standing army, in every respect equal or superior to his own, and was entirely defeated.
p33.zh: Annibal从家中供货不足。罗马民兵不断在野战中,在战争的推进中,成为一支纪律严明,表现良好的常备军;安尼拔的优越性逐日增长,越来越少. 阿斯德鲁巴尔认为,有必要带领整个,或几乎整个他在西班牙指挥的常备军,到他在意大利的弟弟帮助.在这次行军中,据说他被他的向导误导;在一个他不知道的国家,被另一支常备军惊奇和攻击,在各方面都与他自己平等或优越,被彻底击败.

p34.original: When Asdrubal had left Spain, the great Scipio found nothing to oppose him but a militia inferior to his own. He conquered and subdued that militia, and, in the course of the war, his own militia necessarily became a well disciplined and well exercised standing army. That standing army was afterwards carried to Africa, where it found nothing but a militia to oppose it. In order to defend Carthage, it became necessary to recal the standing army of Annibal. The disheartened and frequently defeated African militia joined it, and, at the battle of Zama, composed the greater part of the troops of Annibal. The event of that day determined the fate of the two rival republics.
p34.zh: 当阿斯德鲁巴尔离开西班牙时,伟大的斯西皮奥发现除了一个比自己的低级的民兵之外,没有什么可以反对他. 他征服并制服了这支民兵,在战争中,他自己所在的民兵必然成为一支纪律严明,表现良好的常备军. 这支常备军随后被运至非洲,在那里,它发现只有民兵反对。 为了保卫迦太基,不得不重新调整安尼拔的常备军.心灰意冷并经常被击败的非洲民兵也加入了这个组织,在扎马战役中,安尼巴尔的部队占了大部分.当天的事件决定了两个敌对共和国的命运.

p35.original: From the end of the second Carthaginian war till the fall of the Roman republic, the armies of Rome were in every respect standing armies. The standing army of Macedon made some resistance to their arms. In the height of their grandeur, it cost them two great wars, and three great battles, to subdue that little kingdom, of which the conquest would probably have been still more difficult, had it not been for the cowardice of its last king. The militias of all the civilized nations of the ancient world, of Greece, of Syria, and of Egypt, made but a feeble resistance to the standing armies of Rome. The militias of some barbarous nations defended themselves much better. The Scythian or Tartar militia, which Mithridates drew from the countries north of the Euxine and Caspian seas, were the most formidable enemies whom the Romans had to encounter after the second Carthaginian war. The Parthian and German militias, too, were always respectable, and upon several occasions, gained very considerable advantages over the Roman armies. In general, however, and when the Roman armies were well commanded, they appear to have been very much superior; and if the Romans did not pursue the final conquest either of Parthia or Germany, it was probably because they judged that it was not worth while to add those two barbarous countries to an empire which was already too large. The ancient Parthians appear to have been a nation of Scythian or Tartar extraction, and to have always retained a good deal of the manners of their ancestors. The ancient Germans were, like the Scythians or Tartars, a nation of wandering shepherds, who went to war under the same chiefs whom they were accustomed to follow in peace. 'Their militia was exactly of the same kind with that of the Scythians or Tartars, from whom, too, they were probably descended.
p35.zh: 从第二次迦太基战争结束到罗马共和国倒台,罗马的军队在各方面都是常备军队. 马塞顿的常备军对他们的手臂进行了一些抵抗. 在他们的盛大时期,要征服这个小王国,他们付出了两场大战和三场大战的代价,如果不是因为其末代国王的懦弱,征服这个小王国很可能还要更加困难.古代世界所有文明国家的民兵,希腊,叙利亚,埃及的民兵,对罗马的常备军队只做了微弱的抵抗. 一些野蛮国家的民兵保卫自己要好得多。 米特里达兹从厄克辛海和里海以北的国家中抽调出来的斯西提人或鞑靼人民兵,是第二次迦太基战争后罗马人不得不遇到的最可怕的敌人.帕提亚人和德国民兵也总是受人尊敬的,并且在若干场合比罗马军队获得了相当可观的优势. 然而,总的来说,当罗马军队得到很好的指挥时,他们似乎已经非常优越;如果罗马人没有追求帕提亚或德国的最终征服,那很可能是因为他们判断在将这两个野蛮国家加到一个已经太庞大的帝国中的同时是不值得的.古代的帕提亚人似乎是一个斯喀地亚人或鞑靼人采掘的民族,并且一直保留着祖先的礼仪.古代的德国人,就像斯喀地亚人或鞑靼人一样,是一个流浪的牧羊人的国家,在他们习惯于和平地跟随的同一位酋长手下参战. '他们的民兵与斯喀地亚人或鞑靼人完全相同,他们很可能也从他们那里降下.

p36.original: Many different causes contributed to relax the discipline of the Roman armies. Its extreme severity was, perhaps, one of those causes. In the days of their grandeur, when no enemy appeared capable of opposing them, their heavy armour was laid aside as unnecessarily burdensome, their laborious exercises were neglected, as unnecessarily toilsome. Under the Roman emperors, besides, the standing armies of Rome, those particularly which guarded the German and Pannonian frontiers, became dangerous to their masters, against whom they used frequently to set up their own generals. In order to render them less formidable, according to some authors, Dioclesian, according to others, Constantine, first withdrew them from the frontier, where they had always before been encamped in great bodies, generally of two or three legions each, and dispersed them in small bodies through the different provincial towns, from whence they were scarce ever removed, but when it became necessary to repel an invasion. Small bodies of soldiers, quartered in trading and manufacturing towns, and seldom removed from those quarters, became themselves trades men, artificers, and manufacturers. The civil came to predominate over the military character; and the standing armies of Rome gradually degenerated into a corrupt, neglected, and undisciplined militia, incapable of resisting the attack of the German and Scythian militias, which soon afterwards invaded the western empire. It was only by hiring the militia of some of those nations to oppose to that of others, that the emperors were for some time able to defend themselves. The fall of the western empire is the third great revolution in the affairs of mankind, of which ancient history has preserved any distinct or circumstantial account. It was brought about by the irresistible superiority which the militia of a barbarous has over that of a civilized nation; which the militia of a nation of shepherds has over that of a nation of husbandmen, artificers, and manufacturers. The victories which have been gained by militias have generally been, not over standing armies, but over other militias, in exercise and discipline inferior to themselves. Such were the victories which the Greek militia gained over that of the Persian empire; and such, too, were those which, in later times, the Swiss militia gained over that of the Austrians and Burgundians.
p36.zh: 许多不同的原因都有助于放松罗马军队的纪律.其极端严重性也许是其中之一。 在他们伟大的日子里, 当没有敌人能够反对他们的时候, 他们的厚重的装甲被抛在一边, 作为不必要的负担, 他们的劳累的练习被忽略, 作为不必要的劳累。在罗马皇帝之下,此外,罗马的常备军队,那些特别守卫德国和潘诺尼亚边境的军队,也变得对主人危险,他们经常用来建立自己的将军. 一些作者认为,为了减轻他们的威力,狄奥克莱西亚人(狄奥克莱西亚人)根据其他人的说法,君士坦丁首先将他们从边境撤退,他们以前一直被安营扎寨,被安营扎寨,一般各有两三个军团,然后分散在小尸体中,穿过不同的省城,从那里他们很少被搬走,但当他们成为必须击退入侵的时候.小型的士兵在贸易和制造城市中扎根,很少离开这些地方,他们自己成为了商人、艺术品手工业者和制造商。民国时期逐渐凌驾于军事性质之上;罗马的常备军逐渐堕落为腐败,被忽视,纪律不严的民兵,无力抵抗德军和斯西里特民兵的攻击,这些民兵不久后入侵西帝国. 只有雇用了其中一些国家的民兵来反对其他国家,皇帝们才有一段时间能够自卫。西方帝国的衰落是人类事务中的第三次大革命,古代历史保存了其中任何明显或间接的叙述.其原因是,野蛮人的民兵拥有不可抗拒的优越性,而文明国家的优越性是无法抗拒的;牧羊人的民族的民兵拥有的优越性,而丈夫、工匠和制造商组成的民族的优越性是无法抗拒的。民兵获得的胜利一般不是凌驾于常备军队之上,而是凌驾于其他民兵之上,在操练和纪律上都不如他们自己。 这些是希腊民兵战胜波斯帝国的胜利;瑞士民兵后来战胜奥地利人和布尔贡迪人。

p37.original: The military force of the German and Scythian nations, who established themselves upon ruins of the western empire, continued for some time to be of the same kind in their new settlements, as it had been in their original country. It was a militia of shepherds and husbandmen, which, in time of war, took the field under the command of the same chieftains whom it was accustomed to obey in peace. It was, therefore, tolerably well exercised, and tolerably well disciplined. As arts and industry advanced, however, the authority of the chieftains gradually decayed, and the great body of the people had less time to spare for military exercises. Both the discipline and the exercise of the feudal militia, therefore, went gradually to ruin, and standing armies were gradually introduced to supply the place of it. When the expedient of a standing army, besides, had once been adopted by one civilized nation, it became necessary that all its neighbours should follow the example. They soon found that their safety depended upon their doing so, and that their own militia was altogether incapable of resisting the attack of such an army.
p37.zh: 在西帝国废墟上建立自己的德意志和西西里民族的军事力量,在一段时间内,在他们的新定居点中一直和原来的国家一样. 是牧羊人和丈夫的民兵,在战时,他们把田地交给了他们习惯于和平服从的同一批酋长指挥. 因此,它得以容忍地很好地行使,并被容忍地纪律严明。 然而,随着文艺和工业的进步,酋长们的权威逐渐衰落,人民大军的体力更没有多少时间去进行军事演习. 因此,封建民兵的纪律和锻炼都逐渐走向废墟,并逐渐引入了常备军以供给其位置. 此外,当一个文明国家曾经采用常备军队的权宜之计时,所有邻国都必须效仿。 他们很快发现,他们的安全取决于他们这样做,他们自己的民兵完全无力抵抗这种军队的攻击。

p38.original: The soldiers of a standing army, though they may never have seen an enemy, yet have frequently appeared to possess all the courage of veteran troops, and, the very moment that they took the field, to have been fit to face the hardiest and most experienced veterans. In 1756, when the Russian army marched into Poland, the valour of the Russian soldiers did not appear inferior to that of the Prussians, at that time supposed to be the hardiest and most experienced veterans in Europe. The Russian empire, however, had enjoyed a profound peace for near twenty years before, and could at that time have very few soldiers who had ever seen an enemy. When the Spanish war broke out in 1739, England had enjoyed a profound peace for about eight-and-twenty years. The valour of her soldiers, however, far from being corrupted by that long peace, was never more distinguished than in the attempt upon Carthagena, the first unfortunate exploit of that unfortunate war. In a long peace, the generals, perhaps, may sometimes forget their skill; but where a well regulated standing army has been kept up, the soldiers seem never to forget their valour.
p38.zh: 一支常备军的士兵虽然可能从未见过敌人,但往往似乎拥有老兵部队的所有勇气,而且就在他们攻下战场的那一刻,他们已经适合面对最艰苦和最有经验的老兵。1756年,俄国军队进军波兰时,俄国士兵的英勇并不比普鲁士人低,当时应该是欧洲最艰苦,经验最丰富的老兵. 然而,俄罗斯帝国在近20年前就享有了深远的和平,在那时,能够见到敌人的士兵很少.1739年西班牙战争爆发时,英格兰在大约八二十年间享有了深刻的和平. 然而,她的士兵们的英勇远未被长期和平所破坏,从未像对迦太基纳的企图那样突出,而迦太基纳是这场不幸战争的第一次不幸利用。在一个漫长的和平中,也许将军们有时可能忘记了他们的技巧;但是,如果一支经过严格管制的常备军得到了保持,那么士兵们似乎永远不会忘记他们的英勇。

p39.original: When a civilized nation depends for its defence upon a militia, it is at all times exposed to be conquered by any barbarous nation which happens to be in its neighbourhood. The frequent conquests of all the civilized countries in Asia by the Tartars, sufficiently demonstrates the natural superiority which the militia of a barbarous has over that of a civilized nation. A well regulated standing army is superior to every militia. Such an army, as it can best be maintained by an opulent and civilized nation, so it can alone defend such a nation against the invasion of a poor and barbarous neighbour. It is only by means of a standing army, therefore, that the civilization of any country can be perpetuated, or even preserved, for any considerable time.
p39.zh: 当一个文明国家依靠一个民兵来保卫时,它随时都有可能被任何恰巧在其邻近地区的任何野蛮国家征服。鞑靼人经常征服亚洲所有文明国家,充分显示了野蛮人的民兵对文明国家的天生优越性。一支经过严格管理的常备军优于每个民兵。这样的军队,最好由一个富饶文明的国家来维持,这样它就可以独自保卫这样一个国家,抵御一个穷困野蛮的邻国的入侵. 因此,只有通过一支常备军队,任何国家的文明才能永久维持,甚至维持任何相当长的时间。

p40.original: As it is only by means of a well regulated standing army, that a civilized country can be defended, so it is only by means of it that a barbarous country can be suddenly and tolerably civilized. A standing army establishes, with an irresistible force, the law of the sovereign through the remotest provinces of the empire, and maintains some degree of regular government in countries which could not otherwise admit of any. Whoever examines with attention, the improvements which Peter the Great introduced into the Russian empire, will find that they almost all resolve themselves into the establishment of a well regulated standing army. It is the instrument which executes and maintains all his other regulations. That degree of order and internal peace, which that empire has ever since enjoyed, is altogether owing to the influence of that army.
p40.zh: 因为只有经过严格管理的常备军,才能保卫文明国家,所以,只有依靠这个手段,野蛮国家才能突然和容忍地文明起来.一支常备军以不可抗拒的力量,通过帝国最偏远的省份建立君主的法则,并在本来无法承认任何法律的国家维持某种程度的正规政府.彼得大帝对俄罗斯帝国的改进,无论谁仔细审查,都会发现,他们几乎都决心建立一支管理严密的常备军。执行并维持他所有其他条例的文书就是这项文书。 这个帝国从那时起一直享有的这种程度的秩序和国内和平,完全是由于那支军队的影响。

p41.original: Men of republican principles have been jealous of a standing army, as dangerous to liberty. It certainly is so, wherever the interest of the general, and that of the principal officers, are not necessarily connected with the support of the constitution of the state. The standing army of Caesar destroyed the Roman republic. The standing army of Cromwell turned the long parliament out of doors. But where the sovereign is himself the general, and the principal nobility and gentry of the country the chief officers of the army; where the military force is placed under the command of those who have the greatest interest in the support of the civil authority, because they have themselves the greatest share of that authority, a standing army can never be dangerous to liberty. On the contrary, it may, in some cases, be favourable to liberty. The security which it gives to the sovereign renders unnecessary that troublesome jealousy, which, in some modern republics, seems to watch over the minutest actions, and to be at all times ready to disturb the peace of every citizen. Where the security of the magistrate, though supported by the principal people of the country, is endangered by every popular discontent; where a small tumult is capable of bringing about in a few hours a great revolution, the whole authority of government must be employed to suppress and punish every murmur and complaint against it. To a sovereign, on the contrary, who feels himself supported, not only by the natural aristocracy of the country, but by a well regulated standing army, the rudest, the most groundless, and the most licentious remonstrances, can give little disturbance. He can safely pardon or neglect them, and his consciousness of his own superiority naturally disposes him to do so. That degree of liberty which approaches to licentiousness, can be tolerated only in countries where the sovereign is secured by a well regulated standing army. It is in such countries only, that the public safety does not require that the sovereign should be trusted with any discretionary power, for suppressing even the impertinent wantonness of this licentious liberty.
p41.zh: 共和原则的男子一直嫉妒常备军,认为这对自由是危险的。 当然,只要将军的利益和主要官员的利益不必然与国家宪法的支持有关,就属于这种情况。 凯撒的常备军摧毁了罗马共和国.克伦威尔的常备军将长长的议会从门上翻开. 但是,如果君主本人是将军,而国家的主要贵族和贵族是军队的首席军官;如果军队由那些最关心支持民政当局的人指挥,因为他们拥有这一权力的最大份额,那么一支常设军队永远不会对自由构成危险。 相反,在某些情况下,它可能有利于自由。 它给君主带来的安全使得这种麻烦的嫉妒变得没有必要,在一些现代共和国,这种嫉妒似乎在看好这些零星的行动,随时愿意扰乱每个公民的和平。地方法官的安全虽然得到全国主要人民的支持,但受到一切群众不满的危害;小动乱在几小时内能够带来大革命的,必须利用整个政府的权威来压制和惩罚每一次的喃喃和抱怨. 对一个君主来说,恰恰相反,他感到自己受到支持,不仅受到国家自然贵族的拥护,而且受到管理严密的常备军的拥护,最粗鲁,最无根据,最放肆的复古之士,能够给人一点干扰. 他可以安全地赦免或忽视他们,他对自己优越性的意识自然地使他放弃了这样做.只有在主权得到管理良好的常备军队保障的国家,才能容忍这种接近于奢侈的自由程度。只有在这些国家,公共安全才不要求主权者拥有任何自由裁量权,甚至压制这种残暴自由的不必要肆意。

p42.original: The first duty of the sovereign, therefore, that of defending the society from the violence and injustice of other independent societies, grows gradually more and more expensive, as the society advances in civilization. The military force of the society, which originally cost the sovereign no expense, either in time of peace, or in time of war, must, in the progress of improvement, first be maintained by him in time of war, and afterwards even in time of peace.
p42.zh: 因此,主权者的首要义务是保护社会免遭其他独立社会的暴力和不公正,随着社会文明的进步,其费用逐渐增加。社会的军事力量最初在和平时期或战争时期使君主付出不费钱的代价,但在改进过程中,必须首先由他维持战争时期,之后甚至和平时期。

p43.original: The great change introduced into the art of war by the invention of fire-arms, has enhanced still further both the expense of exercising and disciplining any particular number of soldiers in time of peace, and that of employing them in time of war. Both their arms and their ammunition are become more expensive. A musket is a more expensive machine than a javelin or a bow and arrows; a cannon or a mortar, than a balista or a catapulta. The powder which is spent in a modern review is lost irrecoverably, and occasions a very considerable expense. The javelins and arrows which were thrown or shot in an ancient one, could easily be picked up again, and were, besides, of very little value. The cannon and the mortar are not only much dearer, but much heavier machines than the balista or catapulta; and require a greater expense, not only to prepare them for the field, but to carry them to it. As the superiority of the modern artillery, too, over that of the ancients, is very great; it has become much more difficult, and consequently much more expensive, to fortify a town, so as to resist, even for a few weeks, the attack of that superior artillery. In modern times, many different causes contribute to render the defence of the society more expensive. The unavoidable effects of the natural progress of improvement have, in this respect, been a good deal enhanced by a great revolution in the art of war, to which a mere accident, the invention of gunpowder, seems to have given occasion.
p43.zh: 发明火器对战争艺术带来的巨大变化,进一步增加了在和平时期锻炼和约束任何特定人数的士兵的费用,以及战时雇用士兵的费用。 他们的武器和弹药都变得更加昂贵。火枪是比贾维林或弓箭更昂贵的机器;炮或迫击炮,比巴利斯塔或白宫更昂贵. 在现代审查中花费的粉末是无可挽回的,有时花费了相当大的费用。被扔进或射入古代的杰弗林和箭头很容易被再次捡起来,而且价值很小。 大炮和迫击炮不仅比大炮或大炮更珍贵,而且比大炮或大炮要重得多;而且需要更大的开支,不仅为了准备野战,而且要携带到野战. 由于现代火炮的优势也比古代的要大得多;因此,加固一个城镇变得困难得多,因而代价也大得多,以便抵抗,甚至在几个星期内,这种上层火炮的攻击. 在现代,许多不同的原因都有助于使捍卫社会的成本更高. 在这方面,战争艺术的一次大革命大大加强了自然进步的不可避免的影响,而仅仅一次意外,火药的发明,似乎已使这一革命有了机会。

p44.original: In modern war, the great expense of firearms gives an evident advantage to the nation which can best afford that expense; and, consequently, to an opulent and civilized, over a poor and barbarous nation. In ancient times, the opulent and civilized found it difficult to defend themselves against the poor and barbarous nations. In modern times, the poor and barbarous find it difficult to defend themselves against the opulent and civilized. The invention of fire-arms, an invention which at first sight appears to be so pernicious, is certainly favourable, both to the permanency and to the extension of civilization.
p44.zh: 在现代战争中,武器的巨大开支使最能负担这笔开支的国家,以及因此使一个富饶和文明的国家,比起一个贫穷和野蛮的国家,有明显的优势。 在古代,奢侈和文明的人发现很难抵御贫苦和野蛮的国家。 在现代,穷人和野蛮人发现难以抵御奢侈和文明的势力。火器的发明,这一发明乍看看来是有害的,当然有利于文明的持久和扩展。

p45.original: PART II. Of the Expense of Justice

p46.original: The second duty of the sovereign, that of protecting, as far as possible, every member of the society from the injustice or oppression of every other member of it, or the duty of establishing an exact administration of justice, requires two very different degrees of expense in the different periods of society.
p46.zh: 君主的第二项义务,即尽可能保护社会每个成员免受其每个其他成员的不公正或压迫,或建立确切的司法职责,要求社会不同时期有两种非常不同的支出程度.

p47.original: Among nations of hunters, as there is scarce any property, or at least none that exceeds the value of two or three days labour; so there is seldom any established magistrate, or any regular administration of justice. Men who have no property, can injure one another only in their persons or reputations. But when one man kills, wounds, beats, or defames another, though he to whom the injury is done suffers, he who does it receives no benefit. It is otherwise with the injuries to property. The benefit of the person who does the injury is often equal to the loss of him who suffers it. Envy, malice, or resentment, are the only passions which can prompt one man to injure another in his person or reputation. But the greater part of men are not very frequently under the influence of those passions; and the very worst men are so only occasionally. As their gratification, too, how agreeable soever it may be to certain characters, is not attended with any real or permanent advantage, it is, in the greater part of men, commonly restrained by prudential considerations. Men may live together in society with some tolerable degree of security, though there is no civil magistrate to protect them from the injustice of those passions. But avarice and ambition in the rich, in the poor the hatred of labour and the love of present ease and enjoyment, are the passions which prompt to invade property; passions much more steady in their operation, and much more universal in their influence. Wherever there is a great property, there is great inequality. For one very rich man, there must be at least five hundred poor, and the affluence of the few supposes the indigence of the many. The affluence of the rich excites the indignation of the poor, who are often both driven by want, and prompted by envy to invade his possessions. It is only under the shelter of the civil magistrate, that the owner of that valuable property, which is acquired by the labour of many years, or perhaps of many successive generations, can sleep a single night in security. He is at all times surrounded by unknown enemies, whom, though he never provoked, he can never appease, and from whose injustice he can be protected only by the powerful arm of the civil magistrate, continually held up to chastise it. The acquisition of valuable and extensive property, therefore, necessarily requires the establishment of civil government. Where there is no property, or at least none that exceeds the value of two or three days labour, civil government is not so necessary.
p47.zh: 在狩猎国中,因为几乎没有任何财产,或至少没有财产超过两三天的劳动价值;因此很少有常设治安法官或任何正常的司法。 没有财产的男子,只有在个人或名誉上才能互相伤害。 但当一个人杀人、受伤、殴打或诽谤他人时,即使伤害给谁造成伤害,谁也得不到任何好处。 否则,它与财产损失有关。伤害者的利益往往等于伤害者的损失。怀念、恶意或怨恨,是唯一能促使一个人伤害另一个人或名誉的激情。 但大部分男子并不经常受到这些激情的影响;最坏的男子只是偶尔才受到这种影响。 由于她们也满足于某些人物,无论对某些人物多么满意,她们得不到任何实际或永久的好处,因此,在大部分男子中,这种好处通常受到审慎考虑的限制。男人在社会中可以共同生活,享有某种程度的可容忍的安全,尽管没有民事法官保护他们免受这些激情的不公正待遇。 但富人、穷人、对劳动的仇恨和对现在的轻松和享受的热爱,都是促使人们侵犯财产的热情;他们的热情在运作上更加稳定,在影响上更加普遍。 只要有大的财产,就存在着巨大的不平等。 对于一个非常富有的人来说,必须至少有五百个穷人,而少数人的富裕则认为是众多人的贫困.富贵令穷人愤慨不已,他们往往既受匮乏驱使,又因嫉妒而侵入他的财产。只有在民事法官的庇护下,才能使多年或许多世代的劳动所得的这一宝贵财产的所有人在安全的情况下过一夜。 他始终被不知名的敌人包围着,虽然他从未挑起过敌人,但他永远无法安抚,他只能由民事法官的强大臂膀保护他的不公,不断加以惩罚。 因此,要获得宝贵和广泛的财产,就必须建立民政政府。 如果没有财产,或者至少没有超过两三天劳动价值的财产,那么文官政府就没有必要了.

p48.original: Civil government supposes a certain subordination. But as the necessity of civil government gradually grows up with the acquisition of valuable property; so the principal causes, which naturally introduce subordination, gradually grow up with the growth of that valuable property.
p48.zh: 文官政府认为是某种从属地位. 但随着文官政府的必要性随着宝贵财产的获得逐渐发展;因此自然引入从属地位的主要原因随着宝贵财产的增长而逐渐发展.

p49.original: The causes or circumstances which naturally introduce subordination, or which naturally and antecedent to any civil institution, give some men some superiority over the greater part of their brethren, seem to be four in number.
p49.zh: 自然而然地导致从属地位或自然而然地与任何民间机构相继出现的原因或情况,使一些男子比大部分兄弟具有某种优越性,似乎有四个因素。

p50.original: The first of those causes or circumstances, is the superiority of personal qualifications, of strength, beauty, and agility of body; of wisdom and virtue; of prudence, justice, fortitude, and moderation of mind. The qualifications of the body, unless supported by those of the mind, can give little authority in any period of society. He is a very strong man, who, by mere strength of body, can force two weak ones to obey him. The qualifications of the mind can alone give very great authority. They are however, invisible qualities; always disputable, and generally disputed. No society, whether barbarous or civilized, has ever found it convenient to settle the rules of precedency of rank and subordination, according to those invisible qualities; but according to something that is more plain and palpable.
p50.zh: 这些原因或情况中的第一个是个人资格、力量、美貌和身体的敏捷性优越;智慧和美德优越;谨慎、正义、坚韧和思想温和。身体的资质,除非有心灵的资质支持,否则在社会的任何时期,都不能赋予什么权威. 他是一个非常强壮的人,只要身体强壮,就能迫使两个弱者服从他.思想的资质单凭它就能赋予非常强大的威信. 然而,它们是无形的品质;始终是有争议的,而且普遍有争议。没有任何社会,无论是野蛮的还是文明的,都认为根据这些无形的品质,解决等级和从属地位之前的规则是方便的;但是,根据更明确和更明显的事物。

p51.original: The second of those causes or circumstances, is the superiority of age. An old man, provided his age is not so far advanced as to give suspicion of dotage, is everywhere more respected than a young man of equal rank, fortune, and abilities. Among nations of hunters, such as the native tribes of North America, age is the sole foundation of rank and precedency. Among them, father is the appellation of a superior; brother, of an equal; and son, of an inferior. In the most opulent and civilized nations, age regulates rank among those who are in every other respect equal; and among whom, therefore, there is nothing else to regulate it. Among brothers and among sisters, the eldest always takes place; and in the succession of the paternal estate, every thing which cannot be divided, but must go entire to one person, such as a title of honour, is in most cases given to the eldest. Age is a plain and palpable quality, which admits of no dispute.
p51.zh: 其中第二个原因或情况是年龄优越。 一个老人,只要他的年龄还不够高,不能让人怀疑点,就比一个同等级别、财富和能力青年更受尊重。 在美洲原住民部落等狩猎民族中,年龄是军衔和前辈的唯一基础. 其中,父亲是上司的称号;兄弟是平等的;儿子是下等的. 在最富裕和文明的国家,年龄在所有其他方面都平等,因此,在这些国家中,没有其他什么可以加以规范的。 在兄弟姐妹之间,长子总是在世;在父子财产继承中,每一件不能分割,但必须全部归一个人,如荣誉头衔,在大多数情况下都交给长子.年龄是一种简单和显而易见的质量,这不容争议。

p52.original: The third of those causes or circumstances, is the superiority of fortune. The authority of riches, however, though great in every age of society, is, perhaps, greatest in the rudest ages of society, which admits of any considerable inequality of fortune. A Tartar chief, the increase of whose flocks and herds is sufficient to maintain a thousand men, cannot well employ that increase in any other way than in maintaining a thousand men. The rude state of his society does not afford him any manufactured produce any trinkets or baubles of any kind, for which he can exchange that part of his rude produce which is over and above his own consumption. The thousand men whom he thus maintains, depending entirely upon him for their subsistence, must both obey his orders in war, and submit to his jurisdiction in peace. He is necessarily both their general and their judge, and his chieftainship is the necessary effect of the superiority of his fortune. In an opulent and civilized society, a man may possess a much greater fortune, and yet not be able to command a dozen of people. Though the produce of his estate may be sufficient to maintain, and may, perhaps, actually maintain, more than a thousand people, yet, as those people pay for every thing which they get from him, as he gives scarce any thing to any body but in exchange for an equivalent, there is scarce anybody who considers himself as entirely dependent upon him, and his authority extends only over a few menial servants. The authority of fortune, however, is very great, even in an opulent and civilized society. That it is much greater than that either of age or of personal qualities, has been the constant complaint of every period of society which admitted of any considerable inequality of fortune. The first period of society, that of hunters, admits of no such inequality. Universal poverty establishes their universal equality; and the superiority, either of age or of personal qualities, are the feeble, but the sole foundations of authority and subordination. There is, therefore, little or no authority or subordination in this period of society. The second period of society, that of shepherds, admits of very great inequalities of fortune, and there is no period in which the superiority of fortune gives so great authority to those who possess it. There is no period, accordingly, in which authority and subordination are more perfectly established. The authority of an Arabian scherif is very great; that of a Tartar khan altogether despotical.
p52.zh: 第三个原因或情况是财富的优越性。 然而,财富的威信虽然在社会每个时代都很大,但或许在社会最粗鲁的年代里是最大的,这承认了任何重大的财富不平等。 一个鞑靼族酋长,其羊群和群群的增加足以维持一千人,因此除了维持一千人之外,不能很好地利用这一增加。社会无礼的状态使他无法生产任何种类的制成品,为此他可以将他那部分超出自己消费的无礼产品交换出去。 因此,他所维持的千人,完全依靠他维持生计,既必须服从他的命令,也必须和平地服从他的管辖。 他必然既是他们的将军,又是他们的裁判,他的首领地位是他财富优越性的必要效果.在一个富饶文明的社会里,一个人可能拥有更大的财富,但却不能指挥十几个人. 虽然他的遗产的产物可能足以维持,也许可以实际维持一千多人,但是,由于这些人为他们从他那里得到的一切付出了代价,因为他只把任何一点东西给任何机构,却以等价换取,但认为自己完全依赖他的人却寥寥无几,他的权力只延伸到少数卑微的仆人。 然而,即使在一个富饶和文明的社会里,财富的权威也非常伟大。 这比年龄或个人素质要大得多,这是社会每个时期不断抱怨,承认任何重大的财富不平等。社会的第一个时期,即狩猎者时期,没有承认这种不平等。普遍贫穷确立了他们的普遍平等;无论年龄还是个人素质,优越性都是软弱无力的,而是权威和从属地位的唯一基础。 因此,在这一社会时期几乎没有或根本没有权威或从属地位。社会的第二个时期,牧羊人的时期,承认了非常巨大的财富不平等,没有一个时期,财富的优越性赋予拥有者如此巨大的权威. 因此,没有哪个时期可以更完美地确立权威和从属地位。阿拉伯的牧羊人的权力非常大;一个完全专制的鞑靼可汗的权力非常大。

p53.original: The fourth of those causes or circumstances, is the superiority of birth. Superiority of birth supposes an ancient superiority of fortune in the family of the person who claims it. All families are equally ancient; and the ancestors of the prince, though they may be better known, cannot well be more numerous than those of the beggar. Antiquity of family means everywhere the antiquity either of wealth, or of that greatness which is commonly either founded upon wealth, or accompanied with it. Upstart greatness is everywhere less respected than ancient greatness. The hatred of usurpers, the love of the family of an ancient monarch, are in a great measure founded upon the contempt which men naturally have for the former, and upon their veneration for the latter. As a military officer submits, without reluctance, to the authority of a superior by whom he has always been commanded, but cannot bear that his inferior should be set over his head; so men easily submit to a family to whom they and their ancestors have always submitted; but are fired with indignation when another family, in whom they had never acknowledged any such superiority, assumes a dominion over them.
p53.zh: 第四个原因或情况是出生优越。出生的优越性认为,在声称拥有财富的人的家庭中,财富具有古老的优越性。 所有家族都同样古老;王子的祖先虽然可能比较有名,但不能比乞丐的祖先多得多.家庭的古老意味着任何地方的古老财富,或通常建立在财富之上的伟大财富,或与之相伴而生。起动的伟大在任何地方都不如古代伟大受尊重. 对篡位者的憎恨,对古代君主家族的爱,在很大程度上建立在人们自然对前者的蔑视,以及他们对后者的憎恨之上.军官们毫不犹豫地服从上级的命令,但不能忍受他的下贱地位被凌驾于他的头上;因此,男人们很容易屈服于他们和他们的祖先一向服从的家族;但是当他们从未承认过任何这种优越地位的另一个家族对他们拥有统治权时,却被愤慨地解雇。

p54.original: The distinction of birth, being subsequent to the inequality of fortune, can have no place in nations of hunters, among whom all men, being equal in fortune, must likewise be very nearly equal in birth. The son of a wise and brave man may, indeed, even among them, be somewhat more respected than a man of equal merit, who has the misfortune to be the son of a fool or a coward. The difference, however will not be very great; and there never was, I believe, a great family in the world, whose illustration was entirely derived from the inheritance of wisdom and virtue.
p54.zh: 在财富不平等之后,出生的区别在猎人国家中是没有位置的,在猎人中,所有男人在财富方面是平等的,在出生方面也必须是几乎平等的。 一个聪明勇敢的人的儿子,实际上,甚至他们之中,可能比一个有同等功绩的人受到多少更多的尊重,他不幸是傻瓜或懦夫的儿子. 然而,这种差异不会很大;我认为,世界上从来没有一个伟大的家庭,其说明完全来自智慧和美德的继承。

p55.original: The distinction of birth not only may, but always does, take place among nations of shepherds. Such nations are always strangers to every sort of luxury, and great wealth can scarce ever be dissipated among them by improvident profusion. There are no nations, accordingly, who abound more in families revered and honoured on account of their descent from a long race of great and illustrious ancestors; because there are no nations among whom wealth is likely to continue longer in the same families.
p55.zh: 出生的区别不仅可以而且总是在牧羊国之间发生。这些国家对各种奢侈总是陌生的,巨大的财富可能永远无法通过不情愿的挥霍而消失。 因此,没有哪个国家因为祖辈远大和杰出的种族的血统而受到更多家庭的尊敬和荣誉;因为没有哪个国家在同一家庭中财富可能延续更长。

p56.original: Birth and fortune are evidently the two circumstances which principally set one man above another. They are the two great sources of personal distinction, and are, therefore, the principal causes which naturally establish authority and subordination among men. Among nations of shepherds, both those causes operate with their full force. The great shepherd or herdsman, respected on account of his great wealth, and of the great number of those who depend upon him for subsistence, and revered on account of the nobleness of his birth, and of the immemorial antiquity or his illustrious family, has a natural authority over all the inferior shepherds or herdsmen of his horde or clan. He can command the united force of a greater number of people than any of them. His military power is greater than that of any of them. In time of war, they are all of them naturally disposed to muster themselves under his banner, rather than under that of any other person; and his birth and fortune thus naturally procure to him some sort of executive power. By commanding, too, the united force of a greater number of people than any of them, he is best able to compel any one of them, who may have injured another, to compensate the wrong. He is the person, therefore, to whom all those who are too weak to defend themselves naturally look up for protection. It is to him that they naturally complain of the injuries which they imagine have been done to them; and his interposition, in such cases, is more easily submitted to, even by the person complained of, than that of any other person would be. His birth and fortune thus naturally procure him some sort of judicial authority.
p56.zh: 显然,出生和财富是使一个人凌驾于另一个人之上的两种情况。它们是个人区别的两大根源,因此是自然在男子中确立权威和从属地位的主要原因。 在牧羊人的国家中,这两个原因都全力以赴。 大牧人或牧人,因其巨富而受尊崇,而赖其为生者甚多,因出身贵贱而受尊崇,又因古代或宗族之尊贵而受尊崇,对于一切卑贱的牧人或牧人或宗族或宗族之尊贵者,都具有自然权威. 他可以指挥比他们任何一个都更多的人组成的联合部队. 他的军事实力比他们任何一个都大. 在战时,他们都自然地把自己聚集在他的旗帜下,而不是在任何其他人的旗帜下;因此,他的出生和财富自然地向他获得了某种行政权力。 通过指挥,也比任何一个人都要多的团结力量,他最能迫使其中任何一个可能伤害了另一个人的人赔偿错误. 因此,他是一个人,所有那些过于软弱,无法自卫的人自然地寻求保护。 正是对他而言,他们自然地抱怨他们想象中对他们造成的伤害;在这种情况下,即使被控告的人也更容易接受他的干涉,而不是任何其他人的干涉。 因此,他的出生和财富自然会给他带来某种司法权威。

p57.original: It is in the age of shepherds, in the second period of society, that the inequality of fortune first begins to take place, and introduces among men a degree of authority and subordination, which could not possibly exist before. It thereby introduces some degree of that civil government which is indispensably necessary for its own preservation; and it seems to do this naturally, and even independent of the consideration of that necessity. The consideration of that necessity comes, no doubt, afterwards, to contribute very much to maintain and secure that authority and subordination. The rich, in particular, are necessarily interested to support that order of things, which can alone secure them in the possession of their own advantages. Men of inferior wealth combine to defend those of superior wealth in the possession of their property, in order that men of superior wealth may combine to defend them in the possession of theirs. All the inferior shepherds and herdsmen feel, that the security of their own herds and flocks depends upon the security of those of the great shepherd or herdsman; that the maintenance of their lesser authority depends upon that of his greater authority; and that upon their subordination to him depends his power of keeping their inferiors in subordination to them. They constitute a sort of little nobility, who feel themselves interested to defend the property, and to support the authority, of their own little sovereign, in order that he may be able to defend their property, and to support their authority. Civil government, so far as it is instituted for the security of property, is, in reality, instituted for the defence of the rich against the poor, or of those who have some property against those who have none at all.
p57.zh: 正是在牧羊人的时代,在社会的第二个时期,财富的不平等首先开始发生,在男性中引入了某种程度的权威和从属地位,而这种权力和从属地位以前不可能存在. 因此,它引入了某种程度的民政政府,而这种政府是维护它本身所必不可少的;它似乎自然地这样做,甚至不考虑这种必要性。事后,对这一必要性的审议无疑将大大有助于维持和保障这一权威和从属地位。特别是富人,他们必然有兴趣支持这种事物的顺序,而这种顺序单靠他们自己就能保证他们拥有自己的优势.低等财富的人联合起来保卫拥有财产的上等财富的人,以便高等财富的人联合起来保卫他们拥有的财产. 所有卑劣的牧羊人和牧民都觉得,他们自己的牧羊群和羊群的安全取决于伟大的牧羊人或牧羊人的安全;他们较低的权威的维持取决于他更大的权威;他们服从他的权力取决于他保持他们的卑劣服从他们的能力. 他们构成一种小贵族,他们觉得自己有兴趣捍卫财产,支持他们自己的小君主的权威,以便他能够捍卫他们的财产,支持他们的权威. 实际上,为了财产安全而建立的民政政府是为了保护富人,或保护那些拥有某些财产的人,而保护那些根本没有财产的人。

p58.original: The judicial authority of such a sovereign, however, far from being a cause of expense, was, for a long time, a source of revenue to him. The persons who applied to him for justice were always willing to pay for it, and a present never failed to accompany a petition. After the authority of the sovereign, too, was thoroughly established, the person found guilty, over and above the satisfaction which he was obliged to make to the party, was like-wise forced to pay an amercement to the sovereign. He had given trouble, he had disturbed, he had broke the peace of his lord the king, and for those offences an amercement was thought due. In the Tartar governments of Asia, in the governments of Europe which were founded by the German and Scythian nations who overturned the Roman empire, the administration of justice was a considerable source of revenue, both to the sovereign, and to all the lesser chiefs or lords who exercised under him any particular jurisdiction, either over some particular tribe or clan, or over some particular territory or district. Originally, both the sovereign and the inferior chiefs used to exercise this jurisdiction in their own persons. Afterwards, they universally found it convenient to delegate it to some substitute, bailiff, or judge. This substitute, however, was still obliged to account to his principal or constituent for the profits of the jurisdiction. Whoever reads the instructions (They are to be found in Tyrol's History of England) which were given to the judges of the circuit in the time of Henry II will see clearly that those judges were a sort of itinerant factors, sent round the country for the purpose of levying certain branches of the king's revenue. In those days, the administration of justice not only afforded a certain revenue to the sovereign, but, to procure this revenue, seems to have been one of the principal advantages which he proposed to obtain by the administration of justice.
p58.zh: 然而,长期以来,这样一个君主的司法当局远非造成开支的原因,而是他的一个收入来源。向申诉人申请司法的人总是愿意为此付出代价,一份礼物也从未与请愿书一起提交。 在君主的权威也得到彻底确立之后,被判定有罪的人,除了他有义务向该党作出的满意程度外,还同样被迫向君主支付赎罪金。 他给人麻烦,他扰乱,他打破了国王主的安宁,而且对于这些罪行,人们认为应该作出妥协。在亚洲的鞑靼政府中,在推翻罗马帝国的德意志和锡伯尼亚诸国建立的欧洲政府中,司法是相当可观的收入来源,无论是对于君主,还是对于在他领导下行使任何特定管辖权的下级酋长或领主,无论是对某些特定部落或部族,还是某些特定领土或地区,都是如此.最初,君主和下级酋长都曾经在他们自己的人中行使这种管辖权。之后,他们普遍认为将其委托给一些替代者、法警或法官是方便的。 然而,这一替代人仍有义务将管辖权的利润计入其本金或组成。凡是在亨利二世时期交给巡回法官的指令(这些指令见于蒂罗尔的"英格兰史"),都会清楚地看到这些法官是某种巡回因素,派到全国各地来征收国王收入的某些分支. 在那些时候,司法行政不仅为君主提供了一定的收入,而且为了获得这种收入,他提议通过司法行政获得的主要好处之一。

p59.original: This scheme of making the administration of justice subservient to the purposes of revenue, could scarce fail to be productive of several very gross abuses. The person who applied for justice with a large present in his hand, was likely to get something more than justice; while he who applied for it with a small one was likely to get something less. Justice, too, might frequently be delayed, in order that this present might be repeated. The amercement, besides, of the person complained of, might frequently suggest a very strong reason for finding him in the wrong, even when he had not really been so. That such abuses were far from being uncommon, the ancient history of every country in Europe bears witness.
p59.zh: 这种使司法行政服从于收入目的的图谋,可能不会造成若干非常严重的侵权行为。申请司法的人手里拿着大礼物,可能得到的不只是司法;申请司法的人用小礼物,可能得到的更少。司法工作也会经常被拖延,以便重复目前的情况。 此外,申诉人的同情心可能经常表明,即使他没有真正这样做,也有理由认定他犯有错误。 这种虐待远非罕见,欧洲每个国家的古老历史就是明证。

p60.original: When the sovereign or chief exercises his judicial authority in his own person, how much soever he might abuse it, it must have been scarce possible to get any redress; because there could seldom be any body powerful enough to call him to account. When he exercised it by a bailiff, indeed, redress might sometimes be had. If it was for his own benefit only, that the bailiff had been guilty of an act of injustice, the sovereign himself might not always be unwilling to punish him, or to oblige him to repair the wrong. But if it was for the benefit of his sovereign; if it was in order to make court to the person who appointed him, and who might prefer him, that he had committed any act of oppression; redress would, upon most occasions, be as impossible as if the sovereign had committed it himself. In all barbarous governments, accordingly, in all those ancient governments of Europe in particular, which were founded upon the ruins of the Roman empire, the administration of justice appears for a long time to have been extremely corrupt; far from being quite equal and impartial, even under the best monarchs, and altogether profligate under the worst.
p60.zh: 当君主或酋长亲自行使司法权时,无论他可能滥用多少司法权,都不可能得到任何补救;因为几乎没有任何机构能够有权要求他承担责任。 当他由法警行使权力时,确实有时可能会得到补救。 如果只是为了他自己的利益,法警犯了不公正的行为,那么君主本人可能并不总是不愿意惩罚他,或者强迫他改正错误. 但如果是为了他的君主的利益;如果是为了让任命他的人和可能更喜欢他的人的法庭,他犯下了任何压迫行为;在多数情况下,补救就如同君主自己犯下了这种罪行一样不可能。在所有野蛮政府中,因此,在所有那些建立在罗马帝国废墟之上的古代欧洲政府中,司法行政似乎在很长一段时间内是极其腐败的;远非相当平等和公正的,甚至在最优秀的君主之下,在最坏的统治下是完全挥霍的.

p61.original: Among nations of shepherds, where the sovereign or chief is only the greatest shepherd or herdsman of the horde or clan, he is maintained in the same manner as any of his vassals or subjects, by the increase of his own herds or flocks. Among those nations of husbandmen, who are but just come out of the shepherd state, and who are not much advanced beyond that state, such as the Greek tribes appear to have been about the time of the Trojan war, and our German and Scythian ancestors, when they first settled upon the ruins of the western empire; the sovereign or chief is, in the same manner, only the greatest landlord of the country, and is maintained in the same manner as any other landlord, by a revenue derived from his own private estate, or from what, in modern Europe, was called the demesne of the crown. His subjects, upon ordinary occasions, contribute nothing to his support, except when, in order to protect them from the oppression of some of their fellow-subjects, they stand in need of his authority. The presents which they make him upon such occasions constitute the whole ordinary revenue, the whole of the emoluments which, except, perhaps, upon some very extraordinary emergencies, he derives from his dominion over them. When Agamemnon, in Homer, offers to Achilles, for his friendship, the sovereignty of seven Greek cities, the sole advantage which he mentions as likely to be derived from it was, that the people would honour him with presents. As long as such presents, as long as the emoluments of justice, or what may be called the fees of court, constituted, in this manner, the whole ordinary revenue which the sovereign derived from his sovereignty, it could not well be expected, it could not even decently be proposed, that he should give them up altogether. It might, and it frequently was proposed, that he should regulate and ascertain them. But after they had been so regulated and ascertained, how to hinder a person who was all-powerful from extending them beyond those regulations, was still very difficult, not to say impossible. During the continuance of this state of things, therefore, the corruption of justice, naturally resulting from the arbitrary and uncertain nature of those presents, scarce admitted of any effectual remedy.
