p61.zh: 在牧羊国中,君主或酋长只是群或部族中最伟大的牧羊人或牧羊人,通过自己牧羊或羊群的增多,他与任何一个牧羊人或臣民一样得到同样的维护. 在那些丈夫的国度中,他们只是刚走出牧人国,而且没有超过那个国度的多少进步,如希腊部落似乎已经是特洛伊战争的年代,我们的德国人和斯西思人的祖先,他们最初定居在西帝国的废墟上;主权或酋长,以同样的方式,只是国家最大的地主,并且以与其他任何地主一样的方式维持,其收入来自自己的私人庄园,或者在现代欧洲,从什么地方,被称为王冠的德米恩. 他的臣民在一般情况下,除了为了保护他们免受某些同僚的压迫,他们需要他的权威之外,他不为他的支持作任何贡献. 他们在这种情况下给他的礼物构成整个普通收入,即整个薪酬,除了在某些非常非常的紧急情况下,他来自他对薪酬的统治。 当在荷马的阿伽门农为了他的友谊,向阿基里斯提议拥有七座希腊城市的主权时,他提到唯一可能由此获得的优势是人民会以礼物来纪念他. 只要这样,只要司法的薪酬或所谓的法庭费用以这种方式构成主权人从其主权中产生的整个普通收入,就无法指望,甚至无法体面地提议,他应完全放弃这些收入。 他可能而且经常建议,他应该加以管制和确定。 但是,经过如此管理和确定之后,如何阻止一个全能的人超越这些规章,这仍然非常困难,更不用说不可能了。 因此,在这种状况持续下去期间,司法腐败自然是任意和不确定造成的,很少承认任何有效的补救办法。

p62.original: But when, from different causes, chiefly from the continually increasing expense of defending the nation against the invasion of other nations, the private estate of the sovereign had become altogether insufficient for defraying the expense of the sovereignty; and when it had become necessary that the people should, for their own security, contribute towards this expense by taxes of different kinds; it seems to have been very commonly stipulated, that no present for the administration of justice should, under any pretence, be accepted either by the sovereign, or by his bailiffs and substitutes, the judges. Those presents, it seems to have been supposed, could more easily be abolished altogether, than effectually regulated and ascertained. Fixed salaries were appointed to the judges, which were supposed to compensate to them the loss of whatever might have been their share of the ancient emoluments of justice; as the taxes more than compensated to the sovereign the loss of his. Justice was then said to be administered gratis.
p62.zh: 但是,由于各种原因,主要是由于保卫国家不受其他国家入侵的费用不断增加,主权的私人财产已完全不足以支付主权费用;人民为了自己的安全,必须用不同种类的税收来支付这笔费用;似乎很普遍地规定,在任何借口下,任何司法活动都不得被主权者或其法警和替代者、法官所接受。 这些礼物,看来是应该的,比实际管制和确定更容易被完全废除。法官的固定薪金被任命来补偿他们可能丧失的古代司法薪酬份额;因为税收比君主的损失还多。 然后,据说司法是免费提供的。

p63.original: Justice, however, never was in reality administered gratis in any country. Lawyers and attorneys, at least, must always be paid by the parties; and if they were not, they would perform their duty still worse than they actually perform it. The fees annually paid to lawyers and attorneys, amount, in every court, to a much greater sum than the salaries of the judges. The circumstance of those salaries being paid by the crown, can nowhere much diminish the necessary expense of a law-suit. But it was not so much to diminish the expense, as to prevent the corruption of justice, that the judges were prohibited from receiving my present or fee from the parties.
p63.zh: 然而,在任何国家,司法实际上从来没有免费管理。律师和律师至少必须始终由当事人支付报酬;如果不是,他们履行的职责会比实际履行的还要差。 每年向律师和律师支付的费用,在每个法院都比法官的工资大得多。由王室支付这些工资的情况绝对不能大大降低法律诉讼的必要费用。 但是,为了减少开支,防止司法腐败,法官们被禁止从当事方那里得到我的礼物或费用,这不是什么大事情。

p64.original: The office of judge is in itself so very honourable, that men are willing to accept of it, though accompanied with very small emoluments. The inferior office of justice of peace, though attended with a good deal of trouble, and in most cases with no emoluments at all, is an object of ambition to the greater part of our country gentlemen. The salaries of all the different judges, high and low, together with the whole expense of the administration and execution of justice, even where it is not managed with very good economy, makes, in any civilized country, but a very inconsiderable part of the whole expense of government.
p64.zh: 法官职务本身非常光荣,男人愿意接受,尽管报酬很低。低级的治安官虽然有不少麻烦,而且在多数情况下根本没有报酬,但对于我国大部分的先生们来说,却是野心勃勃的对象. 所有不同的法官,无论高低,其工资,再加上司法的行政和执行的全部费用,即使没有以非常良好的经济管理司法,在任何文明国家,都使得政府的全部费用中,只有极小的一部分。

p65.original: The whole expense of justice, too, might easily be defrayed by the fees of court; and, without exposing the administration of justice to any real hazard of corruption, the public revenue might thus be entirely discharged from a certain, though perhaps but a small incumbrance. It is difficult to regulate the fees of court effectually, where a person so powerful as the sovereign is to share in them and to derive any considerable part of his revenue from them. It is very easy, where the judge is the principal person who can reap any benefit from them. The law can very easily oblige the judge to respect the regulation though it might not always be able to make the sovereign respect it. Where the fees of court are precisely regulated and ascertained where they are paid all at once, at a certain period of every process, into the hands of a cashier or receiver, to be by him distributed in certain known proportions among the different judges after the process is decided and not till it is decided; there seems to be no more danger of corruption than when such fees are prohibited altogether. Those fees, without occasioning any considerable increase in the expense of a law-suit, might be rendered fully sufficient for defraying the whole expense of justice. But not being paid to the judges till the process was determined, they might be some incitement to the diligence of the court in examining and deciding it. In courts which consisted of a considerable number of judges, by proportioning the share of each judge to the number of hours and days which he had employed in examining the process, either in the court, or in a committee, by order of the court, those fees might give some encouragement to the diligence of each particular judge. Public services are never better performed, than when their reward comes only in consequence of their being performed, and is proportioned to the diligence employed in performing them. In the different parliaments of France, the fees of court (called epices and vacations) constitute the far greater part of the emoluments of the judges. After all deductions are made, the neat salary paid by the crown to a counsellor or judge in the parliament of Thoulouse, in rank and dignity the second parliament of the kingdom, amounts only to 150 livres, about £6:11s. sterling a-year. About seven years ago, that sum was in the same place the ordinary yearly wages of a common footman. The distribution of these epices, too, is according to the diligence of the judges. A diligent judge gains a comfortable, though moderate revenue, by his office; an idle one gets little more than his salary. Those parliaments are, perhaps, in many respects, not very convenient courts of justice; but they have never been accused; they seem never even to have been suspected of corruption.
p65.zh: 司法的全部费用也很容易由法院费用支付;而且,在不使司法行政面临任何真正的腐败危险的情况下,公共收入可能完全从某一项支出中扣除,尽管可能只是少量的积蓄。很难对法院的收费进行有效的管理,因为像君主这样有权势的人要分享这种收费并从中获取他相当一部分的收入。 在法官是能够从中获得任何好处的主要人员的情况下,这是非常容易的。法律可以很容易地迫使法官尊重该条例,尽管它可能并不总是能够使君主尊重该条例。 如果法院费用得到准确管理和确定,在每个过程的某个时期,全部由出纳员或收纳员一并支付,在程序决定之后由他按一定的已知比例在不同的法官之间分配,直到决定为止;似乎没有比完全禁止这种费用更可能发生腐败。这些费用,如果不会大大增加诉讼费用,则可能足以支付全部司法费用。 但是,在程序确定之前,不向法官支付报酬,这也许是对法院审查和裁决的某种煽动。 在由相当多法官组成的法院,通过将每位法官的比例与他在法院或委员会审查程序时所花的时间和天数相配,根据法院的命令,这些收费可能在一定程度上鼓励每位法官的勤奋。公共服务的绩效永远好不到哪里去,因为公共服务的回报只是由于公共服务的绩效,而且与公共服务的绩效相称。 在法国的不同议会中,法院费用(称为史诗和假期)是法官薪酬的绝大部分。 在扣除所有扣除后,王冠付给杜卢兹议会的顾问或法官的纯净工资,在王国第二议会的级别和尊严上,每年只相当于150里弗,约为6:11.英镑.大约7年前,这笔钱与普通男仆的普通年薪相同。 这些史诗的分布也是根据法官们的勤勉而来.勤奋的法官从他的办公室获得舒适的收入,尽管是中等的收入;闲暇的法官得到的比他的工资略多一点。 这些议会也许在许多方面并不十分方便;但它们从未受到过指控;它们似乎从未被怀疑腐败。

p66.original: The fees of court seem originally to have been the principal support of the different courts of justice in England. Each court endeavoured to draw to itself as much business as it could, and was, upon that account, willing to take cognizance of many suits which were not originally intended to fall under its jurisdiction. The court of king's bench, instituted for the trial of criminal causes only, took cognizance of civil suits; the plaintiff pretending that the defendant, in not doing him justice, had been guilty of some trespass or misdemeanour. The court of exchequer, instituted for the levying of the king's revenue, and for enforcing the payment of such debts only as were due to the king, took cognizance of all other contract debts; the planitiff alleging that he could not pay the king, because the defendant would not pay him. In consequence of such fictions, it came, in many cases, to depend altogether upon the parties, before what court they would choose to have their cause tried, and each court endeavoured, by superior dispatch and impartiality, to draw to itself as many causes as it could. The present admirable constitution of the courts of justice in England was, perhaps, originally, in a great measure, formed by this emulation, which anciently took place between their respective judges: each judge endeavouring to give, in his own court, the speediest and most effectual remedy which the law would admit, for every sort of injustice. Originally, the courts of law gave damages only for breach of contract. The court of chancery, as a court of conscience, first took upon it to enforce the specific performance of agreements. When the breach of contract consisted in the non-payment of money, the damage sustained could be compensated in no other way than by ordering payment, which was equivalent to a specific performance of the agreement. In such cases, therefore, the remedy of the courts of law was sufficient. It was not so in others. When the tenant sued his lord for having unjustly outed him of his lease, the damages which he recovered were by no means equivalent to the possession of the land. Such causes, therefore, for some time, went all to the court of chancery, to the no small loss of the courts of law. It was to draw back such causes to themselves, that the courts of law are said to have invented the artificial and fictitious writ of ejectment, the most effectual remedy for an unjust outer or dispossession of land.
p66.zh: 法院收费最初似乎是英国不同法院的主要支持. 每个法院都努力尽其所能地为自己谋取生意,并因此愿意承认许多原本不打算属于其管辖范围的诉讼。仅为刑事原因审判而成立的国王法庭受理了民事诉讼;原告假装被告不为他伸张正义,犯有一些违法或轻罪。征收国王收入和强制支付仅欠国王的债务的征收法院承认了所有其他合同债务;规划师声称他不能支付国王,因为被告不会支付他。 由于这种虚构,在许多情况下,在他们选择的哪个法院审理其诉讼事由之前,完全依赖当事方,而每个法院都努力通过上级的派遣和公正,尽可能多地为自己引出诉讼事由。英国法院目前令人钦佩的宪法,最初或许在很大程度上是由这一仿照形成的,这种仿照是各自法官之间古老的:每位法官都努力在自己的法院为各种不公正行为提供法律所承认的最迅速和最有效的补救办法。最初,法院只判给违约赔偿金。 作为良心法庭,法院首先要求法院强制执行协议的具体执行。 如果违反合同的行为包括不支付钱款,所造成的损害只能通过命令付款得到赔偿,这相当于具体履行协议。 因此,在这种情况下,法院的补救办法就足够了。其他国家的情况并非如此。 当房客控告他的主人不公正地放弃他的租约时,他收回的赔偿金绝不等于土地的占有。 因此,一段时间以来,这些原因都由法院解决,法院的损失并不小。 正是出于这些原因,据说法院发明了人为的和虚构的驱逐令状,这是对不公正的外部或剥夺土地的最有效的补救办法。

p67.original: A stamp-duty upon the law proceedings of each particular court, to be levied by that court, and applied towards the maintenance of the judges, and other officers belonging to it, might in the same manner, afford a revenue sufficient for defraying the expense of the administration of justice, without bringing any burden upon the general revenue of the society. The judges, indeed, might in this case, be under the temptation of multiplying unnecessarily the proceedings upon every cause, in order to increase, as much as possible, the produce of such a stamp-duty. It has been the custom in modern Europe to regulate, upon most occasions, the payment of the attorneys and clerks of court according to the number of pages which they had occasion to write; the court, however, requiring that each page should contain so many lines, and each line so many words. In order to increase their payment, the attorneys and clerks have contrived to multiply words beyond all necessity, to the corruption of the law language of, I believe, every court of justice in Europe. A like temptation might, perhaps, occasion a like corruption in the form of law proceedings.
p67.zh: 由法院征收并用于维持法官和其他官员的每个特定法院的法律程序的印花税,同样可能提供足以支付司法行政费用的收入,而不会给社会的一般收入带来任何负担。 实际上,法官们在本案中可能会受到诱惑,不必要地将诉讼扩大到各种原因,以便尽可能增加这种印花税的产量。现代欧洲的习惯是,在大多数情况下,根据律师和法庭书记员的写作页数,对支付他们的费用作出规定;然而,法院要求每一页应包含如此多的行,每一行应包含如此多的字。 为了增加报酬,律师和书记官们想方设法将言词倍加夸张,超越一切必要之处,以至破坏我认为欧洲每个法院的法律语言。类似诱惑可能以法律诉讼的形式出现类似腐败的情况。

p68.original: But whether the administration of justice be so contrived as to defray its own expense, or whether the judges be maintained by fixed salaries paid to them from some other fund, it does not seen necessary that the person or persons entrusted with the executive power should be charged with the management of that fund, or with the payment of those salaries. That fund might arise from the rent of landed estates, the management of each estate being entrusted to the particular court which was to be maintained by it. That fund might arise even from the interest of a sum of money, the lending out of which might, in the same manner, be entrusted to the court which was to be maintained by it. A part, though indeed but a small part of the salary of the judges of the court of session in Scotland, arises from the interest of a sum of money. The necessary instability of such a fund seems, however, to render it an improper one for the maintenance of an institution which ought to last for ever.
p68.zh: 但是,无论司法行政是自行开支,还是由从其他基金付给法官的固定薪金维持,都没有必要要求被赋予行政权力的人管理该基金,或支付这些薪金。这笔资金可能来自地产的租金,每个地产的管理都委托给由法院维持的特定法院。这笔资金甚至可能来自一笔钱的利息,而这笔钱的贷款同样可能委托给法院,而法院将维持这笔资金。一部分,尽管的确只是苏格兰开庭法院法官薪金的一小部分,是因一笔钱的利息而产生。 然而,这种基金的必要不稳定似乎使它成为一个维持一个应该永远维持的机构的不适当基金。

p69.original: The separation of the judicial from the executive power, seems originally to have arisen from the increasing business of the society, in consequence of its increasing improvement. The administration of justice became so laborious and so complicated a duty, as to require the undivided attention of the person to whom it was entrusted. The person entrusted with the executive power, not having leisure to attend to the decision of private causes himself, a deputy was appointed to decide them in his stead. In the progress of the Roman greatness, the consul was too much occupied with the political affairs of the state, to attend to the administration of justice. A praetor, therefore, was appointed to administer it in his stead. In the progress of the European monarchies, which were founded upon the ruins of the Roman empire, the sovereigns and the great lords came universally to consider the administration of justice as an office both too laborious and too ignoble for them to execute in their own persons. They universally, therefore, discharged themselves of it, by appointing a deputy, bailiff or judge.
p69.zh: 司法权与行政权的分离,最初似乎是由于社会业务日益增加而导致的,因为社会日益改善。司法工作变得如此繁琐复杂,要求受委托人给予全心全意的注意。受委托行使行政权力的人,没有闲暇地亲自处理私人事业的决定,因此指定了一名副手代他决定这些决定。在罗马大帝的进化中,执政官被过多地占用了国家政治事务,无法处理司法事务. 因此,任命了一名校长来代他管理。 在建立在罗马帝国废墟之上的欧洲君主制的进步中,君主和大领主们普遍认为司法是一个太劳累和太可鄙的办公室,他们不能在自己的人中执行. 因此,他们普遍通过任命一名副手、法警或法官来履行这一义务。

p70.original: When the judicial is united to the executive power, it is scarce possible that justice should not frequently be sacrificed to what is vulgarly called politics. The persons entrusted with the great interests of the state may even without any corrupt views, sometimes imagine it necessary to sacrifice to those interests the rights of a private man. But upon the impartial administration of justice depends the liberty of every individual, the sense which he has of his own security. In order to make every individual feel himself perfectly secure in the possession of every right which belongs to him, it is not only necessary that the judicial should be separated from the executive power, but that it should be rendered as much as possible independent of that power. The judge should not be liable to be removed from his office according to the caprice of that power. The regular payment of his salary should not depend upon the good will, or even upon the good economy of that power.
p70.zh: 当司法与行政权力统一时,很难说正义不会经常被俗称的政治所牺牲。受托维护国家重大利益的人甚至可以不带任何腐败观点,有时会想象有必要为这些利益牺牲私人的权利。 但是,公正司法取决于每个人的自由,即他本人的安全感。 为了使每一个人都感到自己完全安全地拥有属于他的每一项权利,不仅有必要将司法权与行政权分开,而且应当尽可能使其独立于该权力。法官不应因权力的诱惑而被撤职。定期支付他的工资不应取决于善意,甚至不应取决于该权力的良好经济。

p71.original: PART III. Of the Expense of public Works and public Institutions.
p71.zh: 第三编公共工程和公共机构开支。

p72.original: The third and last duty of the sovereign or commonwealth, is that of erecting and maintaining those public institutions and those public works, which though they may be in the highest degree advantageous to a great society, are, however, of such a nature, that the profit could never repay the expense to any individual, or small number of individuals; and which it, therefore, cannot be expected that any individual, or small number of individuals, should erect or maintain. The performance of this duty requires, too, very different degrees of expense in the different periods of society.
p72.zh: 主权或联邦的第三项也是最后一项义务是建立和维持这些公共机构和公共工程,尽管它们可能对一个伟大的社会最有利,但它们具有这种性质,即利润永远不能偿还任何个人或少数个人的费用;因此,不能指望任何个人或少数个人建立或维持这种性质。履行这项义务也需要在社会的不同时期付出不同程度的费用。

p73.original: After the public institutions and public works necessary for the defence of the society, and for the administration of justice, both of which have already been mentioned, the other works and institutions of this kind are chiefly for facilitating the commerce of the society, and those for promoting the instruction of the people. The institutions for instruction are of two kinds: those for the education of the youth, and those for the instruction of people of all ages. The consideration of the manner in which the expense of those different sorts of public works and institutions may be most properly defrayed will divide this third part of the present chapter into three different articles.
p73.zh: 在为保卫社会,司法行政所必要的公共机构和公共工程之后,其他这类工程和机构主要是为社会商业提供便利,以及促进人民的教育。教学机构分为两类:青年教育机构和各种年龄的人教育机构。 审议如何以最适当方式支付这些不同类型的公共工程和机构的费用,将把本章的第三部分分为三个不同的条款。

p74.original: ARTICLE I.--Of the public Works and Institutions for facilitating the Commerce of the Society.
p74.zh: 第1条 -- -- 促进本协会商业的公共工程和机构。

p75.original: And, first, of those which are necessary for facilitating Commerce in general.
p75.zh: 首先,对于促进一般商业而言,是必需的。

p76.original: That the erection and maintenance of the public works which facilitate the commerce of any country, such as good roads, bridges, navigable canals, harbours, etc. must require very different degrees of expense in the different periods of society, is evident without any proof. The expense of making and maintaining the public roads of any country must evidently increase with the annual produce of the land and labour of that country, or with the quantity and weight of the goods which it becomes necessary to fetch and carry upon those roads. The strength of a bridge must be suited to the number and weight of the carriages which are likely to pass over it. The depth and the supply of water for a navigable canal must be proportioned to the number and tonnage of the lighters which are likely to carry goods upon it; the extent of a harbour, to the number of the shipping which are likely to take shelter in it.
p76.zh: 兴建和维护有利于任何国家商业的公共工程,例如良好的道路、桥梁、通航运河、港口等,必须在社会不同时期要求非常不同的开支,这是显而易见的,没有任何证据。任何国家修建和维护公共道路的费用必须随着该国土地和劳动力的年产量,或者随着在公路上取货和搬运货物的数量和重量而明显增加。桥梁的强度必须适合有可能通过桥梁的马车的数量和重量。通航运河的深度和供水量必须与可能载运货物的打火机的数量和吨位成比例;港口的范围,与可能躲藏在其中的航运数量成比例。

p77.original: It does not seem necessary that the expense of those public works should be defrayed from that public revenue, as it is commonly called, of which the collection and application are in most countries, assigned to the executive power. The greater part of such public works may easily be so managed, as to afford a particular revenue, sufficient for defraying their own expense without bringing any burden upon the general revenue of the society.
p77.zh: 这些公共工程的费用似乎没有必要从这种公共收入中支付,而这种收入通常被称作是行政权力所支配的,在大多数国家,征收和应用是行政收入。 这种公共工程的大部分可能很容易得到管理,从而能够提供一定的收入,足以支付自己的开支,而不会给社会的一般收入带来任何负担。

p78.original: A highway, a bridge, a navigable canal, for example, may, in most cases, be both made add maintained by a small toll upon the carriages which make use of them; a harbour, by a moderate port-duty upon the tonnage of the shipping which load or unload in it. The coinage, another institution for facilitating commerce, in many countries, not only defrays its own expense, but affords a small revenue or a seignorage to the sovereign. The post-office, another institution for the same purpose, over and above defraying its own expense, affords, in almost all countries, a very considerable revenue to the sovereign.
p78.zh: 例如,在多数情况下,公路、桥梁、通航运河都可以由使用这些公路的车厢的少量收费来维持;港口则由在港口内装卸的航运吨位的适度港口义务来维持。铸币局是在许多国家促进商业的另一个机构,它不仅支付自己的费用,而且向主权提供少量收入或铸币。后办事处是另一个出于同样目的的机构,除了支付自己的费用外,在几乎所有国家里,都为主权国家提供了相当可观的收入。

p79.original: When the carriages which pass over a highway or a bridge, and the lighters which sail upon a navigable canal, pay toll in proportion to their weight or their tonnage, they pay for the maintenance of those public works exactly in proportion to the wear and tear which they occasion of them. It seems scarce possible to invent a more equitable way of maintaining such works. This tax or toll, too, though it is advanced by the carrier, is finally paid by the consumer, to whom it must always be charged in the price of the goods. As the expense of carriage, however, is very much reduced by means of such public works, the goods, notwithstanding the toll, come cheaper to the consumer than they could otherwise have done, their price not being so much raised by the toll, as it is lowered by the cheapness of the carriage. The person who finally pays this tax, therefore, gains by the application more than he loses by the payment of it. His payment is exactly in proportion to his gain. It is, in reality, no more than a part of that gain which he is obliged to give up, in order to get the rest. It seems impossible to imagine a more equitable method of raising a tax. When the toll upon carriages of luxury, upon coaches, post-chaises, etc. is made somewhat higher in proportion to their weight, than upon carriages of necessary use, such as carts, waggons, etc. the indolence and vanity of the rich is made to contribute, in a very easy manner, to the relief of the poor, by rendering cheaper the transportation of heavy goods to all the different parts of the country.
p79.zh: 当通过高速公路或桥梁的马车和在通航运河上航行的打火机按照重量或吨位支付相应的费用时,它们就按照自己所经历的磨损情况支付维持这些公共工程的费用。似乎很难发明一种更公平的方式来维持这种工作。 这种税费或通行费,虽然是由承运人垫付的,但最后还是由消费者支付,必须始终以货物的价格向消费者收取。 然而,由于这种公共工程使运输费用大大降低,尽管收费,但货物对消费者来说比他们本来可以做到的便宜,其价格并没有因为收费而提高,因为运输的廉价而降低。 因此,最后缴纳该税的人通过申请获得的收益大于他通过缴纳该税而失去的收益。 他的付款与他的收益成正比。 实际上,他为了获得剩下的钱而不得不放弃的只是这一收益的一部分。似乎无法想象一种更公平的征税方法。奢侈品的车厢、教练、后车厢等造成的损失,按重量比例比必要的车厢,如马车、华贡等,要略高一些。 富人的不义和虚荣,通过使重货物运输到全国各地,更加便宜,从而非常容易地帮助救济穷人。

p80.original: When high-roads, bridges, canals, etc. are in this manner made and supported by the commerce which is carried on by means of them, they can be made only where that commerce requires them, and, consequently, where it is proper to make them. Their expense, too, their grandeur and magnificence, must be suited to what that commerce can afford to pay. They must be made, consequently, as it is proper to make them. A magnificent high-road cannot be made through a desert country, where there is little or no commerce, or merely because it happens to lead to the country villa of the intendant of the province, or to that of some great lord, to whom the intendant finds it convenient to make his court. A great bridge cannot be thrown over a river at a place where nobody passes, or merely to embellish the view from the windows of a neighbouring palace; things which sometimes happen in countries, where works of this kind are carried on by any other revenue than that which they themselves are capable of affording.
p80.zh: 当高架道路、桥梁、运河等以这种方式由商业制造和支撑时,只有在商业需要时才能制造,因此,只有在商业需要时才能制造。 他们的费用,以及他们高傲和壮大的费用,必须适合该商业能够支付的费用。 因此,必须作出这些决定,因为作出这些决定是适当的。一条宏伟的高路不能穿过沙漠国家,那里几乎没有商业或没有商业,或者仅仅因为它恰好通往该省意图者的乡村别墅,或者某个大领主的别墅,意图者认为让自己的宫廷变得方便. 在没有人经过的地方,不能把一座大桥扔到河上,或者只是把邻近宫殿的窗户上的风景装饰一下;有时在各国发生的事情,这种类型的工程除了他们自己能够负担的外,还有任何其他收入。

p81.original: In several different parts of Europe, the toll or lock-duty upon a canal is the property of private persons, whose private interest obliges them to keep up the canal. If it is not kept in tolerable order, the navigation necessarily ceases altogether, and, along with it, the whole profit which they can make by the tolls. If those tolls were put under the management of commissioners, who had themselves no interest in them, they might be less attentive to the maintenance of the works which produced them. The canal of Languedoc cost the king of France and the province upwards of thirteen millions of livres, which (at twenty-eight livres the mark of silver, the value of French money in the end of the last century) amounted to upwards of nine hundred thousand pounds sterling. When that great work was finished, the most likely method, it was found, of keeping it in constant repair, was to make a present of the tolls to Riquet, the engineer who planned and conducted the work. Those tolls constitute, at present, a very large estate to the different branches of the family of that gentleman, who have, therefore, a great interest to keep the work in constant repair. But had those tolls been put under the management of commissioners, who had no such interest, they might perhaps, have been dissipated in ornamental and unnecessary expenses, while the most essential parts of the works were allowed to go to ruin.
p81.zh: 在欧洲的几个不同地区,运河的收费或锁门义务是私人的财产,他们的私人利益迫使他们保持运河。 如果它不能维持在可容忍的秩序中,航行必然会完全停止,连同它一起,它们能够从费用中获得的全部利润。 如果这些费用由委员们管理,他们自己对费用没有兴趣,他们可能不太注意维持生产这些费用的工程。朗盖多克的运河使法国国王和该省损失了1300万里弗尔以上,这(在银印二十八里弗尔,上世纪末法国货币的价值)达到90万英磅以上. 当这项伟大的工作完成后,最可能的方法,就是不断修理它, 就是给计划并进行这项工作的工程师里奎特 做一份收费礼物。 这些通行费目前是这位先生家庭不同分支的一个非常大的财产,因此,他非常有兴趣使工作不断得到维修。 但是,如果这些费用由委员们管理,而委员们可能没有这种兴趣,他们也许就因装饰性开支和不必要的开支而散失,而最关键的部分却被允许毁灭。

p82.original: The tolls for the maintenance of a highroad cannot, with any safety, be made the property of private persons. A high-road, though entirely neglected, does not become altogether impassable, though a canal does. The proprietors of the tolls upon a high-road, therefore, might neglect altogether the repair of the road, and yet continue to levy very nearly the same tolls. It is proper, therefore, that the tolls for the maintenance of such a work should be put under the management of commissioners or trustees.
p82.zh: 维护高架道路的费用,在任何安全的情况下,都不能成为私人的财产。一条高路虽然被完全忽略,但并非完全无法通行,尽管一条运河确实如此。 因此,公路收费的所有人可能完全忽视公路的修理,但仍继续征收几乎相同的收费。 因此,维持这项工作的费用应由专员或受托人管理是适当的。

p83.original: In Great Britain, the abuses which the trustees have committed in the management of those tolls, have, in many cases, been very justly complained of. At many turnpikes, it has been said, the money levied is more than double of what is necessary for executing, in the completest manner, the work, which is often executed in a very slovenly manner, and sometimes not executed at all. The system of repairing the high-roads by tolls of this kind, it must be observed, is not of very long standing. We should not wonder, therefore, if it has not yet been brought to that degree of perfection of which it seems capable. If mean and improper persons are frequently appointed trustees; and if proper courts of inspection and account have not yet been established for controlling their conduct, and for reducing the tolls to what is barely sufficient for executing the work to be done by them; the recency of the institution both accounts and apologizes for those defects, of which, by the wisdom of parliament, the greater part may, in due time, be gradually remedied.
p83.zh: 在大不列颠,受托人在管理这些通行费时所犯下的侵权行为,在许多情况下都受到非常公正的控诉。在许多回合中,有人说,征收的金钱是最完整地执行该作品所必须的两倍多,这种作品往往非常流利地执行,有时根本不执行.此类通行费修补高架道路的系统,必须加以遵守,这种修补系统不长期存在. 因此,我们不应怀疑它是否还没有达到它似乎能够达到的完美程度。 如果经常被任命为卑鄙和不适当的人;如果尚未设立适当的检查和会计法庭来控制他们的行为,并将费用减少到仅足以执行他们应完成的工作的水平;该机构是否正确进行核算并对这些缺陷道歉,而根据议会的智慧,大部分缺陷可能在适当时候逐步得到补救。

p84.original: The money levied at the different turnpikes in Great Britain, is supposed to exceed so much what is necessary for repairing the roads, that the savings which, with proper economy, might be made from it, have been considered, even by some ministers, as a very great resource, which might, at some time or another, be applied to the exigencies of the state. Government, it has been said, by taking the management of the turnpikes into its own hands, and by employing the soldiers, who would work for a very small addition to their pay, could keep the roads in good order, at a much less expense than it can be done by trustees, who have no other workmen to employ, but such as derive their whole subsistence from their wages. A great revenue, half a million, perhaps {Since publishing the two first editions of this book, I have got good reasons to believe that all the turnpike tolls levied in Great Britain do not produce a neat revenue that amounts to half a million; a sum which, under the management of government, would not be sufficient to keep, in repair five of the principal roads in the kingdom}, it has been pretended, might in this manner be gained, without laying any new burden upon the people; and the turnpike roads might be made to contribute to the general expense of the state, in the same manner as the post-office does at present.
p84.zh: 在大不列颠不同城市征收的钱,应该超过修路所必须的,以致于,即使一些大臣也认为,用适当经济方式可以节省下来的钱,是一种非常巨大的资源,在某个时候,这种资源可能应用于国家的紧急需要。 据说,政府把管理转折的事务交给自己处理,雇用士兵(他们的工作将增加他们微薄的薪水),就可以使道路保持良好秩序,费用比受托人少得多,因为受托人没有其他工人可以雇用,但从他们的工资中获得全部生计。 一个巨大的收入,50万,也许{自从出版这本书的两本第一版以来,我有充分的理由相信,在大不列颠征收的所有转帐费不能产生50万的整顿收入;在政府的管理下,这个数额不足以维持,修复王国的五条主要道路},它被假装得到,也许以这种方式获得,而不会给人民带来任何新的负担;转帐费公路可能被用来分担国家的一般费用,就像现在的后台一样。

p85.original: That a considerable revenue might be gained in this manner, I have no doubt, though probably not near so much as the projectors of this plan have supposed. The plan itself, however, seems liable to several very important objections.
p85.zh: 我毫不怀疑,这样可能获得可观的收入,尽管可能没有该计划的投影者所想象的那样接近。 然而,该计划本身似乎受到若干非常重要的反对。

p86.original: First, If the tolls which are levied at the turnpikes should ever be considered as one of the resources for supplying the exigencies of the state, they would certainly be augmented as those exigencies were supposed to require. According to the policy of Great Britain, therefore, they would probably he augmented very fast. The facility with which a great revenue could be drawn from them, would probably encourage administration to recur very frequently te this resource. Though it may, perhaps, be more than doubtful whether half a million could by any economy be saved out of the present tolls, it can scarcely be doubted, but that a million might be saved out of them, if they were doubled; and perhaps two millions, if they were tripled {I have now good reason to believe that all these conjectural sums are by much too large.}. This great revenue, too, might be levied without the appointment of a single new officer to collect and receive it. But the turnpike tolls, being continually augmented in this manner, instead of facilitating the inland commerce of the country, as at present, would soon become a very great incumbrance upon it. The expense of transporting all heavy goods from one part of the country to another, would soon be so much increased, the market for all such goods, consequently, would soon be so much narrowed, that their production would be in a great measure discouraged, and the most important branches of the domestic industry of the country annihilated altogether.
p86.zh: 首先,如果在转盘处收取的通行费被视为满足国家紧急需要的资源之一,它们肯定会像这些紧急需要那样增加。 因此,根据大不列颠的政策,他们很可能会迅速扩大。可从这些基金中获取大量收入的设施,可能鼓励行政部门经常利用这些资源。 虽然也许任何经济体能否从目前的死亡人数中节省50万是十分令人怀疑的,但几乎可以怀疑的是,如果这些损失翻了一番,就可能从中节省100万;如果这些损失翻了一番,也许就可能节省200万;也许还有200万,如果它们翻了三倍,{我现在有充分理由相信所有这些推测的金额都太大了。 }这笔巨额收入也可以在没有任命单一的新官员来收取和接收的情况下征收。 但是,以这种方式不断增加的转折费用,而不是象目前那样促进该国的内陆商业,将很快成为该国的一个重大因素。将所有重型货物从该国一个地区运往另一个地区的费用很快会大大增加,因此,所有这些货物的市场很快会大大缩小,以致其生产将受到很大程度的抑制,而且该国国内工业最重要的部门将完全被摧毁。

p87.original: Secondly, A tax upon carriages, in proportion to their weight, though a very equal tax when applied to the sole purpose of repairing the roads, is a very unequal one when applied to any other purpose, or to supply the common exigencies of the state. When it is applied to the sole purpose above mentioned, each carriage is supposed to pay exactly for the wear and tear which that carriage occasions of the roads. But when it is applied to any other purpose, each carriage is supposed to pay for more than that wear and tear, and contributes to the supply of some other exigency of the state. But as the turnpike toll raises the price of goods in proportion to their weight and not to their value, it is chiefly paid by the consumers of coarse and bulky, not by those of precious and light commodities. Whatever exigency of the state, therefore, this tax might be intended to supply, that exigency would be chiefly supplied at the expense of the poor, not of the rich; at the expense of those who are least able to supply it, not of those who are most able.
p87.zh: 第二,对马车的征税,按其重量的比例计算,虽然在适用于修复道路的唯一目的时,这种征税是十分平等的,但在适用于任何其他目的时,或用于提供国家的共同需要时,这种征税是十分不平等的。 当它适用于上述唯一目的时,每节车厢应支付公路运输时的磨损。 但当它被应用于任何其他目的时,每节车厢都应该支付超过该损耗的费用,并且有助于供应该州的一些其他紧急需要. 但是,随着转速客的收费按重量而不是按价值提高货物价格,主要由粗糙和大宗商品的消费者而不是由贵重和轻重商品的消费者支付。 因此,无论国家需要什么,这种税收可能是为了供应,这种需要主要是以穷人而不是富人为代价,而不是以那些最没有能力供应的人为代价,而不是以那些最有能力的人为代价。

p88.original: Thirdly, If government should at any time neglect the reparation of the high-roads, it would be still more difficult, than it is at present, to compel the proper application of any part of the turnpike tolls. A large revenue might thus be levied upon the people, without any part of it being applied to the only purpose to which a revenue levied in this manner ought ever to be applied. If the meanness and poverty of the trustees of turnpike roads render it sometimes difficult, at present, to oblige them to repair their wrong; their wealth and greatness would render it ten times more so in the case which is here supposed.
p88.zh: 第三,如果政府在任何时候都忽视对高路的赔偿,那么就比目前更难强制适当使用任何部分的转折通行费。 因此,可以向人民征收大笔收入,但其中任何部分都不适用于以这种方式征收的收入的唯一用途。 如果由于Tormpike公路受托人的苛刻和贫困,有时,目前很难迫使他们纠正错误;他们的财富和伟大将使它在此处理应发生的情况中增加十倍。

p89.original: In France, the funds destined for the reparation of the high-roads are under the immediate direction of the executive power. Those funds consist, partly in a certain number of days labour, which the country people are in most parts of Europe obliged to give to the reparation of the highways; and partly in such a portion of the general revenue of the state as the king chooses to spare from his other expenses.
p89.zh: 在法国,用于赔偿高铁的资金由行政权力直接指挥。这些资金部分包括一定天数的劳动,而在欧洲大部分地区,国家人民有义务给予公路补偿;部分包括国家一般收入的这一部分,因为国王选择免除其他开支。

p90.original: By the ancient law of France, as well as by that of most other parts of Europe, the labour of the country people was under the direction of a local or provincial magistracy, which had no immediate dependency upon the king's council. But, by the present practice, both the labour of the country people, and whatever other fund the king may choose to assign for the reparation of the high-roads in any particular province or generality, are entirely under the management of the intendant; an officer who is appointed and removed by the king's council who receives his orders from it, and is in constant correspondence with it. In the progress of despotism, the authority of the executive power gradually absorbs that of every other power in the state, and assumes to itself the management of every branch of revenue which is destined for any public purpose. In France, however, the great post-roads, the roads which make the communication between the principal towns of the kingdom, are in general kept in good order; and, in some provinces, are even a good deal superior to the greater part of the turnpike roads of England. But what we call the cross roads, that is, the far greater part of the roads in the country, are entirely neglected, and are in many places absolutely impassable for any heavy carriage. In some places it is even dangerous to travel on horseback, and mules are the only conveyance which can safely be trusted. The proud minister of an ostentatious court, may frequently take pleasure in executing a work of splendour and magnificence, such as a great highway, which is frequently seen by the principal nobility, whose applauses not only flatter his vanity, but even contribute to support his interest at court. But to execute a great number of little works, in which nothing that can be done can make any great appearance, or excite the smallest degree of admiration in any traveller, and which, in short, have nothing to recommend them but their extreme utility, is a business which appears, in every respect, too mean and paltry to merit the attention of so great a magistrate. Under such an administration therefore, such works are almost always entirely neglected.
p90.zh: 根据法国古代法律,以及欧洲大部分其他地区的法律,国家人民的劳动都由地方或省地方法官领导,而地方法官并不直接依赖国王的议会. 但是,根据目前的做法,无论是国家人民的劳动,还是国王可能选择的任何其他基金来分配用于任何特定省份或泛泛的要道的补偿,都完全由意图者管理;军官由国王的议会任命和罢免,接受他的命令,并与它保持经常的通信联系. 在专制的发展中,行政权力的权力逐渐吸收了州内所有其他权力的权力,并自行承担管理一切用于任何公共目的的收入分支. 然而,在法国,大后路,使王国主要城镇之间沟通的道路总体上保持了良好的秩序;在一些省份,甚至比英格兰大部的特恩皮克公路还优越. 但是,我们所称的十字路口,即国内道路的远大部分,是完全被忽视的,在很多地方绝对不能让任何重型车厢通行. 在有些地方骑马旅行甚至很危险,骡子是唯一可以安全信赖的运输工具. 一个显赫的宫廷的骄傲的大臣,可以经常乐于执行优雅壮丽的作品,如一条大公路,这经常被主要贵族所看到,他们的掌声不仅夸大了他的虚荣,甚至为支持他在宫廷的兴趣作出贡献. 但执行大量小作品,在其中,任何无法做到的事情都无法让任何伟大的外表,或者在任何旅行者中激发最小的钦佩程度,简言之,除了其极端的效用外,没有什么可以推荐的,这似乎是一件在每一个方面都显得太刻薄和微薄的生意,值得如此伟大的地方法官的注意. 因此,在这种管理之下,这类作品几乎总是被完全忽略。

p91.original: In China, and in several other governments of Asia, the executive power charges itself both with the reparation of the high-roads, and with the maintenance of the navigable canals. In the instructions which are given to the governor of each province, those objects, it is said, are constantly recommended to him, and the judgment which the court forms of his conduct is very much regulated by the attention which he appears to have paid to this part of his instructions. This branch of public police, accordingly, is said to be very much attended to in all those countries, but particularly in China, where the high-roads, and still more the navigable canals, it is pretended, exceed very much every thing of the same kind which is known in Europe. The accounts of those works, however, which have been transmitted to Europe, have generally been drawn up by weak and wondering travellers; frequently by stupid and lying missionaries. If they had been examined by more intelligent eyes, and if the accounts of them had been reported by more faithful witnesses, they would not, perhaps, appear to be so wonderful. The account which Bernier gives of some works of this kind in Indostan, falls very short of what had been reported of them by other travellers, more disposed to the marvellous than he was. It may too, perhaps, be in those countries, as it is in France, where the great roads, the great communications, which are likely to be the subjects of conversation at the court and in the capital, are attended to, and all the rest neglected. In China, besides, in Indostan, and in several other governments of Asia, the revenue of the sovereign arises almost altogether from a land tax or land rent, which rises or falls with the rise and fall of the annual produce of the land. The great interest of the sovereign, therefore, his revenue, is in such countries necessarily and immediately connected with the cultivation of the land, with the greatness of its produce, and with the value of its produce. But in order to render that produce both as great and as valuable as possible, it is necessary to procure to it as extensive a market as possible, and consequently to establish the freest, the easiest, and the least expensive communication between all the different parts of the country; which can be done only by means of the best roads and the best navigable canals. But the revenue of the sovereign does not, in any part of Europe, arise chiefly from a land tax or land rent. In all the great kingdoms of Europe, perhaps, the greater part of it may ultimately depend upon the produce of the land: but that dependency is neither so immediate nor so evident. In Europe, therefore, the sovereign does not feel himself so directly called upon to promote the increase, both in quantity and value of the produce of the land, or, by maintaining good roads and canals, to provide the most extensive market for that produce. Though it should be true, therefore, what I apprehend is not a little doubtful, that in some parts of Asia this department of the public police is very properly managed by the executive power, there is not the least probability that, during the present state of things, it could be tolerably managed by that power in any part of Europe.
p91.zh: 在中国,以及亚洲其他几个政府,行政权力本身既要赔偿高架路,又要维持通航运河. 据说,在向各省省长发出的指示中,不断向他推荐这些物品,法院对其行为形式所作的判决受到他似乎已注意的这一部分指示的很大制约。 因此,据说所有这些国家都非常关心这个公共警察部门,但特别是在中国,那里的道路很高,而且更多的是通航的运河,它被装扮成,远远超过了欧洲已知的每一样东西。 然而,这些作品被传送到欧洲,其叙述通常是由弱小和好奇的旅行者起草的;往往是由愚蠢和说谎的传教士撰写的。 如果被更聪明的目光所检查,如果他们的叙述被更忠实的目击证人报告,他们也许不会显得如此美妙.Bernier在印度对一些这类作品的叙述 与其它旅行者对之的报道相差甚远, 比他更喜欢神奇的作品。 也许,它也可能是在这些国家,就像在法国一样,那里有伟大的道路,伟大的通讯,很可能是法院和首都对话的主题,而其余的则被忽视。在中国,除了印度斯坦和亚洲其他几个政府,君主的收入几乎完全来自土地税或土地租金,随着土地年产的增减而上升或下降。 因此,主权者的极大利益,即他的收入,必然和这些国家直接地与土地的种植有关,与土地的丰盛,与土地的产值有关. 但是,为了使这种产品尽可能大,尽可能宝贵,必须采购一个尽可能广泛的市场,从而在全国所有不同地区之间建立最自由、最容易和最廉价的通信;这只能通过最佳道路和最佳通航运河来实现。 但是,在欧洲任何地区,君主的收入主要不是来自土地税或土地租金。在欧洲所有大王国中,也许它的大部分最终可能依赖于土地的产物:但是这种依赖性既不是那么直接,也不是那么明显. 因此,在欧洲,君主并不认为自己会直接要求促进土地产品数量和价值的增加,或者通过保持良好的道路和运河,为这些产品提供最广泛的市场。 因此,尽管我所发现的应该是事实,但并非有点可疑,在亚洲的一些地区,这个公共警察部门由行政权力管理得非常恰当,但在这个现状下,它在欧洲任何地区都能够被该权力所容忍地管理,这种可能性并非最小。

p92.original: Even those public works, which are of such a nature that they cannot afford any revenue for maintaining themselves, but of which the conveniency is nearly confined to some particular place or district, are always better maintained by a local or provincial revenue, under the management of a local and provincial administration, than by the general revenue of the state, of which the executive power must always have the management. Were the streets of London to be lighted and paved at the expense of the treasury, is there any probability that they would be so well lighted and paved as they are at present, or even at so small an expense? The expense, besides, instead of being raised by a local tax upon the inhabitants of each particular street, parish, or district in London, would, in this case, be defrayed out of the general revenue of the state, and would consequently be raised by a tax upon all the inhabitants of the kingdom, of whom the greater part derive no sort of benefit from the lighting and paving of the streets of London.
p92.zh: 即使是那些具有无法负担维持自己所需的任何收入,但租借权几乎局限于某个特定地方或地区性质的公共工程,也总是由地方或省级收入来维持,由地方和省级行政部门管理,而不是由国家的一般收入来维持,而行政权力必须始终由行政部门管理。 如果伦敦的街道被照亮和铺设费用以国库为代价,那么它们是否会像现在这样被照亮和铺设,或者即使花费这么小的费用? 此外,这笔费用不是由当地对伦敦每个街道、教区或区的居民征收的税费,而是由该州的一般收入支付,因此将由王国所有居民的税费支付,其中多数居民没有从伦敦街道的照明和铺设中获得任何好处。

p93.original: The abuses which sometimes creep into the local and provincial administration of a local and provincial revenue, how enormous soever they may appear, are in reality, however, almost always very trifling in comparison of those which commonly take place in the administration and expenditure of the revenue of a great empire. They are, besides, much more easily corrected. Under the local or provincial administration of the justices of the peace in Great Britain, the six days labour which the country people are obliged to give to the reparation of the highways, is not always, perhaps, very judiciously applied, but it is scarce ever exacted with any circumstance of cruelty or oppression. In France, under the administration of the intendants, the application is not always more judicious, and the exaction is frequently the most cruel and oppressive. Such corvees, as they are called, make one of the principal instruments of tyranny by which those officers chastise any parish or communeaute, which has had the misfortune to fall under their displeasure.
p93.zh: 地方和省政府有时会滥用地方和省财政收入,其数额可能如此之大,但实际上与一个大帝国的财政收入管理和开支通常相比,这些侵权行为几乎总是非常轻微。 此外,它们更容易得到纠正。 在大不列颠地方或省级治安官管理下,该国人民有义务为补偿高速公路而付出的六天劳动,可能并非总是非常明智地加以运用,但很少受到任何残酷或压迫的折磨。 在法国,在意图者的管理下,申请并不总是更明智,而且勒索往往是最残忍和最压迫性的。所谓的这种地牢,是那些军官惩罚任何教区或乡镇的主要暴政工具之一,他们不幸地陷入了他们的不满之中。

p94.original: Of the public Works and Institution which are necessary for facilitating particular Branches of Commerce.
p94.zh: 为促进特定商业部门所必需的公共工程和机构。

p95.original: The object of the public works and institutions above mentioned, is to facilitate commerce in general. But in order to facilitate some particular branches of it, particular institutions are necessary, which again require a particular and extraordinary expense.
p95.zh: 上述公共工程和机构的目标是促进一般商业。 但是,为了便利它的某些特定分支,需要特别的机构,这又需要特别和特别的开支。

p96.original: Some particular branches of commerce which are carried on with barbarous and uncivilized nations, require extraordinary protection. An ordinary store or counting-house could give little security to the goods of the merchants who trade to the western coast of Africa. To defend them from the barbarous natives, it is necessary that the place where they are deposited should be in some measure fortified. The disorders in the government of Indostan have been supposed to render a like precaution necessary, even among that mild and gentle people; and it was under pretence of securing their persons and property from violence, that both the English and French East India companies were allowed to erect the first forts which they possessed in that country. Among other nations, whose vigorous government will suffer no strangers to possess any fortified place within their territory, it may be necessary to maintain some ambassador, minister, or consul, who may both decide, according to their own customs, the differences arising among his own countrymen, and, in their disputes with the natives, may by means of his public character, interfere with more authority and afford them a more powerful protection than they could expect from any private man. The interests of commerce have frequently made it necessary to maintain ministers in foreign countries, where the purposes either of war or alliance would not have required any. The commerce of the Turkey company first occasioned the establishment of an ordinary ambassador at Constantinople. The first English embassies to Russia arose altogether from commercial interests. The constant interference with those interests, necessarily occasioned between the subjects of the different states of Europe, has probably introduced the custom of keeping, in all neighbouring countries, ambassadors or ministers constantly resident, even in the time of peace. This custom, unknown to ancient times, seems not to be older than the end of the fifteenth, or beginning of the sixteenth century; that is, than the time when commerce first began to extend itself to the greater part of the nations of Europe, and when they first began to attend to its interests.
p96.zh: 与野蛮和不文明国家一起从事的某些特定的商业分支需要特别的保护。普通商店或计票所对在非洲西海岸进行贸易的商人的商品没有多大保障。 为了保护他们免受野蛮的原住民的伤害,必须在一定程度上加强他们存放的地点。 印度斯坦政府内部的混乱本来是有必要采取类似预防措施的,即使是那些温和温和的人;而且正是在保护自己的人身和财产免遭暴力的幌子下,才允许英法东印度公司在该国建立它们拥有的第一个堡垒。 在另一些国家中,强有力的政府不会让陌生人在其领土上拥有任何强化的地盘,因此,可能有必要保留一些大使、部长或领事,他们可以根据自己的习俗,决定本国人之间的分歧,并在与土著人的争端中,通过他的公开性,干涉更多的权威,并给予他们比任何私人所期望的更强大的保护。商业利益常常使得有必要驻外使节,因为战争或结盟的目的不需要任何。 土耳其公司的商业首次在君士坦丁堡设立普通大使.英国驻俄罗斯的第一批大使馆完全源于商业利益。 欧洲不同国家的臣民之间必然不断干涉这些利益,这很可能在所有邻国,甚至在和平时期,都引入了保持大使或部长常住的习惯。 这种古老的习俗,似乎并不比十五世纪末,或十六世纪初更古老;即比起商代开始向欧洲大部分国家延伸,以及商代开始关心商代的利益的时候.

p97.original: It seems not unreasonable, that the extraordinary expense which the protection of any particular branch of commerce may occasion, should be defrayed by a moderate tax upon that particular branch; by a moderate fine, for example, to be paid by the traders when they first enter into it; or, what is more equal, by a particular duty of so much per cent. upon the goods which they either import into, or export out of, the particular countries with which it is carried on. The protection of trade, in general, from pirates and freebooters, is said to have given occasion to the first institution of the duties of customs. But, if it was thought reasonable to lay a general tax upon trade, in order to defray the expense of protecting trade in general, it should seem equally reasonable to lay a particular tax upon a particular branch of trade, in order to defray the extraordinary expense of protecting that branch.
p97.zh: 保护任何特定商业分支可能发生的特别费用,应当由该特定分支的温和税收支付;例如,贸易商在首次进入该分支时缴纳中等程度的罚款;或者,更为平等的是,由它们进出口其所属的特定国家的货物承担如此大的比例的特殊责任,这似乎并非不合理。 据说,一般保护贸易不受海盗和自由开业者之害,是第一个关税制度的机会。 但是,如果认为对贸易规定一般税是合理的,为了支付一般保护贸易的费用,那么,对某一贸易分支规定某种税似乎同样是合理的,以便支付保护该分支的特别费用。

p98.original: The protection of trade, in general, has always been considered as essential to the defence of the commonwealth, and, upon that account, a necessary part of the duty of the executive power. The collection and application of the general duties of customs, therefore, have always been left to that power. But the protection of any particular branch of trade is a part of the general protection of trade; a part, therefore, of the duty of that power; and if nations always acted consistently, the particular duties levied for the purposes of such particular protection, should always have been left equally to its disposal. But in this respect, as well as in many others, nations have not always acted consistently; and in the greater part of the commercial states of Europe, particular companies of merchants have had the address to persuade the legislature to entrust to them the performance of this part of the duty of the sovereign, together with all the powers which are necessarily connected with it.
p98.zh: 一般来说,保护贸易一直被认为是捍卫联邦的关键,因此也是行政权力责任的必要部分。 因此,海关一般关税的征收和适用一直由这一权力来决定。 但是,对任何特定贸易分支的保护是一般贸易保护的一部分;因此,是该大国义务的一部分;如果各国始终采取一致行动,为这种特定保护的目的征收的特定义务就应当永远由它同等地支配。 但在这方面,以及在许多其他国家,各国并非始终一贯地采取行动;在欧洲大部分商业国家,某些商业公司曾有地址劝说立法机构委托它们履行主权者的部分义务,以及与之相关的所有权力。

p99.original: These companies, though they may, perhaps, have been useful for the first introduction of some branches of commerce, by making, at their own expense, an experiment which the state might not think it prudent to make, have in the long-run proved, universally, either burdensome or useless, and have either mismanaged or confined the trade.
p99.zh: 这些公司虽然也许对首次引进一些商业分支有用,但自费进行国家可能认为不审慎的试验,从长远来看,这些试验被普遍证明是繁琐的或无用的,或者管理不当,或者限制贸易。

p100.original: When those companies do not trade upon a joint stock, but are obliged to admit any person, properly qualified, upon paying a certain fine, and agreeing to submit to the regulations of the company, each member trading upon his own stock, and at his own risk, they are called regulated companies. When they trade upon a joint stock, each member sharing in the common profit or loss, in proportion to his share in this stock, they are called joint-stock companies. Such companies, whether regulated or joint-stock, sometimes have, and sometimes have not, exclusive privileges.
p100.zh: 当这些公司不以股份交易,而有义务在支付一定的罚款并同意服从公司规章后,接纳任何符合适当资格的人时,每个成员以自己的股票交易,冒着自己的风险,则称为受监管公司。 当他们以股份交易时,每个成员按照他在股份中的份额分享共同的利润或损失,它们被称为股份公司. 这类公司,无论是受监管公司还是股份公司,有时拥有、有时没有专属特权。

p101.original: Regulated companies resemble, in every respect, the corporation of trades, so common in the cities and towns of all the different countries of Europe; and are a sort of enlarged monopolies of the same kind. As no inhabitant of a town can exercise an incorporated trade, without first obtaining his freedom in the incorporation, so, in most cases, no subject of the state can lawfully carry on any branch of foreign trade, for which a regulated company is established, without first becoming a member of that company. The monopoly is more or less strict, according as the terms of admission are more or less difficult, and according as the directors of the company have more or less authority, or have it more or less in their power to manage in such a manner as to confine the greater part of the trade to themselves and their particular friends. In the most ancient regulated companies, the privileges of apprenticeship were the same as in other corporations, and entitled the person who had served his time to a member of the company, to become himself a member, either without paying any fine, or upon paying a much smaller one than what was exacted of other people. The usual corporation spirit, wherever the law does not restrain it, prevails in all regulated companies. When they have been allowed to act according to their natural genius, they have always, in order to confine the competition to as small a number of persons as possible, endeavoured to subject the trade to many burdensome regulations. When the law has restrained them from doing this, they have become altogether useless and insignificant.
p101.zh: 受监管的公司在各个方面都类似于贸易公司,在欧洲所有不同国家的城市和城镇中如此常见;它们是一种扩大的同类垄断。 由于一个城镇的居民不能从事公司贸易,而不能首先在公司注册中获得自由,因此,在大多数情况下,国家任何主体都不能合法地从事任何外贸部门,而为外贸部门设立了受管制的公司,而不能首先成为该公司的成员。垄断或多或少是严格,因为准入条件或多或少是困难的,而且公司董事们或多或少有权威,或或多或少有权力管理,以致将贸易的较大部分限制在自己和他们特定的朋友身上. 在最古老的受管制公司中,学徒的特权与其他公司相同,使服务时间的人有资格成为公司成员,要么不交任何罚款,要么在支付比其他人要少得多的罚款时成为成员。通常的公司精神,无论法律如何不加以约束,在所有受监管的公司中都占上风。 当他们被允许按照他们的天赋行事时,他们总是为了把竞争限制在尽可能少的人之内,努力使贸易受到许多繁琐的管制。 当法律禁止他们这样做时,他们就变得毫无用处和无足轻重。

p102.original: The regulated companies for foreign commerce which at present subsist in Great Britain, are the ancient merchant-adventurers company, now commonly called the Hamburgh company, the Russia company, the Eastland company, the Turkey company, and the African company.
p102.zh: 目前存在于大不列颠的受管制的外国商业公司是古老的商家-冒险公司,现在通常称为汉堡公司、俄罗斯公司、东兰公司、土耳其公司和非洲公司。

p103.original: The terms of admission into the Hamburgh company are now said to be quite easy; and the directors either have it not in their power to subject the trade to any troublesome restraint or regulations, or, at least, have not of late exercised that power. It has not always been so. About the middle of the last century, the fine for admission was fifty, and at one time one hundred pounds, and the conduct of the company was said to be extremely oppressive. In 1643, in 1645, and in 1661, the clothiers and free traders of the west of England complained of them to parliament, as of monopolists, who confined the trade, and oppressed the manufactures of the country. Though those complaints produced no act of parliament, they had probably intimidated the company so far, as to oblige them to reform their conduct. Since that time, at least, there have been no complaints against them. By the 10th and 11th of William III. c.6, the fine for admission into the Russia company was reduced to five pounds; and by the 25th of Charles II. c.7, that for admission into the Eastland company to forty shillings; while, at the same time, Sweden, Denmark, and Norway, all the countries on the north side of the Baltic, were exempted from their exclusive charter. The conduct of those companies had probably given occasion to those two acts of parliament. Before that time, Sir Josiah Child had represented both these and the Hamburgh company as extremely oppressive, and imputed to their bad management the low state of the trade, which we at that time carried on to the countries comprehended within their respective charters. But though such companies may not, in the present times, be very oppressive, they are certainly altogether useless. To be merely useless, indeed, is perhaps, the highest eulogy which can ever justly be bestowed upon a regulated company; and all the three companies above mentioned seem, in their present state, to deserve this eulogy.
p103.zh: 据说,汉堡公司的入股条件现在相当容易;董事们要么没有权力对贸易进行任何麻烦的制约或管制,要么至少没有迟到行使这种权力。情况并非总是如此。大约在上世纪中叶,录取罚款为50元,一度为100磅,据说公司的行为极具压迫性.1643年,1645年,以及1661年,英格兰西部的布衣商和自由商人向议会抱怨,就像垄断者一样,他们限制了贸易,压迫了国家的制造. 虽然这些投诉没有引起议会的行动,但迄今为止,他们可能已经恐吓该公司,迫使他们改革行为。 从那时起,至少没有人对他们提出过任何申诉。至威廉三世c.6的第十和十一,进入俄罗斯公司的罚款减为五磅;至查理二世c.7的二十五,进入东兰公司时的罚款减为四十先令;同时,波罗的海北岸的瑞典,丹麦,挪威等国家均免予其专属特许. 这些公司的行为可能为议会的这两项法案提供了机会。在此之前,约西亚·克莱德爵士曾代表这些公司和汉堡公司极具压迫性,并指责他们管理不良,即当时我们一直把贸易的低水平归咎于各国,而这些国家在各自的章程中都理解了这一点。 但是,尽管在当今时代,这类公司可能不是非常压迫性的,但它们当然是完全无用的。仅仅是无用,事实上,也许,这是可以公正地授予受监管公司的最高悼词;上述所有三家公司,在目前的状况下,似乎都值得这一悼词。

p104.original: The fine for admission into the Turkey company was formerly twenty-five pounds for all persons under twenty-six years of age, and fifty pounds for all persons above that age. Nobody but mere merchants could be admitted; a restriction which excluded all shop-keepers and retailers. By a bye-law, no British manufactures could be exported to Turkey but in the general ships of the company; and as those ships sailed always from the port of London, this restriction confined the trade to that expensive port, and the traders to those who lived in London and in its neighbourhood. By another bye-law, no person living within twenty miles of London, and not free of the city, could be admitted a member; another restriction which, joined to the foregoing, necessarily excluded all but the freemen of London. As the time for the loading and sailing of those general ships depended altogether upon the directors, they could easily fill them with their own goods, and those of their particular friends, to the exclusion of others, who, they might pretend, had made their proposals too late. In this state of things, therefore, this company was, in every respect, a strict and oppressive monopoly. Those abuses gave occasion to the act of the 26th of George II. c. 18, reducing the fine for admission to twenty pounds for all persons, without any distinction of ages, or any restriction, either to mere merchants, or to the freemen of London; and granting to all such persons the liberty of exporting, from all the ports of Great Britain, to any port in Turkey, all British goods, of which the exportation was not prohibited, upon paying both the general duties of customs, and the particular duties assessed for defraying the necessary expenses of the company; and submitting, at the same time, to the lawful authority of the British ambassador and consuls resident in Turkey, and to the bye-laws of the company duly enacted. To prevent any oppression by those bye-laws, it was by the same act ordained, that if any seven members of the company conceived themselves aggrieved by any bye-law which should be enacted after the passing of this act, they might appeal to the board of trade and plantations (to the authority of which a committee of the privy council has now succeeded), provided such appeal was brought within twelve months after the bye-law was enacted; and that, if any seven members conceived themselves aggrieved by any bye-law which had been enacted before the passing of this act, they might bring a like appeal, provided it was within twelve months after the day on which this act was to take place. The experience of one year, however, may not always be sufficient to discover to all the members of a great company the pernicious tendency of a particular bye-law; and if several of them should afterwards discover it, neither the board of trade, nor the committee of council, can afford them any redress. The object, besides, of the greater part of the bye-laws of all regulated companies, as well as of all other corporations, is not so much to oppress those who are already members, as to discourage others from becoming so; which may be done, not only by a high fine, but by many other contrivances. The constant view of such companies is always to raise the rate of their own profit as high as they can; to keep the market, both for the goods which they export, and for those which they import, as much understocked as they can; which can be done only by restraining the competition, or by discouraging new adventurers from entering into the trade. A fine, even of twenty pounds, besides, though it may not, perhaps, be sufficient to discourage any man from entering into the Turkey trade, with an intention to continue in it, may be enough to discourage a speculative merchant from hazarding a single adventure in it. In all trades, the regular established traders, even though not incorporated, naturally combine to raise profits, which are noway so likely to be kept, at all times, down to their proper level, as by the occasional competition of speculative adventurers. The Turkey trade, though in some measure laid open by this act of parliament, is still considered by many people as very far from being altogether free. The Turkey company contribute to maintain an ambassador and two or three consuls, who, like other public ministers, ought to be maintained altogether by the state, and the trade laid open to all his majesty's subjects. The different taxes levied by the company, for this and other corporation purposes, might afford a revenue much more than sufficient to enable a state to maintain such ministers.
p104.zh: 进入土耳其公司的罚款原先是对所有26岁以下的人25磅,对超过该年龄的人50磅。 只有商人才能被接纳;这种限制排除了所有店主和零售商。 根据一项细则,英国的制成品不能出口到土耳其,但只能出口到该公司的普通船只;而且由于这些船只总是从伦敦港航行,这种限制将贸易限制在昂贵的港口,贸易商则限制在伦敦及其附近居住的人。 根据另一条细则,住在伦敦二十英里以内、不能离开该市的人都不能被接纳为成员;另外一项限制,加上上述限制,必然排除伦敦自由人以外的所有人。 由于这些普通船舶的装船和航行时间完全取决于船长,他们可以很容易地把自己的货物和他们特定朋友的货物装满,而把其他人排除在外,他们可能假装提出他们的建议为时已晚。 因此,在目前这种情况下,这家公司在各个方面都是严格和压迫性的垄断。 这些侵权行为使乔治二世的26日行动成为可能。18,对所有人,不分年龄,或对商人,或对伦敦自由人,将入境罚款减为20英镑;给予所有这类人从大不列颠所有港口出口土耳其任何港口的所有不禁止出口的英国货物,同时支付海关的一般关税和为支付公司必要的费用而评估的特定关税;同时,向驻土耳其的英国大使和领事的合法权威以及公司正式颁布的章程提交。 为了防止这些细则受到任何压迫,根据同一法令,如果公司的任何七名成员在通过任何细则后产生受到任何细则侵害的情况,他们可以向贸易和种植园委员会(现在由一个初级理事会委员会继承其权力)提出上诉,条件是这种上诉是在细则颁布后十二个月内提出的;如果任何七名成员在通过本法之前颁布的任何细则法下产生,他们可以提出类似的上诉,条件是在本法颁布之日起十二个月内提出。 然而,一年的经验可能并不总是足以使大公司的所有成员都发现某项具体细则的有害倾向;如果其中若干成员事后发现这种倾向,贸易委员会和理事会委员会都无法为他们提供任何补救。 此外,所有受监管公司以及所有其他公司的大部分章程的目的不是压迫那些已经是成员的人,而是劝阻其他人不要成为成员;这样做不仅可以通过高额罚款,而且可以通过许多其他办法。此类公司的一贯观点总是尽可能提高自身利润率;保持市场,无论是对其出口的商品,还是对其进口的商品,都尽可能少地储存;这只能通过限制竞争,或者通过阻止新的冒险者进入贸易来实现. 此外,罚款,甚至20磅,虽然可能不足以阻止任何人进入土耳其贸易,并打算继续,但可能足以阻止投机商人破坏土耳其的一次冒险。在所有行业中,正规的已建立的贸易商即使没有并入,也自然地结合起来筹集利润,这些利润在任何时候都不可能一直保持在适当的水平上,就像投机冒险家偶尔的竞争那样. 土耳其的贸易尽管在某种程度上是由议会的这一法案所开放的,但许多人仍然认为,这种贸易远远没有完全自由。 土耳其公司出资维持一名大使和二至三名领事,他们和其他公共部长一样,应该完全由国家维持,贸易对所有陛下的臣民开放。公司为此和其他公司目的征收的不同税种,可能使国家能够维持这些部长的收入远远超出这一数额。

p105.original: Regulated companies, it was observed by Sir Josiah Child, though they had frequently supported public ministers, had never maintained any forts or garrisons in the countries to which they traded; whereas joint-stock companies frequently had. And, in reality, the former seem to be much more unfit for this sort of service than the latter. First, the directors of a regulated company have no particular interest in the prosperity of the general trade of the company, for the sake of which such forts and garrisons are maintained. The decay of that general trade may even frequently contribute to the advantage of their own private trade; as, by diminishing the number of their competitors, it may enable them both to buy cheaper, and to sell dearer. The directors of a joint-stock company, on the contrary, having only their share in the profits which are made upon the common stock committed to their management, have no private trade of their own, of which the interest can be separated from that of the general trade of the company. Their private interest is connected with the prosperity of the general trade of the company, and with the maintenance of the forts and garrisons which are necessary for its defence. They are more likely, therefore, to have that continual and careful attention which that maintenance necessarily requires. Secondly, The directors of a joint-stock company have always the management of a large capital, the joint stock of the company, a part of which they may frequently employ, with propriety, in building, repairing, and maintaining such necessary forts and garrisons. But the directors of a regulated company, having the management of no common capital, have no other fund to employ in this way, but the casual revenue arising from the admission fines, and from the corporation duties imposed upon the trade of the company. Though they had the same interest, therefore, to attend to the maintenance of such forts and garrisons, they can seldom have the same ability to render that attention effectual. The maintenance of a public minister, requiring scarce any attention, and but a moderate and limited expense, is a business much more suitable both to the temper and abilities of a regulated company.
p105.zh: Josiah Child爵士指出,受管制的公司虽然经常支持公共部长,但从未在它们交易的国家维持任何要塞或驻防点;而股份公司经常有。 而实际上,前者似乎比后者更不适合这种服务. 第一,受管制公司的董事对公司一般贸易的繁荣没有特殊的利益,为了维持这种要塞和驻防. 这种一般贸易的衰败甚至可能经常助长它们自己的私人贸易的优势;因为通过减少竞争者的数量,它们既可以购买更便宜的产品,又可以出售较贵的产品。 相反,股份公司的董事在共同股票的利润中只占有其份额,而承诺管理的共同股票上却没有自己的私人交易,其中的利益可以与公司的一般交易分开。 他们的私人利益与公司一般贸易的繁荣有关,也与维护其防卫所必需的要塞和驻防地有关. 因此,它们更有可能得到这种维持工作所必然需要的持续和认真的注意。 第二,股份公司的董事总是管理着一个大型资本,即公司的股份,他们可以经常在适当的情况下使用其中的一部分来建造、修理和维持这种必要的堡垒和驻防地。 但是,受管制公司的董事们没有共同资本的管理,没有其他基金可以以这种方式雇用,而只是因入股罚款和公司对公司贸易征收的公司税而产生的临时收入。 因此,尽管它们同样关心维护这些要塞和驻防地,但它们很少能够使这种注意产生效果。维持一个需要很少注意的公使,但开支是适度的和有限的,这种业务对于受管制公司的脾气和能力都更为合适。

p106.original: Long after the time of Sir Josiah Child, however, in 1750, a regulated company was established, the present company of merchants trading to Africa; which was expressly charged at first with the maintenance of all the British forts and garrisons that lie between Cape Blanc and the Cape of Good Hope, and afterwards with that of those only which lie between Cape Rouge and the Cape of Good Hope. The act which establishes this company (the 23rd of George II. c.51 ), seems to have had two distinct objects in view; first, to restrain effectually the oppressive and monopolizing spirit which is natural to the directors of a regulated company; and, secondly, to force them, as much as possible, to give an attention, which is not natural to them, towards the maintenance of forts and garrisons.
p106.zh: 然而在约西亚·柴尔德爵士时期很久后,1750年,成立了一家受管制的公司,即现在的向非洲贸易的商家公司;起初明确负责维护位于布兰卡角和好望角之间的所有英国要塞和驻军,后来又负责维护仅位于红角和好望角之间的那些要塞和驻军.建立这家公司的法案(George II.c.51第23条)看来有两个不同的目标;第一,有效地约束受管制公司的董事们自然而然的压迫和垄断精神;第二,尽可能迫使他们注意维持堡垒和驻防地,这对他们来说不是自然的。

p107.original: For the first of these purposes, the fine for admission is limited to forty shillings. The company is prohibited from trading in their corporate capacity, or upon a joint stock; from borrowing money upon common seal, or from laying any restraints upon the trade, which may be carried on freely from all places, and by all persons being British subjects, and paying the fine. The government is in a committee of nine persons, who meet at London, but who are chosen annually by the freemen of the company at London, Bristol, and Liverpool; three from each place. No committeeman can be continued in office for more than three years together. Any committee-man might be removed by the board of trade and plantations, now by a committee of council, after being heard in his own defence. The committee are forbid to export negroes from Africa, or to import any African goods into Great Britain. But as they are charged with the maintenance of forts and garrisons, they may, for that purpose export from Great Britain to Africa goods and stores of different kinds. Out of the moneys which they shall receive from the company, they are allowed a sum, not exceeding eight hundred pounds, for the salaries of their clerks and agents at London, Bristol, and Liverpool, the house-rent of their offices at London, and all other expenses of management, commission, and agency, in England. What remains of this sum, after defraying these different expenses, they may divide among themselves, as compensation for their trouble, in what manner they think proper. By this constitution, it might have been expected, that the spirit of monopoly would have been effectually restrained, and the first of these purposes sufficiently answered. It would seem, however, that it had not. Though by the 4th of George III. c.20, the fort of Senegal, with all its dependencies, had been invested in the company of merchants trading to Africa, yet, in the year following (by the 5th of George III. c.44), not only Senegal and its dependencies, but the whole coast, from the port of Sallee, in South Barbary, to Cape Rouge, was exempted from the jurisdiction of that company, was vested in the crown, and the trade to it declared free to all his majesty's subjects. The company had been suspected of restraining the trade and of establishing some sort of improper monopoly. It is not, however, very easy to conceive how, under the regulations of the 23d George II. they could do so. In the printed debates of the house of commons, not always the most authentic records of truth, I observe, however, that they have been accused of this. The members of the committee of nine being all merchants, and the governors and factors in their different forts and settlements being all dependent upon them, it is not unlikely that the latter might have given peculiar attention to the consignments and commissions of the former, which would establish a real monopoly.
p107.zh: 就其中第一项目的而言,入境罚款限于40先令。禁止公司以公司能力进行交易或以股份进行交易;禁止以共同的印章借款,或禁止对交易施加任何限制,因为交易可以自由从任何地方和所有英国国民进行,并支付罚款。 政府由9人组成委员会,他们在伦敦开会,但每年由伦敦,布里斯托尔和利物浦公司的自由人选出;每个地方3人.任何委员不得继续任职三年以上。任何委员会人员在为自己辩护后,都可能被贸易和种植园委员会,即现在的议会委员会罢免。 委员会禁止从非洲出口黑人,或向大不列颠进口任何非洲货物。 但是,由于它们负责维持要塞和驻军,它们可以为此目的从大不列颠向非洲出口各种货物和储存。 他们从公司得到的钱中,有一笔不超过800磅的款项,用于支付在伦敦、布里斯托尔和利物浦的职员和代理人的工资,以及他们在伦敦的办公室的房租,还有他们在英国的管理、佣金和代理等所有其他费用。 在支付这些不同的开支之后,他们可能彼此间分裂,作为对他们的麻烦的补偿,以何种方式认为适当。 根据这部宪法,人们可能预料垄断精神本来会受到实际限制,而其中的第一个目的已经得到充分的响应。 然而,似乎没有。 虽然到乔治三世c.20的第四世时,塞内加尔的堡垒及其所有附属地都投资给向非洲贸易的商人公司,但是在次年(乔治三世c.44的第五世时),不仅塞内加尔及其附属地,而且从南巴巴里的萨尔利港到红角的整个海岸都免除了该公司的管辖,其贸易权被授予王冠,并且宣布其所有皇帝臣民均可自由交易。该公司被怀疑限制贸易,并建立了某种不正当的垄断。 然而,很难想象,根据23d George II的规定,他们如何能够做到这一点。 然而,在普通人院的印刷辩论中,我注意到,他们被指控犯有这些罪行,但并不总是最真实的真实记录。 九人委员会的成员都是商人,总督和他们不同的堡垒和定居点中的因素都依赖他们,因此,他们不可能对前者的托运货物和佣金给予特殊注意,因为前者将确立真正的垄断地位。

p108.original: For the second of these purposes, the maintenance of the forts and garrisons, an annual sum has been allotted to them by parliament, generally about £13,000. For the proper application of this sum, the committee is obliged to account annually to the cursitor baron of exchequer; which account is afterwards to be laid before parliament. But parliament, which gives so little attention to the application of millions, is not likely to give much to that of £13,000 a-year; and the cursitor baron of exchequer, from his profession and education, is not likely to be profoundly skilled in the proper expense of forts and garrisons. The captains of his majesty's navy, indeed, or any other commissioned officers, appointed by the board of admiralty, may inquire into the condition of the forts and garrisons, and report their observations to that board. But that board seems to have no direct jurisdiction over the committee, nor any authority to correct those whose conduct it may thus inquire into; and the captains of his majesty's navy, besides, are not supposed to be always deeply learned in the science of fortification. Removal from an office, which can be enjoyed only for the term of three years, and of which the lawful emoluments, even during that term, are so very small, seems to be the utmost punishment to which any committee-man is liable, for any fault, except direct malversation, or embezzlement, either of the public money, or of that of the company; and the fear of the punishment can never be a motive of sufficient weight to force a continual and careful attention to a business to which he has no other interest to attend. The committee are accused of having sent out bricks and stones from England for the reparation of Cape Coast Castle, on the coast of Guinea; a business for which parliament had several times granted an extraordinary sum of money. These bricks and stones, too, which had thus been sent upon so long a voyage, were said to have been of so bad a quality, that it was necessary to rebuild, from the foundation, the walls which had been repaired with them. The forts and garrisons which lie north of Cape Rouge, are not only maintained at the expense of the state, but are under the immediate government of the executive power; and why those which lie south of that cape, and which, too, are, in part at least, maintained at the expense of the state, should be under a different government, it seems not very easy even to imagine a good reason. The protection of the Mediterranean trade was the original purpose or pretence of the garrisons of Gibraltar and Minorca; and the maintenance and government of those garrisons have always been, very properly, committed, not to the Turkey company, but to the executive power. In the extent of its dominion consists, in a great measure, the pride and dignity of that power; and it is not very likely to fail in attention to what is necessary for the defence of that dominion. The garrisons at Gibraltar and Minorca, accordingly, have never been neglected. Though Minorca has been twice taken, and is now probably lost for ever, that disaster has never been imputed to any neglect in the executive power. I would not, however, be understood to insinuate, that either of those expensive garrisons was ever, even in the smallest degree, necessary for the purpose for which they were originally dismembered from the Spanish monarchy. That dismemberment, perhaps, never served any other real purpose than to alienate from England her natural ally the king of Spain, and to unite the two principal branches of the house of Bourbon in a much stricter and more permanent alliance than the ties of blood could ever have united them.
p108.zh: 其中第二个用途是维持堡垒和卫戍区,议会每年拨给它们一笔款项,一般约为13 000英镑。 为了适当使用这笔金额,委员会必须每年向国库典狱长负责;此后,该笔账将提交议会。 但议会如此不重视数百万的应用,不太可能给每年13000英镑的应用多少;而典狱长从他的专业和教育上来说,他不太可能在堡垒和驻军的适当开支方面有很深的技能.陛下海军的舰长,实际上,或海军上将委员会任命的任何其他受命军官,可以调查要塞和驻防区的状况,并向该委员会报告其意见。 但是,该委员会似乎对委员会没有直接管辖权,也没有任何权力纠正委员会可能因此调查的行为;此外,他的海军上尉不应该总是深入了解防御科学。被免职,只能享受3年任期,而合法薪酬,即使在这一任期中,也极小,似乎是任何委员会人员对任何过失应负的最大惩罚,但直接渎职或挪用公款或公司公款除外;对惩罚的恐惧永远不能成为迫使他继续认真关注一个他没有其他兴趣的企业的动机。 委员会被指控从英国运出砖块和石块,用于赔偿几内亚海岸的海岸角城堡;议会已多次为这一事业提供一笔特别的金额。 这些砖块和石头也因此被送去了如此长的航程,据说质量太差,必须从地基上重建用它们修补的城墙。位于红角以北的要塞和驻防区,不仅以州为代价维持,还处于行政权的直属政府之下;以及为什么那些位于披风以南,而且至少以州为代价维持的部分要塞和驻防区,都应该在不同的政府之下,这似乎甚至不易想象出一个好的理由.保护地中海贸易是直布罗陀和米雷卡驻军的最初目的或借口;这些驻军的维持和政府一直非常适当地致力于不是土耳其连,而是行政权力。就其统治范围而言,在很大程度上,它代表着该政权的自豪和尊严;它不会忽视捍卫该统治所必需的条件。 因此,直布罗陀和米雷卡的驻军从未受到忽视。 虽然Minica曾两次被带走,现在可能永远丢失,但这一灾难从未被归咎于行政权力中的任何忽视。 然而,我并不理解影射,这些昂贵的驻军中,有的甚至从最小程度来说,对于他们最初从西班牙君主制中分裂出来的目的来说,都是必要的。割裂也许除了疏远她与英国的天然盟友西班牙国王之外,别无其他真正目的,并且将波旁家族的两大分支团结起来,结成比血缘关系更严格、更永久的联盟。

p109.original: Joint-stock companies, established either by royal charter, or by act of parliament, are different in several respects, not only from regulated companies, but from private copartneries.
p109.zh: 根据皇家章程或议会法案设立的股份公司在几个方面不同,不仅与受管制的公司不同,而且与私营合伙企业也不同。

p110.original: First, In a private copartnery, no partner without the consent of the company, can transfer his share to another person, or introduce a new member into the company. Each member, however, may, upon proper warning, withdraw from the copartnery, and demand payment from them of his share of the common stock. In a joint-stock company, on the contrary, no member can demand payment of his share from the company; but each member can, without their consent, transfer his share to another person, and thereby introduce a new member. The value of a share in a joint stock is always the price which it will bring in the market; and this may be either greater or less in any proportion, than the sum which its owner stands credited for in the stock of the company.
p110.zh: 一,在私人合伙企业中,未经公司同意,任何合伙人不得将自己的股份转让给他人,或者将新成员引进公司. 但是,每个成员在接到适当警告后,可以退出合伙企业,要求他们支付其在共同股票中的份额。在一个股份制公司,相反,任何成员都不得要求公司支付其股份;但是,每个成员可以不经同意将其股份转让给另一个人,从而引入一个新的成员.股份股的价值始终是它将带入市场的价格;这比其所有者在公司股票中所占的金额大或小。

p111.original: Secondly, In a private copartnery, each partner is bound for the debts contracted by the company, to the whole extent of his fortune. In a joint-stock company, on the contrary, each partner is bound only to the extent of his share.
p111.zh: 第二,在一个私人合伙企业中,每个合伙人都有义务承担公司所订约的债务,以他的全部财富为限。 相反,在一个股份公司中,每个合伙人只受其股份范围内的约束。

p112.original: The trade of a joint-stock company is always managed by a court of directors. This court, indeed, is frequently subject, in many respects, to the control of a general court of proprietors. But the greater part of these proprietors seldom pretend to understand any thing of the business of the company; and when the spirit of faction happens not to prevail among them, give themselves no trouble about it, but receive contentedly such halfyearly or yearly dividend as the directors think proper to make to them. This total exemption front trouble and front risk, beyond a limited sum, encourages many people to become adventurers in joint-stock companies, who would, upon no account, hazard their fortunes in any private copartnery. Such companies, therefore, commonly draw to themselves much greater stocks, than any private copartnery can boast of. The trading stock of the South Sea company at one time amounted to upwards of thirty-three millions eight hundred thousand pounds. The divided capital of the Bank of England amounts, at present, to ten millions seven hundred and eighty thousand pounds. The directors of such companies, however, being the managers rather of other people's money than of their own, it cannot well be expected that they should watch over it with the same anxious vigilance with which the partners in a private copartnery frequently watch over their own. Like the stewards of a rich man, they are apt to consider attention to small matters as not for their master's honour, and very easily give themselves a dispensation from having it. Negligence and profusion, therefore, must always prevail, more or less, in the management of the affairs of such a company. It is upon this account, that joint-stock companies for foreign trade have seldom been able to maintain the competition against private adventurers. They have, accordingly, very seldom succeeded without an exclusive privilege; and frequently have not succeeded with one. Without an exclusive privilege, they have commonly mismanaged the trade. With an exclusive privilege, they have both mismanaged and confined it.
p112.zh: 股份制公司的贸易始终由董事法院管理. 实际上,在许多方面,该法院常常受到一般业主法院的控制。 但是,这些业主中的大部分人很少假装了解公司的任何业务;当派系精神恰好不能在他们中间占上风时,不要给自己惹麻烦,而是在半年或每年得到董事们认为适当的红利。 这种完全免责的前方麻烦和前方风险,除了有限的金额外,鼓励许多人成为股份公司的冒险者,他们不会在任何私人合伙企业中危及他们的财富。 因此,这些公司通常比任何私人合伙企业所声称的要多得多的股票。南海公司一次交易股票高达33万80万斤以上. 目前,英格兰银行的资本分割为1千万780万英镑。 然而,这些公司的董事是他人的钱而不是自己的钱的管理者,不能指望他们以私人合伙企业的伙伴们经常注意的同样焦急的警惕来监督这些钱。和有钱人的管家一样,他们很适合考虑对小事的关注,而不是为了主人的荣誉,而且很容易让自己摆脱这种关注。 因此,在管理这种公司事务方面,必须多少总是占上风。 正是出于这一考虑,外贸股份公司很少能够维持对私人冒险者的竞争。 因此,他们很少在没有专属特权的情况下取得成功;而且常常没有以这种特权取得成功。 没有专属特权,他们通常对贸易管理不当。 他们拥有一种独有的特权,既管理不当,又加以限制。

p113.original: The Royal African company, the predecessors of the present African company, had an exclusive privilege by charter; but as that charter had not been confirmed by act of parliament, the trade, in consequence of the declaration of rights, was, soon after the Revolution, laid open to all his majesty's subjects. The Hudson's Bay company are, as to their legal rights, in the same situation as the Royal African company. Their exclusive charter has not been confirmed by act of parliament. The South Sea company, as long as they continued to be a trading company, had an exclusive privilege confirmed by act of parliament; as have likewise the present united company of merchants trading to the East Indies.
p113.zh: 非洲皇家公司是目前非洲公司的前身,它享有特许专有特权;但是,由于该特许专有特权没有得到议会法案的确认,因此,在革命后不久,由于宣布权利,该贸易向国王陛下的所有臣民开放。哈德逊湾公司就其合法权利而言,与皇家非洲公司处于同样状况. 他们的专属章程没有得到议会法案的确认。南海公司只要继续是一家贸易公司,就享有议会法案确认的独家特权;目前向东印度群岛贸易的商人联合公司也是如此。

p114.original: The Royal African company soon found that they could not maintain the competition against private adventurers, whom, notwithstanding the declaration of rights, they continued for some time to call interlopers, and to persecute as such. In 1698, however, the private adventurers were subjected to a duty of ten per cent. upon almost all the different branches of their trade, to be employed by the company in the maintenance of their forts and garrisons. But, notwithstanding this heavy tax, the company were still unable to maintain the competition. Their stock and credit gradually declined. In 1712, their debts had become so great, that a particular act of parliament was thought necessary, both for their security and for that of their creditors. It was enacted, that the resolution of two-thirds of these creditors in number and value should bind the rust, both with regard to the time which should be allowed to the company for the payment of their debts, and with regard to any other agreement which it might be thought proper to make with them concerning those debts. In 1730, their affairs were in so great disorder, that they were altogether incapable of maintaining their forts and garrisons, the sole purpose and pretext of their institution.
