Those beings, in whatever their essence might be supposed to consist, were parts of the great system of the universe, and parts, too, productive of the most important effects. Whatever human reason could either conclude or conjecture concerning them, made, as it were, two chapters, though no doubt two very important ones, of the science which pretended to give an account of the origin and revolutions of the great system of the universe. But in the universities of Europe, where philosophy was taught only as subservient to theology, it was natural to dwell longer upon these two chapters than upon any other of the science. They were gradually more and more extended, and were divided into many inferior chapters; till at last the doctrine of spirits, of which so little can be known, came to take up as much room in the system of philosophy as the doctrine of bodies, of which so much can be known. The doctrines concerning those two subjects were considered as making two distinct sciences. What are called metaphysics, or pneumatics, were set in opposition to physics, and were cultivated not only as the more sublime, but, for the purposes of a particular profession, as the more useful science of the two. The proper subject of experiment and observation, a subject in which a careful attention is capable of making so many useful discoveries, was almost entirely neglected. The subject in which, after a very few simple and almost obvious truths, the most careful attention can discover nothing but obscurity and uncertainty, and can consequently produce nothing but subtleties and sophisms, was greatly cultivated.
p163.zh: 在古代的哲学中,无论教授什么关于人的思想或神的性质,都成为物理学系统的一部分。 这些生物,无论它们本质上是什么, 都属于宇宙大系统的一部分, 以及一些部分, 产生最重要的效果。 无论人类的任何理由可以得出什么结论,也可以猜测它们。 科学的两章,尽管无疑是两个非常重要的章,都假装说明了宇宙伟大体系的起源和革命。 但是在欧洲的大学里,哲学只作为神学的附庸来教授,自然会比其他科学更长时间地停留在这两章上. 它们逐渐被扩大,被分成许多低劣的章节;直到终于灵体学说,其中鲜为人知,才在哲学体系中占据了和体体学说一样的空间,其中很多可以被人们知道.有关这两个主题的理论被认为是使两种不同的科学。所谓元物理,或称肺学,是被设定为与物理对立的,被培养的不仅是更次生的,而且为了特定职业的目的,是两者中更有用的科学.实验和观察的恰当主题,一个引起认真注意,能够作出如此众多有益的发现的主题,几乎被完全忽略了. 在经过极少数简单和几乎显而易见的真理之后,最仔细的注意只能发现模糊和不确定,从而只能产生微妙和 sophism 的主题得到了极大的培养。

p164.original: When those two sciences had thus been set in opposition to one another, the comparison between them naturally gave birth to a third, to what was called ontology, or the science which treated of the qualities and attributes which were common to both the subjects of the other two sciences. But if subtleties and sophisms composed the greater part of the metaphysics or pneumatics of the schools, they composed the whole of this cobweb science of ontology, which was likewise sometimes called metaphysics.
p164.zh: 当这两种科学因此相互对立时,它们之间的比较自然产生三分之一,即所谓的肿瘤学,或处理其他两种科学共同的素质和属性的科学。 但是,如果细微的和苏菲主义构成学校的元物理或肺学的较大部分,它们就构成了这个科布网科学的本体学整体,这有时也被称为元物理.

p165.original: Wherein consisted the happiness and perfection of a man, considered not only as an individual, but as the member of a family, of a state, and of the great society of mankind, was the object which the ancient moral philosophy proposed to investigate. In that philosophy, the duties of human life were treated of as subservient to the happiness and perfection of human life, But when moral, as well as natural philosophy, came to be taught only as subservient to theology, the duties of human life were treated of as chiefly subservient to the happiness of a life to come. In the ancient philosophy, the perfection of virtue was represented as necessarily productive, to the person who possessed it, of the most perfect happiness in this life. In the modern philosophy, it was frequently represented as generally, or rather as almost always, inconsistent with any degree of happiness in this life; and heaven was to be earned only by penance and mortification, by the austerities and abasement of a monk, not by the liberal, generous, and spirited conduct of a man. Casuistry, and an ascetic morality, made up, in most cases, the greater part of the moral philosophy of the schools. By far the most important of all the different branches of philosophy became in this manner by far the most corrupted.
p165.zh: 其中包含了一个人的幸福和完美,不仅被视为个人,而且被视为一个家庭的成员,一个国家的成员,以及人类伟大社会的成员,是古代道德哲学提出要调查的对象. 在这种哲学中,人类生活的义务被视作对人类生活的幸福和完美所屈从,但当道德和自然哲学被仅仅作为神学的附庸来教导时,人类生活的义务被视作对后世生活的幸福所主要屈从. 在古代哲学中,美德的完美被表现为 必然是生产性的, 对拥有美德的人来说,是这一生中最完美的幸福. 在现代哲学中,它经常被表述为一般的,或者说几乎总是的,与这个生活中任何程度的幸福都不一致;而天堂只能通过忏悔和毁谤,通过对和尚的紧缩和贬低来获得,而不是通过一个男人的自由,慷慨和精神的行为来获得.萨斯主义,以及一种醋制的道德,在多数情况下,构成了学校道德哲学的更大部分.至今为止,哲学中所有不同分支中最重要的部分都以这种方式变成了迄今为止最腐败的.

p166.original: Such, therefore, was the common course of philosophical education in the greater part of the universities in Europe. Logic was taught first; ontology came in the second place; pneumatology, comprehending the doctrine concerning the nature of the human soul and of the Deity, in the third; in the fourth followed a debased system of moral philosophy, which was considered as immediately connected with the doctrines of pneumatology, with the immortality of the human soul, and with the rewards and punishments which, from the justice of the Deity, were to be expected in a life to come: a short and superficial system of physics usually concluded the course.
p166.zh: 因此,这是欧洲大部分大学的哲学教育的常见课程。逻辑学是先教的;肿瘤学是第二教的;肺病学是第三教的,理解了人类灵魂和神性的性质的学说;第四教的道德哲学是继一个道德哲学的去基础体系,认为它与肺病学理论,人类灵魂的不朽直接相关,与从神性正义中可以预期的后世的奖惩有关:一个短暂而肤浅的物理体系通常会完成课程.

p167.original: The alterations which the universities of Europe thus introduced into the ancient course of philosophy were all meant for the education of ecclesiastics, and to render it a more proper introduction to the study of theology. But the additional quantity of subtlety and sophistry, the casuistry and ascetic morality which those alterations introduced into it, certainly did not render it more for the education of gentlemen or men of the world, or more likely either to improve the understanding or to mend the heart.
p167.zh: 欧洲各大学因此对古老哲学课程的改变,都是为了教育教会,使其更适当地成为神学研究的入门。 但是,这些改变所引入的微妙和索菲斯主义、精密和醋质道德的额外数量,当然并没有使它更有利于世界的绅士或男人的教育,或者更可能改善理解或修补心灵。

p168.original: This course of philosophy is what still continues to be taught in the greater part of the universities of Europe, with more or less diligence, according as the constitution of each particular university happens to render diligence more or less necessary to the teachers. In some of the richest and best endowed universities, the tutors content themselves with teaching a few unconnected shreds and parcels of this corrupted course; and even these they commonly teach very negligently and superficially.
p168.zh: 这种哲学课程是欧洲大部分大学继续教授的,多少是勤奋的,因为每个特定大学的章程恰好使勤奋对教师或多或少是必需的。在一些最富有、最富有的大学里,导师们满足于教授一些不相连的破烂课程;即使这些课程也常常很疏忽和肤浅地教授。

p169.original: The improvements which, in modern times have been made in several different branches of philosophy, have not, the greater part of them, been made in universities, though some, no doubt, have. The greater part of universities have not even been very forward to adopt those improvements after they were made; and several of those learned societies have chosen to remain, for a long time, the sanctuaries in which exploded systems and obsolete prejudices found shelter and protection, after they had been hunted out of every other corner of the world. In general, the richest and best endowed universities have been slowest in adopting those improvements, and the most averse to permit any considerable change in the established plan of education. Those improvements were more easily introduced into some of the poorer universities, in which the teachers, depending upon their reputation for the greater part of their subsistence, were obliged to pay more attention to the current opinions of the world.
p169.zh: 现代在哲学的几个不同分支中所作的改进,在大学中并没有,其中的大部分,虽然有些无疑已经作了。大部分大学在作出这些改进之后,甚至没有非常积极地采取这些改进措施;一些学识丰富的社会在世界上其他每一个角落都被猎杀之后,长期选择继续作为爆炸性系统和过时偏见找到住所和保护的避难所。总的来说,最富有和最富有的大学在采用这些改进方面最为缓慢,最不愿意让既定教育计划有任何重大改变。 这些改进更容易引入一些较穷的大学,在这些大学中,教师们根据他们大部分生计的声誉,不得不更多地关注世界目前的观点。

p170.original: But though the public schools and universities of Europe were originally intended only for the education of a particular profession, that of churchmen; and though they were not always very diligent in instructing their pupils, even in the sciences which were supposed necessary for that profession; yet they gradually drew to themselves the education of almost all other people, particularly of almost all gentlemen and men of fortune. No better method, it seems, could be fallen upon, of spending, with any advantage, the long interval between infancy and that period of life at which men begin to apply in good earnest to the real business of the world, the business which is to employ them during the remainder of their days. The greater part of what is taught in schools and universities, however, does not seem to be the most proper preparation for that business.
p170.zh: 但是,虽然欧洲的公立学校和大学最初只针对特定专业的教育,即教会人士的教育;虽然他们并不总是很勤奋地教导学生,甚至从事本该为该专业所必需的科学;然而,他们却逐渐吸引了几乎所有其他人的教育,特别是几乎所有绅士和富人的教育。似乎没有更好的方法可以依靠在婴儿期和男子开始认真对待世界实际业务的这一生命期之间花费时间,这有其优势。 这个世界实际业务是在剩余时间内雇用他们的。 然而,中小学和大学大部分的教学内容似乎不是最恰当的准备工作。

p171.original: In England, it becomes every day more and more the custom to send young people to travel in foreign countries immediately upon their leaving school, and without sending them to any university. Our young people, it is said, generally return home much improved by their travels. A young man, who goes abroad at seventeen or eighteen, and returns home at one-and-twenty, returns three or four years older than he was when he went abroad; and at that age it is very difficult not to improve a good deal in three or four years. In the course of his travels, he generally acquires some knowledge of one or two foreign languages; a knowledge, however, which is seldom sufficient to enable him either to speak or write them with propriety. In other respects, he commonly returns home more conceited, more unprincipled, more dissipated, and more incapable of my serious application, either to study or to business, than he could well have become in so short a time had he lived at home. By travelling so very young, by spending in the most frivolous dissipation the most previous years of his life, at a distance from the inspection and control of his parents and relations, every useful habit, which the earlier parts of his education might have had some tendency to form in him, instead of being riveted and confirmed, is almost necessarily either weakened or effaced. Nothing but the discredit into which the universities are allowing themselves to fall, could ever have brought into repute so very absurd a practice as that of travelling at this early period of life. By sending his son abroad, a father delivers himself, at least for some time, from so disagreeable an object as that of a son unemployed, neglected, and going to ruin before his eyes.
p171.zh: 在英国,每天越来越多的习惯是,让年轻人离开学校后立即到外国旅行,而不送他们去任何大学. 据说,我们的年轻人由于旅行而普遍改善了返回家园的条件。少年以十七,十八岁出国,一二岁回国,比出国时大三,四岁回国;到了那个年龄,三四年内很难不改善好生意. 在旅行过程中,他一般会掌握一两种外语的一些知识;然而,这种知识很少足以使他能够讲好或写好这些外语。 在其他方面,他通常会更自负、更无原则、更分散、更不能认真申请,无论是学习还是经商,而如果住在家中,他很可能在如此短的时间内就已经无法回国。旅行非常年轻,在前些年最轻率的消散中度过,远离对父母和关系的检查和控制,每一个有用的习惯,他教育的早期部分都可能有些倾向形成在他身上,而不是被激怒和证实,几乎必然被削弱或抹去。 除了大学们所陷入的无名之谈之外,其他的大学都曾如此荒谬,就像在生命的早期旅行一样。 通过将儿子送出国,一个父亲将自己送出,至少是一段时间,从一个像一个儿子那样令人不快的物体上送出,这个物体就是失业,被忽视,并且会在他眼皮底下毁灭.

p172.original: Such have been the effects of some of the modern institutions for education.
p172.zh: 这些是一些现代教育机构的影响。

p173.original: Different plans and different institutions for education seem to have taken place in other ages and nations.
p173.zh: 其他年龄和国家似乎也制定了不同的计划和不同的教育机构。

p174.original: In the republics of ancient Greece, every free citizen was instructed, under the direction of the public magistrate, in gymnastic exercises and in music. By gymnastic exercises, it was intended to harden his body, to sharpen his courage, and to prepare him for the fatigues and dangers of war; and as the Greek militia was, by all accounts, one of the best that ever was in the world, this part of their public education must have answered completely the purpose for which it was intended. By the other part, music, it was proposed, at least by the philosophers and historians, who have given us an account of those institutions, to humanize the mind, to soften the temper, and to dispose it for performing all the social and moral duties of public and private life.
p174.zh: 在古希腊各共和国,每个自由公民在公共治安法官的指导下,都接受体育锻炼和音乐方面的指导。 通过体操锻炼,本意是使身体硬化,磨练勇气,让他为战争的疲劳和危险做好准备;而且由于希腊民兵从各方面讲都是世界上最好的,所以他们的这部分公共教育一定完全回答了它的目的. 另一方面,音乐,至少是哲学家和历史学家提出的,他们为我们讲述了这些机构的情况,他们提议使思想人性化,缓和脾气,并把它用于履行公共和私人生活的所有社会和道德义务。

p175.original: In ancient Rome, the exercises of the Campus Martius answered the same purpose as those of the Gymnasium in ancient Greece, and they seem to have answered it equally well. But among the Romans there was nothing which corresponded to the musical education of the Greeks. The morals of the Romans, however, both in private and public life, seem to have been, not only equal, but, upon the whole, a good deal superior to those of the Greeks. That they were superior in private life, we have the express testimony of Polybius, and of Dionysius of Halicarnassus, two authors well acquainted with both nations; and the whole tenor of the Greek and Roman history bears witness to the superiority of the public morals of the Romans. The good temper and moderation of contending factions seem to be the most essential circumstances in the public morals of a free people. But the factions of the Greeks were almost always violent and sanguinary; whereas, till the time of the Gracchi, no blood had ever been shed in any Roman faction; and from the time of the Gracchi, the Roman republic may be considered as in reality dissolved. Notwithstanding, therefore, the very respectable authority of Plato, Aristotle, and Polybius, and notwithstanding the very ingenious reasons by which Mr. Montesquieu endeavours to support that authority, it seems probable that the musical education of the Greeks had no great effect in mending their morals, since, without any such education, those of the Romans were, upon the whole, superior. The respect of those ancient sages for the institutions of their ancestors had probably disposed them to find much political wisdom in what was, perhaps, merely an ancient custom, continued, without interruption, from the earliest period of those societies, to the times in which they had arrived at a considerable degree of refinement. Music and dancing are the great amusements of almost all barbarous nations, and the great accomplishments which are supposed to fit any man for entertaining his society. It is so at this day among the negroes on the coast of Africa. It was so among the ancient Celtes, among the ancient Scandinavians, and, as we may learn from Homer, among the ancient Greeks, in the times preceding the Trojan war. When the Greek tribes had formed themselves into little republics, it was natural that the study of those accomplishments should for a long time make a part of the public and common education of the people.
p175.zh: 在古罗马,Campus Martius的练习与古希腊的体操同样回答了目的,他们似乎同样很好地回答了. 但在罗马人当中,没有与希腊人的音乐教育相对应的东西. 然而,无论是在私人生活还是公共生活中,罗马人的道德似乎不仅平等,而且在总体上也优于希腊人的道德。 在私生活上他们优异,我们有波利比乌斯和哈利卡纳苏斯的狄奥尼修斯的见证,两位著作家对两国都非常熟悉;整个希腊和罗马历史的主旨见证了罗马人公共道德的优越性.争斗派别的良好脾气和温和似乎是自由人民公共道德中最基本的条件。 但希腊人的派系几乎总是暴力的,血统主义的;而直到格拉奇时代,任何罗马派别都没有流血;从格拉奇时代开始,罗马共和国可以被认为是现实中的解体. 因此,尽管柏拉图、亚里士多德和波利比乌斯的权威非常可敬,尽管他有非常聪明的理由。蒙特斯基厄努力支持这一权威,希腊人的音乐教育似乎在修补道德方面没有很大影响,因为没有这种教育,罗马人的音乐教育总的来说就占上风。尊重这些古老的贤者对其祖先机构的尊重,可能使他们在也许仅仅是一种古老的习俗中找到许多政治智慧,从这些社会的最初时期一直不间断地持续到他们达到相当完善的时代。音乐和舞蹈是几乎所有野蛮国家的伟大娱乐,是任何一个人理应适合娱乐其社会的巨大成就。 今天,非洲海岸的黑人中就是这样。 它在古代凯尔特人,古代斯堪的纳维亚人中是如此,在我们从荷马人,古希腊人中学习,在特洛伊战争前的时代中也如此. 当希腊各部落组成小共和国时,对这些成就的研究在很长一段时间内自然会成为公众和人民共同教育的一部分。

p176.original: The masters who instructed the young people, either in music or in military exercises, do not seem to have been paid, or even appointed by the state, either in Rome or even at Athens, the Greek republic of whose laws and customs we are the best informed. The state required that every free citizen should fit himself for defending it in war, and should upon that account, learn his military exercises. But it left him to learn them of such masters as he could find; and it seems to have advanced nothing for this purpose, but a public field or place of exercise, in which he should practise and perform them.
p176.zh: 无论是在音乐还是在军事演习中,指导年轻人的主人似乎没有报酬,甚至没有国家任命,无论是在罗马还是在雅典,我们最了解希腊共和国的法律和习俗。国家要求每个自由公民在战争中都适合保卫国家,并因此学习军事演习。 但是,这让他学习他能找到的主人;而且似乎没有为此而推进任何工作,而是一个公共领域或锻炼场所,他应该在其中实践和表演这些东西。

p177.original: In the early ages, both of the Greek and Roman republics, the other parts of education seem to have consisted in learning to read, write, and account, according to the arithmetic of the times. These accomplishments the richer citizens seem frequently to have acquired at home, by the assistance of some domestic pedagogue, who was, generally, either a slave or a freedman; and the poorer citizens in the schools of such masters as made a trade of teaching for hire. Such parts of education, however, were abandoned altogether to the care of the parents or guardians of each individual. It does not appear that the state ever assumed any inspection or direction of them. By a law of Solon, indeed, the children were acquitted from maintaining those parents who had neglected to instruct them in some profitable trade or business.
p177.zh: 在早期,无论是希腊共和国还是罗马共和国,其他教育部分似乎都由学习读写,记账组成,根据当时的算术. 这些成就似乎经常是在国内获得的,得到一些国内教育家的帮助,他们一般是奴隶或自由人;在师资学校中较贫穷的公民则从事雇佣教学。 然而,这些教育部分完全被放弃,由每个人的父母或监护人照管。国家似乎从未对他们进行任何检查或指示。 根据索隆的一项法律,孩子们确实被免除了抚养那些忽视了教育他们从事一些有利可图的交易或商业的父母的责任。

p178.original: In the progress of refinement, when philosophy and rhetoric came into fashion, the better sort of people used to send their children to the schools of philosophers and rhetoricians, in order to be instructed in these fashionable sciences. But those schools were not supported by the public. They were, for a long time, barely tolerated by it. The demand for philosophy and rhetoric was, for a long time, so small, that the first professed teachers of either could not find constant employment in any one city, but were obliged to travel about from place to place. In this manner lived Zeno of Elea, Protagoras, Gorgias, Hippias, and many others. As the demand increased, the school, both of philosophy and rhetoric, became stationary, first in Athens, and afterwards in several other cities. The state, however, seems never to have encouraged them further, than by assigning to some of them a particular place to teach in, which was sometimes done, too, by private donors. The state seems to have assigned the Academy to Plato, the Lyceum to Aristotle, and the Portico to Zeno of Citta, the founder of the Stoics. But Epicurus bequeathed his gardens to his own school. Till about the time of Marcus Antoninus, however, no teacher appears to have had any salary from the public, or to have had any other emoluments, but what arose from the honorarius or fees of his scholars. The bounty which that philosophical emperor, as we learn from Lucian, bestowed upon one of the teachers of philosophy, probably lasted no longer than his own life. There was nothing equivalent to the privileges of graduation; and to have attended any of those schools was not necessary, in order to be permitted to practise any particular trade or profession. If the opinion of their own utility could not draw scholars to them, the law neither forced anybody to go to them, nor rewarded anybody for having gone to them. The teachers had no jurisdiction over their pupils, nor any other authority besides that natural authority which superior virtue and abilities never fail to procure from young people towards those who are entrusted with any part of their education.
p178.zh: 在不断完善的过程中,当哲学和修辞学成为时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚时尚 但是,这些学校没有得到公众的支持。 他们被它容忍了很久长期以来,对哲学和修辞的要求如此之小,以致于第一位自称是其中之一的教师在任何一个城市都找不到固定的工作,而不得不四处旅行。以这种方式生活着伊莱亚的泽诺,普罗塔戈拉斯,戈尔吉亚斯,希皮亚斯等许多民族. 随着需求增加,学校无论是哲学还是修辞学,都变得静止不动,首先在雅典,后来又在其他几个城市. 然而,国家似乎从未进一步鼓励他们,只是为他们中的某些人指定一个特定的教学地点,有时私人捐助者也这样做。 该州似乎将学院分配给了柏拉图,莱塞姆派分配给了亚里士多德,波蒂科派分配给了斯多克派的创始人Citta的泽诺. 但埃皮库鲁斯将他的花园留给了自己的学校. 然而直到马库斯·安东尼努斯(Marcus Antoninus)的时代,似乎没有一位教师从公众那里得到任何薪水,或者有任何其他报酬,但是他的学者们的荣誉或费用产生了什么. 那个哲学皇帝给我们的恩惠,就像我们从卢西安那里学到的, 给了哲学的一位老师, 可能不会持续到他自己的生命。毕业的特权与毕业无关;在任何这类学校就读都没有必要,以便允许从事任何特定行业或专业。法律既未强迫任何人去他们那里,也未奖励任何人去他们那里。教师对其学生没有管辖权,除了这一自然权威之外,任何其他权威都具有优越的美德和能力,永远不能不从年轻人那里得到那些受托接受任何部分教育的人。

p179.original: At Rome, the study of the civil law made a part of the education, not of the greater part of the citizens, but of some particular families. The young people, however, who wished to acquire knowledge in the law, had no public school to go to, and had no other method of studying it, than by frequenting the company of such of their relations and friends as were supposed to understand it. It is, perhaps, worth while to remark, that though the laws of the twelve tables were many of them copied from those of some ancient Greek republics, yet law never seems to have grown up to be a science in any republic of ancient Greece. In Rome it became a science very early, and gave a considerable degree of illustration to those citizens who had the reputation of understanding it. In the republics of ancient Greece, particularly in Athens, the ordinary courts of justice consisted of numerous, and therefore disorderly, bodies of people, who frequently decided almost at random, or as clamour, faction, and party-spirit, happened to determine. The ignominy of an unjust decision, when it was to be divided among five hundred, a thousand, or fifteen hundred people (for some of their courts were so very numerous), could not fall very heavy upon any individual. At Rome, on the contrary, the principal courts of justice consisted either of a single judge, or of a small number of judges, whose characters, especially as they deliberated always in public, could not fail to be very much affected by any rash or unjust decision. In doubtful cases such courts, from their anxiety to avoid blame, would naturally endeavour to shelter themselves under the example or precedent of the judges who had sat before them, either in the same or in some other court. This attention to practice and precedent, necessarily formed the Roman law into that regular and orderly system in which it has been delivered down to us; and the like attention has had the like effects upon the laws of every other country where such attention has taken place. The superiority of character in the Romans over that of the Greeks, so much remarked by Polybius and Dionysius of Halicarnassus, was probably more owing to the better constitution of their courts of justice, than to any of the circumstances to which those authors ascribe it. The Romans are said to have been particularly distinguished for their superior respect to an oath. But the people who were accustomed to make oath only before some diligent and well informed court of justice, would naturally be much more attentive to what they swore, than they who were accustomed to do the same thing before mobbish and disorderly assemblies.
p179.zh: 在罗马,对民法的研究使教育成为了一部分,不是公民中较大的一部分,而是某些特定家庭的一部分. 然而,希望获得法律知识的年轻人没有公立学校,也没有其他学习方法,只能经常与他们本来应该理解的这种关系和朋友在一起。 也许值得指出的是,虽然十二表的法律中有许多是从一些古希腊共和国的法律中复制出来的,但法律似乎从未发展成为古希腊任何一个共和国的科学。在罗马,它很早就成为了一种科学,并给那些有了解它的声誉的公民提供了相当程度的例证. 在古希腊各共和国,特别是在雅典,普通法院由众多的、因而是无序的人群组成,他们常常几乎随意地或作为喧嚣、派别和党派精神来决定。一项不公正的决定,如果分为500、1 000或1 500人(因为有些法院数量如此之多),那么这种不光彩不会对任何个人造成很大的影响。 相反,在罗马,主要法院要么由一名法官组成,要么由少数法官组成,法官的性格,特别是因为他们总是在公开场合审议,因此不能不受到任何鲁莽或不公正的裁决的很大影响。 在有疑问的案件中,这些法院出于避免受到指责的焦虑,自然会努力以在它们审理的法官的榜样或先例为借口,或者在同一法庭,或者在其他一些法庭上。 这种对实践和先例的注意,必然使罗马法律形成一种正常和有序的制度,在这种制度下,它交给了我们;而类似的注意对引起这种注意的每一个其他国家的法律都产生了类似的影响。罗马人中性格优于希腊人,哈利卡纳苏斯的Polybius和Dionysius也如此强调这一点,这很可能更多是由于他们法院的章程较好,而不是由于这些作者所描述的任何情况。 据说罗马人以对誓词的优异尊重而特别显赫. 但习惯只在勤奋和知情的法庭上宣誓的人,自然会比习惯在暴徒和无序集会前做同样事情的人,更注意他们所发誓的.

p180.original: The abilities, both civil and military, of the Greeks and Romans, will readily be allowed to have been at least equal to those of any modern nation. Our prejudice is perhaps rather to overrate them. But except in what related to military exercises, the state seems to have been at no pains to form those great abilities; for I cannot be induced to believe that the musical education of the Greeks could be of much consequence in forming them. Masters, however, had been found, it seems, for instructing the better sort of people among those nations, in every art and science in which the circumstances of their society rendered it necessary or convenient for them to be instructed. The demand for such instruction produced, what it always produces, the talent for giving it; and the emulation which an unrestrained competition never fails to excite, appears to have brought that talent to a very high degree of perfection. In the attention which the ancient philosophers excited, in the empire which they acquired over the opinions and principles of their auditors, in the faculty which they possessed of giving a certain tone and character to the conduct and conversation of those auditors, they appear to have been much superior to any modern teachers. In modern times, the diligence of public teachers is more or less corrupted by the circumstances which render them more or less independent of their success and reputation in their particular professions. Their salaries, too, put the private teacher, who would pretend to come into competition with them, in the same state with a merchant who attempts to trade without a bounty, in competition with those who trade with a considerable one. If he sells his goods at nearly the same price, he cannot have the same profit; and poverty and beggary at least, if not bankruptcy and ruin, will infallibly be his lot. If he attempts to sell them much dearer, he is likely to have so few customers, that his circumstances will not be much mended. The privileges of graduation, besides, are in many countries necessary, or at least extremely convenient, to most men of learned professions, that is, to the far greater part of those who have occasion for a learned education. But those privileges can be obtained only by attending the lectures of the public teachers. The most careful attendance upon the ablest instructions of any private teacher cannot always give any title to demand them. It is from these different causes that the private teacher of any of the sciences, which are commonly taught in universities, is, in modern times, generally considered as in the very lowest order of men of letters. A man of real abilities can scarce find out a more humiliating or a more unprofitable employment to turn them to. The endowments of schools and colleges have in this manner not only corrupted the diligence of public teachers, but have rendered it almost impossible to have any good private ones.
p180.zh: 希腊人和罗马人的能力,无论是民事能力还是军事能力,都很容易被允许至少与任何现代国家的能力平等。 我们的偏见或许是夸大其词。 但除了与军事演习相关的内容外,国家似乎没有尽心尽力形成这些伟大的能力;因为我无法被诱导相信希腊人的音乐教育在形成这些能力时会产生很大的后果. 然而,似乎已经发现,在那些国家中,在各种艺术和科学中,指导那些国家中比较好的人是主人公,在这种艺术和科学中,他们的社会情况使他们有必要或方便地接受指导。对这种教育的需求、这种教育的一贯成果、给予这种教育的天赋,以及无限制的竞争从未失败的模仿,似乎使这种天赋达到非常完美的程度。古代哲学家们所激动的注意力,在他们对其审计员的意见和原则获得的帝国中,在他们拥有的给这些审计员的行为和谈话以某种语气和特征的系里,他们似乎比任何现代教师都优越得多。 在现代,公共教师的勤奋程度或多或少地受到环境的破坏,这些环境使他们或多或少地独立于自己在特定专业中的成功和声誉。 他们的薪水也使假想与他们竞争的私人教师与一个试图在没有赏金的情况下进行贸易的商人处于同一状态,与那些与相当数量的人进行贸易的竞争. 如果他以几乎相同的价格出售他的商品,他就不能有同样的利润;而贫穷和乞丐至少,如果不是破产和毁灭,将是他的命运。 如果他想卖得更亲切,那么他的顾客就可能如此之少,以至于他的情况不会大有改观。 此外,在许多国家,毕业的特权对于大多数有学识的专业人员来说是必要的,或者至少是极为方便的,即对于有学识的那些人来说,是相当多。 但是,只有参加公共教师的讲座,才能获得这些特权。 根据任何私人教师的最好指示,最谨慎的出勤者不能总是给予要求他们的任何资格。 正是由于这些不同的原因,在现代,任何理科的私人教师,在大学中通常教课,一般被认为是在最底层的男性字母顺序中.真正有能力的人很难找到更丢脸或更无利可图的工作来将他们转向。学校和学院的捐赠以这种方式不仅腐蚀了公共教师的勤奋,而且几乎不可能有任何好的私人教师。

p181.original: Were there no public institutions for education, no system, no science, would be taught, for which there was not some demand, or which the circumstances of the times did not render it either necessary or convenient, or at least fashionable to learn. A private teacher could never find his account in teaching either an exploded and antiquated system of a science acknowledged to be useful, or a science universally believed to be a mere useless and pedantic heap of sophistry and nonsense. Such systems, such sciences, can subsist nowhere but in those incorporated societies for education, whose prosperity and revenue are in a great measure independent of their industry. Were there no public institutions for education, a gentleman, after going through, with application and abilities, the most complete course of education which the circumstances of the times were supposed to afford, could not come into the world completely ignorant of everything which is the common subject of conversation among gentlemen and men of the world.
p181.zh: 如果没有公立的教育机构,就将没有制度,没有科学的教学,而对于这种教育,没有某种需求,或者由于时代的情况,没有使学习成为必要或方便的,或者至少是时尚的。私人教师在教授一个被公认为有用的爆炸式和过时的科学系统时,或是一个被普遍认为只是无用和恋童癖的索菲斯主义和无稽之谈的科学时,永远找不到他的叙述。 这种系统,这种科学,除了在融合的教育社会中生活外,是无处不在的,因为这些社会中的繁荣和收入在很大程度上独立于其工业。 如果没有公立教育机构,绅士们在经过了应用和能力之后,通过当时的情况理应能够承受的最完整的教育课程,不可能完全不懂得世界绅士们和男人们共同对话的话题。

p182.original: There are no public institutions for the education of women, and there is accordingly nothing useless, absurd, or fantastical, in the common course of their education. They are taught what their parents or guardians judge it necessary or useful for them to learn, and they are taught nothing else. Every part of their education tends evidently to some useful purpose; either to improve the natural attractions of their person, or to form their mind to reserve, to modesty, to chastity, and to economy; to render them both likely to became the mistresses of a family, and to behave properly when they have become such. In every part of her life, a woman feels some conveniency or advantage from every part of her education. It seldom happens that a man, in any part of his life, derives any conveniency or advantage from some of the most laborious and troublesome parts of his education.
p182.zh: 妇女教育没有公立机构,因此,在她们共同的教育过程中,没有任何无用、荒谬或奇幻的。教他们父母或监护人如何判断学习是否必要或有用,而教他们别无他法。 他们的每一个教育部分显然都倾向于某种有用的目的;或者改善他们个人的自然吸引力,或者形成他们保留、谦虚、贞操和经济的思想;使他们既有可能成为家庭的情妇,又在他们成为家庭的情妇时行为得体。 在生活的每一阶段,妇女都从教育的每一部分中感到有些屈从或优势。一个人在其一生的任何阶段,很少从他教育中最费力和最烦恼的部分获得任何宽容或优势。

p183.original: Ought the public, therefore, to give no attention, it may be asked, to the education of the people? Or, if it ought to give any, what are the different parts of education which it ought to attend to in the different orders of the people? and in what manner ought it to attend to them?
p183.zh: 因此,公众不应该不注意,也许可以要求它去注意人民的教育? 或者,如果说它应该给予什么,它应该按照人民的不同秩序去处理什么教育的不同部分? 它应该以什么方式去照顾他们?

p184.original: In some cases, the state of society necessarily places the greater part of individuals in such situations as naturally form in them, without any attention of government, almost all the abilities and virtues which that state requires, or perhaps can admit of. In other cases, the state of the society does not place the greater part of individuals in such situations; and some attention of government is necessary, in order to prevent the almost entire corruption and degeneracy of the great body of the people.
p184.zh: 在某些情况下,社会状况必然将大部分个人置于他们自然形成的状况中,而政府却不给予任何关注,几乎是国家所需要的或可能承认的所有能力和美德。 在其他情况下,社会状况并不将较大部分的个人置于这种情况下;为了防止人民伟大身体的几乎全部的腐败和退化,政府必须给予一定的注意.

p185.original: In the progress of the division of labour, the employment of the far greater part of those who live by labour, that is, of the great body of the people, comes to be confined to a few very simple operations; frequently to one or two. But the understandings of the greater part of men are necessarily formed by their ordinary employments. The man whose whole life is spent in performing a few simple operations, of which the effects, too, are perhaps always the same, or very nearly the same, has no occasion to exert his understanding, or to exercise his invention, in finding out expedients for removing difficulties which never occur. He naturally loses, therefore, the habit of such exertion, and generally becomes as stupid and ignorant as it is possible for a human creature to become. The torpor of his mind renders him not only incapable of relishing or bearing a part in any rational conversation, but of conceiving any generous, noble, or tender sentiment, and consequently of forming any just judgment concerning many even of the ordinary duties of private life. Of the great and extensive interests of his country he is altogether incapable of judging; and unless very particular pains have been taken to render him otherwise, he is equally incapable of defending his country in war. The uniformity of his stationary life naturally corrupts the courage of his mind, and makes him regard, with abhorrence, the irregular, uncertain, and adventurous life of a soldier. It corrupts even the activity of his body, and renders him incapable of exerting his strength with vigour and perseverance in any other employment, than that to which he has been bred. His dexterity at his own particular trade seems, in this manner, to be acquired at the expense of his intellectual, social, and martial virtues. But in every improved and civilized society, this is the state into which the labouring poor, that is, the great body of the people, must necessarily fall, unless government takes some pains to prevent it.
p185.zh: 在劳动分工的进程中,广大劳动群众,即广大人民群众的就业,都限于几个非常简单的操作;经常是一两个. 但是,对大部分男性的理解必然是因为他们的普通职业而形成的.一生从事一些简单手术的人,其效果也许也总是一样,或者几乎是相同的,没有机会表达他的理解或行使他的发明,找出消除从未发生的困难的时机。 因此,他自然会失去这种劳作的习惯,一般会变得像人类生物一样愚蠢和无知.思想的扭曲使他不仅不能享受或参与任何理性的对话,而且不能想象任何慷慨、高尚或温柔的情绪,从而对许多甚至私人生活的一般义务形成任何公正的判断。 他完全无法判断他的国家的巨大和广泛的利益;除非他受到特别的痛苦,否则他同样无法在战争中保卫他的国家。 他的固定生活的统一性自然地腐蚀了他的心灵的勇气,并让他怀恨在心,怀恨在心,不规则的,不确定的,冒险的士兵生活. 它甚至腐蚀了他的身体活动,使他无法在任何其他工作上,而不是在培养他的工作上,用精力和坚韧不拔地发挥力气。 他对自己的特殊贸易的狡猾性,以这种方式看来,是以牺牲他的知识,社会和武术的美德而获得的. 但在每一个改良和文明的社会里,这就是劳苦的穷人,即人民的伟大身体,必然会沦陷的状态,除非政府采取一些痛苦来阻止它.

p186.original: It is otherwise in the barbarous societies, as they are commonly called, of hunters, of shepherds, and even of husbandmen in that rude state of husbandry which precedes the improvement of manufactures, and the extension of foreign commerce. In such societies, the varied occupations of every man oblige every man to exert his capacity, and to invent expedients for removing difficulties which are continually occurring. Invention is kept alive, and the mind is not suffered to fall into that drowsy stupidity, which, in a civilized society, seems to benumb the understanding of almost all the inferior ranks of people. In those barbarous societies, as they are called, every man, it has already been observed, is a warrior. Every man, too, is in some measure a statesman, and can form a tolerable judgment concerning the interest of the society, and the conduct of those who govern it. How far their chiefs are good judges in peace, or good leaders in war, is obvious to the observation of almost every single man among them. In such a society, indeed, no man can well acquire that improved and refined understanding which a few men sometimes possess in a more civilized state. Though in a rude society there is a good deal of variety in the occupations of every individual, there is not a great deal in those of the whole society. Every man does, or is capable of doing, almost every thing which any other man does, or is capable of being. Every man has a considerable degree of knowledge, ingenuity, and invention but scarce any man has a great degree. The degree, however, which is commonly possessed, is generally sufficient for conducting the whole simple business of the society. In a civilized state, on the contrary, though there is little variety in the occupations of the greater part of individuals, there is an almost infinite variety in those of the whole society. These varied occupations present an almost infinite variety of objects to the contemplation of those few, who, being attached to no particular occupation themselves, have leisure and inclination to examine the occupations of other people. The contemplation of so great a variety of objects necessarily exercises their minds in endless comparisons and combinations, and renders their understandings, in an extraordinary degree, both acute anti comprehensive. Unless those few, however, happen to be placed in some very particular situations, their great abilities, though honourable to themselves, may contribute very little to the good government or happiness of their society. Notwithstanding the great abilities of those few, all the nobler parts of the human character may be, in a great measure, obliterated and extinguished in the great body of the people.
p186.zh: 否则,在野蛮社会,即通常所称的猎人、牧羊人、甚至丈夫,在改进制成品和扩大对外商业之前,就处于这种粗鲁的畜牧业状态。 在这种社会中,每个人的各种职业都要求每个人发挥其能力,并发明各种手段来消除不断发生的困难。发明被保持生命力,心灵不会陷入这种昏沉沉的愚蠢之中,在一个文明的社会里,这似乎就是对几乎所有低等阶层的人的理解。 在这些野蛮的社会里,人们称之为 " 每一个已经观察到的人,都是战士 " 。每个人,在某种程度上,也是政治家,可以对社会的利益和治理社会的人的行为形成一种可以容忍的判断. 他们的首领在和平中是好评事,或者在战争中是好评事,这在他们中几乎每一个人的观察中都很明显. 实际上,在这样一个社会中,没有一个人能够很好地获得一些男人有时在更文明的状态下所具备的这种更好和更好的理解。 虽然在一个粗鲁的社会中,每个人的职业都有很大的种类,但是整个社会的职业并不多。 每个人都做,或者有能力做, 几乎每一个事情 任何人做,或者有能力做。 每个人都有相当程度的知识、智慧和发明,但很少有人有很强的学识。 然而,通常拥有的学位一般足以开展整个社会的简单业务。 相反,在一个文明国家,虽然大部分个人的职业几乎没有多样性,但整个社会的这种职业几乎无穷无尽。 这些职业种类繁多,几乎无穷无尽。 只有少数人认为,他们本身没有从事任何特定职业,因此闲暇和倾向于审查其他人的职业。 对如此众多物体的思考,必然用无穷无尽的比较和组合来锻炼他们的思想,并使得他们的理解,在非凡的程度上,都具有尖锐的反综合性. 然而,除非少数人恰好被置于某些非常特殊的情况中,否则他们的伟大能力,虽然是对自己光荣的,但对他们社会的善政或幸福可能贡献甚微。 尽管这些少数人具有巨大能力,但人类性格中所有较崇高的部分,在人民伟大身体中,都可能在很大程度上被消灭和消灭。

p187.original: The education of the common people requires, perhaps, in a civilized and commercial society, the attention of the public, more than that of people of some rank and fortune. People of some rank and fortune are generally eighteen or nineteen years of age before they enter upon that particular business, profession, or trade, by which they propose to distinguish themselves in the world. They have, before that, full time to acquire, or at least to fit themselves for afterwards acquiring, every accomplishment which can recommend them to the public esteem, or render them worthy of it. Their parents or guardians are generally sufficiently anxious that they should be so accomplished, and are in most cases, willing enough to lay out the expense which is necessary for that purpose. If they are not always properly educated, it is seldom from the want of expense laid out upon their education, but from the improper application of that expense. It is seldom from the want of masters, but from the negligence and incapacity of the masters who are to be had, and from the difficulty, or rather from the impossibility, which there is, in the present state of things, of finding any better. The employments, too, in which people of some rank or fortune spend the greater part of their lives, are not, like those of the common people, simple and uniform. They are almost all of them extremely complicated, and such as exercise the head more than the hands. The understandings of those who are engaged in such employments, can seldom grow torpid for want of exercise. The employments of people of some rank and fortune, besides, are seldom such as harass them from morning to night. They generally have a good deal of leisure, during which they may perfect themselves in every branch, either of useful or ornamental knowledge, of which they may have laid the foundation, or for which they may have acquired some taste in the earlier part of life.
p187.zh: 普通民众的教育,也许在一个文明的商业社会中,需要公众的注意,比一些级别和财富的人要多.某些级别和财富的人一般在进入某一行业、职业或行业之前年满18或19岁,他们提议在世界上作出区分。在此之前,他们拥有充分的时间来获得或至少适合在之后获得一切成就,这些成就可以推荐他们给公众,或使他们值得尊重。 他们的父母或监护人一般都十分担心他们应该完成这些任务,在大多数情况下,他们都愿意为此确定必要的费用。 如果她们并非总是受过适当的教育,那么很少是因为教育费用匮乏,而是因为不适当地使用这种费用。 这很少来自主人的匮乏,而是来自主人的失职和无能,以及来自困难,或者更确切地说,来自不可能找到更好的东西,而在当前的状况中,这是不可能的。某些级别或财富的人在其中度过大部分生活,其就业也不像普通人那样简单而统一。 它们几乎都极为复杂,例如,比手更能锻炼头部。从事这种工作的人的理解很少会因为缺乏锻炼而变得难以忍受。 此外,一些级别和财富的人的雇用很少像从早到晚骚扰他们那样。 他们一般都有相当的闲暇时间,期间他们可以在每一个分支中完善自己,无论是有用知识还是装饰知识,他们可能已经为这些知识奠定了基础,或者在生命的早期就已经获得一些品味.

p188.original: It is otherwise with the common people. They have little time to spare for education. Their parents can scarce afford to maintain them, even in infancy. As soon as they are able to work, they must apply to some trade, by which they can earn their subsistence. That trade, too, is generally so simple and uniform, as to give little exercise to the understanding; while, at the same time, their labour is both so constant and so severe, that it leaves them little leisure and less inclination to apply to, or even to think of any thing else.
p188.zh: 否则,它与普通人民有关。 他们几乎没有时间去接受教育。 他们的父母连婴儿期都负担不起抚养他们的费用。 一旦他们能够工作,他们就必须申请从事某些贸易,通过这些贸易,他们可以赚取生计。 这种贸易一般也如此简单和统一,很少给理解带来任何锻炼;与此同时,他们的劳动既如此持久又如此严重,使他们很少闲暇,更不愿意适用,甚至更不愿考虑任何其他事情。

p189.original: But though the common people cannot, in any civilized society, be so well instructed as people of some rank and fortune; the most essential parts of education, however, to read, write, and account, can be acquired at so early a period of life, that the greater part, even of those who are to be bred to the lowest occupations, have time to acquire them before they can be employed in those occupations. For a very small expense, the public can facilitate, can encourage and can even impose upon almost the whole body of the people, the necessity of acquiring those most essential parts of education.
p189.zh: 但是,尽管在任何文明社会中,普通人不能像一些级别和财富的人那样得到如此好的指导;但是,教育中最基本的部分,读写和核算,可以在生命的如此早期获得,因此,大部分人,即使是那些被培养到最底层职业的人,都有时间在从事这些职业之前获得这些知识。公众可以促进、鼓励甚至将获得教育这些最基本部分的必要性强加于几乎整个人民。

p190.original: The public can facilitate this acquisition, by establishing in every parish or district a little school, where children maybe taught for a reward so moderate, that even a common labourer may afford it; the master being partly, but not wholly, paid by the public; because, if he was wholly, or even principally, paid by it, he would soon learn to neglect his business. In Scotland, the establishment of such parish schools has taught almost the whole common people to read, and a very great proportion of them to write and account. In England, the establishment of charity schools has had an effect of the same kind, though not so universally, because the establishment is not so universal. If, in those little schools, the books by which the children are taught to read, were a little more instructive than they commonly are; and if, instead of a little smattering in Latin, which the children of the common people are sometimes taught there, and which can scarce ever be of any use to them, they were instructed in the elementary parts of geometry and mechanics; the literary education of this rank of people would, perhaps, be as complete as can be. There is scarce a common trade, which does not afford some opportunities of applying to it the principles of geometry and mechanics, and which would not, therefore, gradually exercise and improve the common people in those principles, the necessary introduction to the most sublime, as well as to the most useful sciences.
p190.zh: 公众可以通过在每一个教区或地区建立一所小学校来推动这一收购,儿童可能在那里为获得如此温和的奖励而授课,甚至一个普通的工人也付得起;主人的部分,但并非全部,由公众支付;因为,如果他是全部,甚至主要由它支付,他很快会学会忽视自己的业务。 在苏格兰,这种教区学校的建立使几乎所有的普通人都能够阅读,其中很大一部分人能够写作和记账。 在英国,慈善学校的建立也产生了同样的效果,虽然不是普遍的效果,因为这种建立并不普遍. 如果在这些小学校里,教孩子们阅读的书籍比一般的多一点启发性;如果不是用拉丁语讲一点东西,而常人的孩子有时在那里教一些东西,而这些东西对他们也没有什么用处,那么他们就被指示在几何学和力学的初级部分;这种级别的人的文学教育也许会尽可能地完整.几乎没有一种共同的贸易,这种贸易没有提供一些机会来应用几何学和力学的原则,因此,这种贸易不会逐步地行使和改进这些原则中的共同人民,即对最崇高的科学以及最有用的科学进行必要的介绍。

p191.original: The public can encourage the acquisition of those most essential parts of education, by giving small premiums, and little badges of distinction, to the children of the common people who excel in them.
p191.zh: 公众可以鼓励获得这些最基本的教育部分,为那些在教育中表现突出的普通人的子女提供少量的保险费和少有的奖章。

p192.original: The public can impose upon almost the whole body of the people the necessity of acquiring the most essential parts of education, by obliging every man to undergo an examination or probation in them, before he can obtain the freedom in any corporation, or be allowed to set up any trade, either in a village or town corporate.
p192.zh: 公众可以强迫几乎全体人民接受最基本的教育,要求每个人接受考试或缓刑,然后才能在任何公司获得自由,或获准在村庄或城镇的公司中建立任何贸易。

p193.original: It was in this manner, by facilitating the acquisition of their military and gymnastic exercises, by encouraging it, and even by imposing upon the whole body of the people the necessity of learning those exercises, that the Greek and Roman republics maintained the martial spirit of their respective citizens. They facilitated the acquisition of those exercises, by appointing a certain place for learning and practising them, and by granting to certain masters the privilege of teaching in that place. Those masters do not appear to have had either salaries or exclusive privileges of any kind. Their reward consisted altogether in what they got from their scholars; and a citizen, who had learnt his exercises in the public gymnasia, had no sort of legal advantage over one who had learnt them privately, provided the latter had learned them equally well. Those republics encouraged the acquisition of those exercises, by bestowing little premiums and badges of distinction upon those who excelled in them. To have gained a prize in the Olympic, Isthmian, or Nemaean games, gave illustration, not only to the person who gained it, but to his whole family and kindred. The obligation which every citizen was under, to serve a certain number of years, if called upon, in the armies of the republic, sufficiently imposed the necessity of learning those exercises, without which he could not be fit for that service.
p193.zh: 正是通过这种方式,通过便利获得军事和体操训练,鼓励这种训练,甚至通过强迫全体人民学习这些训练,希腊共和国和罗马共和国维持了各自公民的戒严精神。 他们通过指定一定的学习和练习地点,以及给予某些大师在那里的教学特权,为获得这些练习提供了便利。 这些主人似乎既没有薪水,也没有任何种类的专属特权。 他们的奖励完全来自他们的学者;一位公民在公共体操中学习过他的练习,他比私下学习的人没有某种法律优势,只要后者同样学习过这些运动。 这些共和国鼓励获得这些演习,对在演习中表现突出的人给予很少的奖励和奖章。 为了在奥运会中获得奖项,伊斯米安或内马恩的比赛中,不仅向获得奖项的人,而且向全家和亲友,提供了插图.每位公民在共和国军队中服役若干年(如果有要求的话)的义务,充分要求必须学习这些练习,没有这些练习,他就无法胜任这项工作。

p194.original: That in the progress of improvement, the practice of military exercises, unless government takes proper pains to support it, goes gradually to decay, and, together with it, the martial spirit of the great body of the people, the example of modern Europe sufficiently demonstrates. But the security of every society must always depend, more or less, upon the martial spirit of the great body of the people. In the present times, indeed, that martial spirit alone, and unsupported by a well-disciplined standing army, would not, perhaps, be sufficient for the defence and security of any society. But where every citizen had the spirit of a soldier, a smaller standing army would surely be requisite. That spirit, besides, would necessarily diminish very much the dangers to liberty, whether real or imaginary, which are commonly apprehended from a standing army. As it would very much facilitate the operations of that army against a foreign invader; so it would obstruct them as much, if unfortunately they should ever be directed against the constitution of the state.
p194.zh: 在改进过程中,军事演习的实践,除非政府采取适当痛心支持,否则就逐渐走向衰败,连同它,人民伟大身体的武术精神,现代欧洲的榜样就足以证明. 但是,每个社会的安全,总得多少地依靠人民伟大身体的武功精神. 实际上,在当今时代,光有这种武术精神,没有一支纪律严明的常备军队的支持,也许不足以维持任何社会的防卫和安全。 但是,如果每个公民都有士兵的精神,那么一支规模较小的常备部队肯定是必要的。 此外,这种精神必然会大大降低自由所面临的危险,无论是真实的还是想象的,这些危险通常是从常备部队中捕获的。因为这将大大便利该军队对外国侵略者的行动;因此,如果它们不幸地遭到国家宪法的反对,它也会阻碍它们。

p195.original: The ancient institutions of Greece and Rome seem to have been much more effectual for maintaining the martial spirit of the great body of the people, than the establishment of what are called the militias of modern times. They were much more simple. When they were once established, they executed themselves, and it required little or no attention from government to maintain them in the most perfect vigour. Whereas to maintain, even in tolerable execution, the complex regulations of any modern militia, requires the continual and painful attention of government, without which they are constantly falling into total neglect and disuse. The influence, besides, of the ancient institutions, was much more universal. By means of them, the whole body of the people was completely instructed in the use of arms; whereas it is but a very small part of them who can ever be so instructed by the regulations of any modern militia, except, perhaps, that of Switzerland. But a coward, a man incapable either of defending or of revenging himself, evidently wants one of the most essential parts of the character of a man. He is as much mutilated and deformed in his mind as another is in his body, who is either deprived of some of its most essential members, or has lost the use of them. He is evidently the more wretched and miserable of the two; because happiness and misery, which reside altogether in the mind, must necessarily depend more upon the healthful or unhealthful, the mutilated or entire state of the mind, than upon that of the body. Even though the martial spirit of the people were of no use towards the defence of the society, yet, to prevent that sort of mental mutilation, deformity, and wretchedness, which cowardice necessarily involves in it, from spreading themselves through the great body of the people, would still deserve the most serious attention of government; in the same manner as it would deserve its most serious attention to prevent a leprosy, or any other loathsome and offensive disease, though neither mortal nor dangerous, from spreading itself among them; though, perhaps, no other public good might result from such attention, besides the prevention of so great a public evil.
p195.zh: 希腊和罗马的古代机构似乎对于维持人民伟大身体的武术精神来说,比起现代所谓的民兵的建立,效果要大得多. 他们更简单。 当他们一成立,他们就被处决了,政府几乎不需要或根本不需要注意,以最完美的活力维持他们。 尽管维持,即使是在可容忍的处决中,任何现代民兵的复杂条例都需要政府持续和痛苦的注意,没有政府,他们就会不断陷入完全忽视和失去使用。 此外,古代机构的影响更加普遍。 通过这些手段,全国人民完全接受了使用武器的指示;而只有很小一部分人能够接受任何现代民兵(也许瑞士民兵除外)条例的这种指示。 但是,一个懦夫,一个既不能自卫又不能复仇的人,显然想要一个人性格中最重要的部分之一. 他的大脑与另一个人一样残缺和畸形,他的身体要么被剥夺了一些最基本的成员,要么失去了他们的使用。 他显然更悲惨,更悲惨;因为幸福和痛苦完全存在于心灵之中,必须更多地依赖健康或不健康、肢体残缺或整个心灵状态,而不是身体状况。 尽管人民的武斗精神对捍卫社会毫无用处,然而,防止这种精神残伤、畸形和恶劣,而懦弱必然涉及这种残割、畸形和恶劣,通过伟大的人民身体传播,政府仍应给予最认真的注意;同样,政府也应给予最认真的注意,防止麻风病或任何其他令人憎恶的和令人发指的疾病,尽管这种疾病既不是人,也不是危险疾病,但在其间传播;虽然,也许,除了预防如此严重的公共邪恶之外,这种注意不会产生任何其他公益。

p196.original: The same thing may be said of the gross ignorance and stupidity which, in a civilized society, seem so frequently to benumb the understandings of all the inferior ranks of people. A man without the proper use of the intellectual faculties of a man, is, if possible, more contemptible than even a coward, and seems to be mutilated and deformed in a still more essential part of the character of human nature. Though the state was to derive no advantage from the instruction of the inferior ranks of people, it would still deserve its attention that they should not be altogether uninstructed. The state, however, derives no inconsiderable advantage from their instruction. The more they are instructed, the less liable they are to the delusions of enthusiasm and superstition, which, among ignorant nations frequently occasion the most dreadful disorders. An instructed and intelligent people, besides, are always more decent and orderly than an ignorant and stupid one. They feel themselves, each individually, more respectable, and more likely to obtain the respect of their lawful superiors, and they are, therefore, more disposed to respect those superiors. They are more disposed to examine, and more capable of seeing through, the interested complaints of faction and sedition; and they are, upon that account, less apt to be misled into any wanton or unnecessary opposition to the measures of government. In free countries, where the safety of government depends very much upon the favourable judgment which the people may form of its conduct, it must surely be of the highest importance, that they should not be disposed to judge rashly or capriciously concerning it.
p196.zh: 同样,在文明社会中,这种无知和愚蠢似乎经常地使所有低等阶层的人理解这种无知和愚蠢。一个人没有正确利用一个人的知识能力,如果可能的话,比起一个懦夫,更是可鄙的,似乎被肢解和变形,在人类性格中仍然更为重要的一部分. 虽然国家不会从低等阶层的人的教导中获得任何好处,但人们仍然应当注意,他们不应完全没有受到指导。 但是,国家从他们的教导中并没有获得多少好处。 他们越听命于别人,就越难以接受热情和迷信的妄想,在无知的国家中,这种妄想往往造成最可怕的疾病。 而且,受教者和聪明人总是比无知和愚蠢者更体面和有秩序。 他们感到自己,每个人,都更加受人尊重,更可能获得合法上司的尊重,因此,他们更愿意尊重这些上司。 他们更愿意审查并更有能力通过对派别和煽动叛乱的不满;因此,他们更不愿意被误导到任何肆意或不必要地反对政府的措施。 在自由国家中,政府的安全在很大程度上取决于人民对其行为可能作出的有利判断,因此,绝对是最重要的,即不应轻率地或随意地判断政府的行为。

p197.original: Art. III.--Of the Expense of the Institutions for the Instruction of People of all Ages.
p197.zh: 第2条。 三. -- -- 各种年龄的人的教育机构开支。

p198.original: The institutions for the instruction of people of all ages, are chiefly those for religious instruction. This is a species of instruction, of which the object is not so much to render the people good citizens in this world, as to prepare them for another and a better world in the life to come. The teachers of the doctrine which contains this instruction, in the same manner as other teachers, may either depend altogether for their subsistence upon the voluntary contributions of their hearers; or they may derive it from some other fund, to which the law of their country may entitle them; such as a landed estate, a tythe or land tax, an established salary or stipend. Their exertion, their zeal and industry, are likely to be much greater in the former situation than in the latter. In this respect, the teachers of a new religion have always had a considerable advantage in attacking those ancient and established systems, of which the clergy, reposing themselves upon their benefices, had neglected to keep up the fervour of faith and devotion in the great body of the people; and having given themselves up to indolence, were become altogether incapable of making any vigorous exertion in defence even of their own establishment. The clergy of an established and well endowed religion frequently become men of learning and elegance, who possess all the virtues of gentlemen, or which can recommend them to the esteem of gentlemen; but they are apt gradually to lose the qualities, both good and bad, which gave them authority and influence with the inferior ranks of people, and which had perhaps been the original causes of the success and establishment of their religion. Such a clergy, when attacked by a set of popular and bold, though perhaps stupid and ignorant enthusiasts, feel themselves as perfectly defenceless as the indolent, effeminate, and full fed nations of the southern parts of Asia, when they were invaded by the active, hardy, and hungry Tartars of the north. Such a clergy, upon such an emergency, have commonly no other resource than to call upon the civil magistrate to persecute, destroy, or drive out their adversaries, as disturbers of the public peace. It was thus that the Roman catholic clergy called upon the civil magistrate to persecute the protestants, and the church of England to persecute the dissenters; and that in general every religious sect, when it has once enjoyed, for a century or two, the security of a legal establishment, has found itself incapable of making any vigorous defence against any new sect which chose to attack its doctrine or discipline. Upon such occasions, the advantage, in point of learning and good writing, may sometimes be on the side of the established church. But the arts of popularity, all the arts of gaining proselytes, are constantly on the side of its adversaries. In England, those arts have been long neglected by the well endowed clergy of the established church, and are at present chiefly cultivated by the dissenters and by the methodists. The independent provisions, however, which in many places have been made for dissenting teachers, by means of voluntary subscriptions, of trust rights, and other evasions of the law, seem very much to have abated the zeal and activity of those teachers. They have many of them become very learned, ingenious, and respectable men; but they have in general ceased to be very popular preachers. The methodists, without half the learning of the dissenters, are much more in vogue.
p198.zh: 不分年龄的人的教育机构主要是宗教教育机构。 这是一个教育的种类,其目标并不在于为今世人民造福,而在于使他们为未来生活的另一个更美好的世界做好准备。包含这一指示的学说教师可以与其他教师一样,完全依靠听众的自愿捐款维持生计;或者他们可以从其他基金获得,而这些国家的法律可能赋予他们这种基金的权利;例如土地财产、土地税或土地税、既定工资或津贴。 他们的努力、热情和工业在前一种情况中可能比后一种情况大得多。 在这方面,新宗教的教师在攻击这些古老和既定的制度方面总是有相当的优势,神职人员利用这些制度,却忽视了保持对人民伟大身体的信仰和奉献的热情;他们自责,甚至连自己的建立也完全无法为防卫作出任何积极的努力。 一个既有的和天资丰厚的宗教的神职人员经常成为有学识和优雅的人,他们拥有绅士的一切美德,或者可以推荐他们给绅士的尊崇;但是他们逐渐地丧失了无论好坏的品质,这给了他们与低等阶层的威信和影响,这或许是他们宗教的成功和建立最初的原因.这样的神职人员,当受到一群群众和大胆的,虽然也许愚蠢和无知的爱好者的攻击时,感觉自己完全没有自卫能力,就像无所事事,精疲力竭,饱满的亚洲南部地区国家一样,当他们被北方活跃的,坚硬的,饥饿的鞑靼人入侵时.在发生这种紧急情况时,这种神职人员通常没有其他手段,只能要求民事法官作为扰乱公共和平的人,迫害、摧毁或赶走他们的对手。 因此,罗马天主教神职人员呼吁民事法官迫害抗议者,而英格兰教会则迫害异议者;一般而言,每个宗教派别,当曾经享有一个或两个世纪的法制机构的安全时,都发现自己无法对任何选择攻击其教义或纪律的新教派提出任何有力的辩护。 在这种情况下,在学习和写作上的好处有时可能站在既有教会的一边。 但流行的艺术,所有获得传教士的艺术,总是站在对手一边. 在英国,这些艺术长期以来一直被既有教会的优秀神职人员忽视,目前主要由异议者和方法家栽培。 然而,许多地方通过自愿订阅、信任权利和其他逃避法律行为,对持不同意见的教师作出了独立规定,这些规定似乎大大削弱了这些教师的热情和活动。 他们中有许多人变得非常有学识,有才华,受人尊敬的人;但总的来说,他们不再是非常受欢迎的传教士.方法主义者,没有一半的异议者的学习,更是活泼.

p199.original: In the church of Rome the industry and zeal of the inferior clergy are kept more alive by the powerful motive of self-interest, than perhaps in any established protestant church. The parochial clergy derive many of them, a very considerable part of their subsistence from the voluntary oblations of the people; a source of revenue, which confession gives them many opportunities of improving. The mendicant orders derive their whole subsistence from such oblations. It is with them as with the hussars and light infantry of some armies; no plunder, no pay. The parochial clergy are like those teachers whose reward depends partly upon their salary, and partly upon the fees or honoraries which they get from their pupils; and these must always depend, more or less, upon their industry and reputation. The mendicant orders are like those teachers whose subsistence depends altogether upon their industry. They are obliged, therefore, to use every art which can animate the devotion of the common people. The establishment of the two great mendicant orders of St Dominic and St. Francis, it is observed by Machiavel, revived, in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, the languishing faith and devotion of the catholic church. In Roman catholic countries, the spirit of devotion is supported altogether by the monks, and by the poorer parochial clergy. The great dignitaries of the church, with all the accomplishments of gentlemen and men of the world, and sometimes with those of men of learning, are careful to maintain the necessary discipline over their inferiors, but seldom give themselves any trouble about the instruction of the people.
p199.zh: 在罗马的教堂里, 低级神职人员的产业和热情 被强大的 利益动机所维持, 比起任何既定的 抗议教会。教区神职人员从许多人那里获得,他们生计的相当一部分来自人民的自愿疏远;这是收入来源,使他们有许多改善的机会。死刑令就是从这种偏执中得来的。 他们和一些军队的胡萨人和轻步兵一样,没有掠夺,没有报酬。教士们就像那些教师一样,他们的奖励部分取决于他们的工资,部分取决于他们从学生那里得到的酬金或荣誉;而这些报酬或荣誉必须始终多少取决于他们的行业和声誉。违抗命令就像那些靠行业维生的教师一样。 因此,他们必须利用一切能够激发普通人民献身精神的艺术。圣多明我会和圣多明会的两大统治者的建立弗兰西斯,马奇雅维尔观察到,在13和14世纪,天主教会的沉痛信仰和奉献精神得以恢复。在罗马天主教国家,奉献精神得到僧侣和较穷的教士的完全支持.教会的伟大政要,有全世界绅士和士人的一切成就,有时也有学习的士人,都小心谨慎地保持对下等人的必要纪律,但很少给自己任何关于人民教导的麻烦.

p200.original: "Most of the arts and professions in a state," says by far the most illustrious philosopher and historian of the present age, "are of such a nature, that, while they promote the interests of the society, they are also useful or agreeable to some individuals; and, in that case, the constant rule of the magistrate, except, perhaps, on the first introduction of any art, is, to leave the profession to itself, and trust its encouragement to the individuals who reap the benefit of it. The artizans, finding their profits to rise by the favour of their customers, increase, as much as possible, their skill and industry; and as matters are not disturbed by any injudicious tampering, the commodity is always sure to be at all times nearly proportioned to the demand.
p200.zh: "一个状态下的大部分艺术和专业"说,迄今为止,当代最杰出的哲学家和历史学家"是这样的性质,虽然他们促进社会的利益,但也对一些个人有用或同意;在这种情况下,地方法官的恒定规则,除了任何艺术的首次引进,或许是让这个职业自己来决定,并且相信这个职业的鼓励是让从中得益的个人来决定的.蒿类动物发现他们的利润因顾客的好意而上升,因此尽可能地增加他们的技能和产业;而且由于事务没有受到任何有害的篡改的干扰,商品总是会随时与需求接近比例.

p201.original: "But there are also some callings which, though useful and even necessary in a state, bring no advantage or pleasure to any individual; and the supreme power is obliged to alter its conduct with regard to the retainers of those professions. It must give them public encouragement in order to their subsistence; and it must provide against that negligence to which they will naturally be subject, either by annexing particular honours to profession, by establishing a long subordination of ranks, and a strict dependence, or by some other expedient. The persons employed in the finances, fleets, and magistracy, are instances of this order of men.
p201.zh: "但也有一些召见,虽然在某州有用甚至必要,但不会给任何个人带来任何好处或乐趣;最高权力机关有义务改变其对于这些职业保留者的行为. 它必须公开鼓励他们维持生计;它必须防止他们自然会受到的疏忽,或者通过将特定荣誉与职业结合起来,通过建立长期的军衔从属关系和严格的依赖关系,或者通过某种其他手段。受雇于财政、船队和治安法官的人就是这种男子秩序的例子。

p202.original: "It may naturally be thought, at first sight, that the ecclesiastics belong to the first class, and that their encouragement, as well as that of lawyers and physicians, may safely be entrusted to the liberality of individuals, who are attached to their doctrines, and who find benefit or consolation from their spiritual ministry and assistance. Their industry and vigilance will, no doubt, be whetted by such an additional motive; and their skill in the profession, as well as their address in governing the minds of the people, must receive daily increase, from their increasing practice, study, and attention.
p202.zh: "自然可以认为,初觉悟者属于一等,他们的鼓励,以及律师和医生的鼓励,可以安全地委托给个人的自由主义,他们依附他们的学说,从他们的精神部和帮助中找到好处或安慰. 他们的行业和警惕无疑将受到这种额外动机的打击;他们在专业上的技巧以及管理人民思想的地址,必须从他们日益增加的实践、学习和关注中得到每天的增加。

p203.original: "But if we consider the matter more closely, we shall find that this interested diligence of the clergy is what every wise legislator will study to prevent; because, in every religion except the true, it is highly pernicious, and it has even a natural tendency to pervert the truth, by infusing into it a strong mixture of superstition, folly, and delusion. Each ghostly practitioner, in order to render himself more precious and sacred in the eyes of his retainers, will inspire them with the most violent abhorrence of all other sects, and continually endeavour, by some novelty, to excite the languid devotion of his audience. No regard will be paid to truth, morals, or decency, in the doctrines inculcated. Every tenet will be adopted that best suits the disorderly affections of the human frame. Customers will be drawn to each conventicle by new industry and address, in practising on the passions and credulity of the populace. And, in the end, the civil magistrate will find that he has dearly paid for his intended frugality, in saving a fixed establishment for the priests; and that, in reality, the most decent and advantageous composition, which he can make with the spiritual guides, is to bribe their indolence, by assigning stated salaries to their profession, and rendering it superfluous for them to be farther active, than merely to prevent their flock from straying in quest of new pastors. And in this manner ecclesiastical establishments, though commonly they arose at first from religious views, prove in the end advantageous to the political interests of society."
p203.zh: "但是如果我们更仔细地考虑这件事,我们将发现神职人员这种关心的勤奋是每一个明智的立法者所研究的来防止的;因为在除真教外的每一个宗教中,这是极其有害的,甚至有自然的扭曲真理的倾向,通过向它注入迷信,愚蠢和妄想的强烈的混合. 每个幽灵的修行者为了让自己在保留者的眼中更加珍贵和神圣,将以最暴力的憎恶其他教派来激励他们,并且通过某种新颖的手法,不断地努力激起他的观众的无耻奉献. 在灌输的教义中,将不考虑真理、道德或体面。每一个原则都将被采纳,最符合人类的无序感情。顾客们会被新产业和地址吸引到每个修道院去,以实践民众的热情和信心。 最后,民事法官会发现,他为了自己的节俭付出了高昂的代价,为牧师们保留了固定的场所;实际上,他与精神导师们一起能够做的最体面和最有利的组成,就是贿赂他们的哀伤,为他们的职业分配所报的工资,使他们更加活跃,而不是仅仅为了防止他们的羊群在寻找新的牧师时迷路。教会机构虽然一开始通常来自宗教观点,但最终证明有利于社会的政治利益。”

p204.original: But whatever may have been the good or bad effects of the independent provision of the clergy, it has, perhaps, been very seldom bestowed upon them from any view to those effects. Times of violent religious controversy have generally been times of equally violent political faction. Upon such occasions, each political party has either found it, or imagined it, for his interest, to league itself with some one or other of the contending religious sects. But this could be done only by adopting, or, at least, by favouring the tenets of that particular sect. The sect which had the good fortune to be leagued with the conquering party necessarily shared in the victory of its ally, by whose favour and protection it was soon enabled, in some degree, to silence and subdue all its adversaries. Those adversaries had generally leagued themselves with the enemies of the conquering party, and were, therefore the enemies of that party. The clergy of this particular sect having thus become complete masters of the field, and their influence and authority with the great body of the people being in its highest vigour, they were powerful enough to overawe the chiefs and leaders of their own party, and to oblige the civil magistrate to respect their opinions and inclinations. Their first demand was generally that he should silence and subdue all their adversaries; and their second, that he should bestow an independent provision on themselves. As they had generally contributed a good deal to the victory, it seemed not unreasonable that they should have some share in the spoil. They were weary, besides, of humouring the people, and of depending upon their caprice for a subsistence. In making this demand, therefore, they consulted their own ease and comfort, without troubling themselves about the effect which it might have, in future times, upon the influence and authority of their order. The civil magistrate, who could comply with their demand only by giving them something which he would have chosen much rather to take, or to keep to himself, was seldom very forward to grant it. Necessity, however, always forced him to submit at last, though frequently not till after many delays, evasions, and affected excuses.
p204.zh: 但是,无论神职人员独立供给的好坏影响如何,从任何角度看,都可能很少赋予他们这些影响。暴力宗教争议的时代一般是同样暴力的政治派别的时代。 在这样的情况下,每个政党要么发现,要么为了他的利益,想象着与某一个或某些相互争吵的宗教派别结盟。 但只有采纳,或至少支持该特定教派的原则,才能做到这一点。与被征服的一方结盟的这一支派必然同盟军的胜利一样,通过他们的恩惠和保护,它很快在某种程度上得以保持沉默,征服其所有对手。 这些对手一般都与征服党的敌人结盟,因此是该党的敌人。 这一特定教派的神职人员因此成为该领域的完全主人,他们的影响和权威,人民之大体充满活力,他们的力量足以夸大本党的首领和领导人,迫使民事治安法官尊重他们的意见和倾向。 他们的第一项要求是,他应该保持沉默,制服所有对手;第二项要求是,他应该给自己独立的规定。 由于他们一般都为胜利贡献了很大,因此他们应该拥有一部分战利品,这似乎并非不合理. 他们厌倦了幽默 和依靠他们的奢侈维持生计。 因此,在提出这一要求时,他们参考了自己的轻松和舒适之处,没有担心今后它可能对秩序的影响和权威产生什么影响。民事法官只能满足他们的要求,向他们提供他本来会选择的很多东西,或者保留给自己,但很少会很主动地同意。 然而,必须始终迫使他最终屈服,尽管常常在多次拖延、逃避和有影响的借口之后才能屈服。

p205.original: But if politics had never called in the aid of religion, had the conquering party never adopted the tenets of one sect more than those of another, when it had gained the victory, it would probably have dealt equally and impartially with all the different sects, and have allowed every man to choose his own priest, and his own religion, as he thought proper. There would, and, in this case, no doubt, have been, a great multitude of religious sects. Almost every different congregation might probably have had a little sect by itself, or have entertained some peculiar tenets of its own. Each teacher, would, no doubt, have felt himself under the necessity of making the utmost exertion, and of using every art, both to preserve and to increase the number of his disciples. But as every other teacher would have felt himself under the same necessity, the success of no one teacher, or sect of teachers, could have been very great. The interested and active zeal of religious teachers can be dangerous and troublesome only where there is either but one sect tolerated in the society, or where the whole of a large society is divided into two or three great sects; the teachers of each acting by concert, and under a regular discipline and subordination. But that zeal must be altogether innocent, where the society is divided into two or three hundred, or, perhaps, into as many thousand small sects, of which no one could be considerable enough to disturb the public tranquillity. The teachers of each sect, seeing themselves surrounded on all sides with more adversaries than friends, would be obliged to learn that candour and moderation which are so seldom to be found among the teachers of those great sects, whose tenets, being supported by the civil magistrate, are held in veneration by almost all the inhabitants of extensive kingdoms and empires, and who, therefore, see nothing round them but followers, disciples, and humble admirers. The teachers of each little sect, finding themselves almost alone, would be obliged to respect those of almost every other sect; and the concessions which they would mutually find in both convenient and agreeable to make one to another, might in time, probably reduce the doctrine of the greater part of them to that pure and rational religion, free from every mixture of absurdity, imposture, or fanaticism, such as wise men have, in all ages of the world, wished to see established; but such as positive law has, perhaps, never yet established, and probably never will establish in any country; because, with regard to religion, positive law always has been, and probably always will be, more or less influenced by popular superstition and enthusiasm. This plan of ecclesiastical government, or, more properly, of no ecclesiastical government, was what the sect called Independents (a sect, no doubt, of very wild enthusiasts), proposed to establish in England towards the end of the civil war. If it had been established, though of a very unphilosophical origin, it would probably, by this time, have been productive of the most philosophical good temper and moderation with regard to every sort of religious principle. It has been established in Pennsylvania, where, though the quakers happen to be the most numerous, the law, in reality, favours no one sect more than another; and it is there said to have been productive of this philosophical good temper and moderation.
p205.zh: 但是如果政治从未向宗教求助,如果被征服的政党从未采纳过一个教派比另一个教派的信条,当它获得了胜利时,它很可能已经平等地,公正地对待所有不同的教派,并且允许每个人选择自己的牧师,以及他自己的宗教,正如他认为合适的那样. 在这个案例中,无疑会有众多的宗教派别。几乎每个不同的会众 可能都有一个小教派 或娱乐一些自己的特殊教义。每一个老师,无疑都会觉得自己必须尽最大的努力,必须利用一切艺术,既要保存,又要增加他的门徒人数. 但是,正如其他每一位老师都会觉得自己在同样的必要性之下,没有一位老师或者教师的宗派的成功本来是会非常伟大的.宗教教师的关心和积极热情,只有在社会上只容忍一个教派,或者将一个大社会全社会分为两个或三个大教派的情况下,才能是危险的和麻烦的;每个教派的教师都是通过协奏曲来演绎的,在正规的纪律和从属之下. 但这种热情必须是完全无辜的,社会被分成二三百个,或者也许,分成上千个小教派,其中没有人能足以扰乱公众的安宁.每一教派的教师,看到自己在四面环绕,敌手比友人多,因此不得不学会这些伟大教派的教师中很少找到的坦率和温和,这些教派的教义得到民事法官的支持,几乎被广大王国和帝国的所有居民所崇尚,因此,他们除了追随者、门徒和谦卑的崇拜者之外,看不到任何包围他们的东西。 每个小教派的教师几乎都孤立无援,他们有义务尊重几乎每个其他教派的教师;他们相互之间会发现的让步,既方便又可以相互同意,可能及时将它们中的大部分的教义降低为纯正和理性的宗教,而不受世界各个年龄层中各种荒谬、无礼或狂热的混合,如智者们都希望看到这种教义得到确立;但是,例如实在法也许从未确立过,而且很可能永远不会在任何国家确立;因为,在宗教方面,实在法始终而且可能永远不会受到流行的迷信和热情的影响。 这个教会政府的计划,或者更恰当地说,没有教会政府的计划,是该教派所谓的"独立派"(一个无疑是非常野生的爱好者的一个教派),提议在内战即将结束时在英格兰建立. 如果建立这种制度,尽管它来源于非哲学,但到这个时候,它很可能在每一种宗教原则方面产生了最哲学性的温和和。 它已经在宾夕法尼亚州建立,虽然夸张者恰好是人数最多的,但实际上法律却不偏爱任何一个教派,据说它产生了这种哲学上的好脾气和温和。

p206.original: But though this equality of treatment should not be productive of this good temper and moderation in all, or even in the greater part of the religious sects of a particular country; yet, provided those sects were sufficiently numerous, and each of them consequently too small to disturb the public tranquillity, the excessive zeal of each for its particular tenets could not well be productive of any very hurtful effects, but, on the contrary, of several good ones; and if the government was perfectly decided, both to let them all alone, and to oblige them all to let alone one another, there is little danger that they would not of their own accord, subdivide themselves fast enough, so as soon to become sufficiently numerous.
p206.zh: 但是,虽然这种待遇平等不应产生任何好的温和,甚至某个特定国家的大部分宗教派别;然而,只要这些教派数量足够多,因此每个教派都太小,无法扰乱公众的安宁,但是,每个教派对于其特定教义的过度热衷并不能产生任何非常有害的影响,相反,是几个良好教义;如果政府得到完美决定,既要让所有教派单独存在,又要迫使所有教派彼此单独存在,那么,它们不会自愿地迅速分裂起来,以便尽快足够数量。

p207.original: In every civilized society, in every society where the distinction of ranks has once been completely established, there have been always two different schemes or systems of morality current at the same time; of which the one may be called the strict or austere; the other the liberal, or, if you will, the loose system. The former is generally admired and revered by the common people; the latter is commonly more esteemed and adopted by what are called the people of fashion. The degree of disapprobation with which we ought to mark the vices of levity, the vices which are apt to arise from great prosperity, and from the excess of gaiety and good humour, seems to constitute the principal distinction between those two opposite schemes or systems. In the liberal or loose system, luxury, wanton, and even disorderly mirth, the pursuit of pleasure to some degree of intemperance, the breach of chastity, at least in one of the two sexes, etc. provided they are not accompanied with gross indecency, and do not lead to falsehood and injustice, are generally treated with a good deal of indulgence, and are easily either excused or pardoned altogether. In the austere system, on the contrary, those excesses are regarded with the utmost abhorrence and detestation. The vices of levity are always ruinous to the common people, and a single week's thoughtlessness and dissipation is often sufficient to undo a poor workman for ever, and to drive him, through despair, upon committing the most enormous crimes. The wiser and better sort of the common people, therefore, have always the utmost abhorrence and detestation of such excesses, which their experience tells them are so immediately fatal to people of their condition. The disorder and extravagance of several years, on the contrary, will not always ruin a man of fashion; and people of that rank are very apt to consider the power of indulging in some degree of excess, as one of the advantages of their fortune; and the liberty of doing so without censure or reproach, as one of the privileges which belong to their station. In people of their own station, therefore, they regard such excesses with but a small degree of disapprobation, and censure them either very slightly or not at all.
p207.zh: 在每一个文明社会中,在曾经完全确立等级划分的每一个社会中,总是同时存在两种不同的道德计划或制度;其中一种可以称为严格或严格;另一种是自由的,或者,如果你愿意的话,是松散的制度.前者一般受到普通百姓的钦佩和敬重;后者通常更受到人们的敬重和被所谓的时尚大众所采纳. 我们应当对轻描淡写地的弊端表示不满意,这种弊端可能产生于巨大的繁荣,以及过于粗俗和幽默,这似乎构成了这两种相反的计划或制度之间的主要区别。 在自由或松散的制度中,奢侈,恣意,甚至无序的狂笑,追求愉悦到某种程度的不节制,破坏贞操,至少是在两个性别中之一的贞操等等,只要不伴有严重猥亵,也不导致虚假和不公正,一般会受到相当宽大的待遇,并且很容易被原谅或完全赦免. 相反,在严酷的体系中,这些过分行为被视为极为憎恶和厌恶。奢侈的恶习总是给普通人带来毁灭,一周的无思无虑和散去往往足以永远使一个穷苦的工人彻底解脱,并且通过绝望,使他在犯下最巨大的罪行时被驱赶. 因此,更聪明、更优秀的普通人民总是最憎恶和憎恶这种过分的行为,他们的经验表明,这种行为立即对处于其状况的人造成致命的伤害。 相反,几年的混乱和奢侈不会永远摧毁一个时尚的人;而这种级别的人非常适合将某种程度的过度的沉浸的力量视为他们财富的优势之一;在不受到指责或指责的情况下这样做的自由,是属于他们驻地的特权之一。 因此,在他们自己站的人中,他们只视这种过分行为为小程度的不满意,并对他们进行微小的谴责或根本不谴责。

p208.original: Almost all religious sects have begun among the common people, from whom they have generally drawn their earliest, as well as their most numerous proselytes. The austere system of morality has, accordingly, been adopted by those sects almost constantly, or with very few exceptions; for there have been some. It was the system by which they could best recommend themselves to that order of people, to whom they first proposed their plan of reformation upon what had been before established. Many of them, perhaps the greater part of them, have even endeavoured to gain credit by refining upon this austere system, and by carrying it to some degree of folly and extravagance; and this excessive rigour has frequently recommended them, more than any thing else, to the respect and veneration of the common people.
p208.zh: 几乎所有的宗教派别都从普通人中开始,他们一般都从中汲取最早的,以及最众多的传教士. 因此,这些教派几乎经常采用严格的道德制度,或极少例外;因为有一些教派。 这是他们最能向人民推荐自己的制度,他们首先向人民提出了在建立之前的改造计划。其中许多人,或许是他们中的大部分人,甚至努力通过完善这种苛刻的制度,并通过某种程度的愚蠢和奢侈来获得信用;这种过分的严谨态度经常建议他们,比其他任何事情都更加尊重和敬仰普通人民。

p209.original: A man of rank and fortune is, by his station, the distinguished member of a great society, who attend to every part of his conduct, and who thereby oblige him to attend to every part of it himself. His authority and consideration depend very much upon the respect which this society bears to him. He dares not do anything which would disgrace or discredit him in it; and he is obliged to a very strict observation of that species of morals, whether liberal or austere, which the general consent of this society prescribes to persons of his rank and fortune. A man of low condition, on the contrary, is far from being a distinguished member of any great society. While he remains in a country village, his conduct may be attended to, and he may be obliged to attend to it himself. In this situation, and in this situation only, he may have what is called a character to lose. But as soon as he comes into a great city, he is sunk in obscurity and darkness. His conduct is observed and attended to by nobody; and he is, therefore, very likely to neglect it himself, and to abandon himself to every sort of low profligacy and vice. He never emerges so effectually from this obscurity, his conduct never excites so much the attention of any respectable society, as by his becoming the member of a small religious sect. He from that moment acquires a degree of consideration which he never had before. All his brother sectaries are, for the credit of the sect, interested to observe his conduct; and, if he gives occasion to any scandal, if he deviates very much from those austere morals which they almost always require of one another, to punish him by what is always a very severe punishment, even where no evil effects attend it, expulsion or excommunication from the sect. In little religious sects, accordingly, the morals of the common people have been almost always remarkably regular and orderly; generally much more so than in the established church. The morals of those little sects, indeed, have frequently been rather disagreeably rigorous and unsocial.
p209.zh: 官阶高贵的人,依其职位,是伟大社会的杰出成员,注意其行为的每一部分,从而责成他亲自处理其每一部分. 他的权威和考虑在很大程度上取决于这个社会对他的尊重。 他不敢做任何会使他蒙受耻辱或名誉受损的事情;他有义务严格观察这种道德,无论是自由的还是严厉的,而这种道德是社会普遍同意他的级别和财富的人所应具备的。条件低的人,恰恰相反,远非任何伟大社会的杰出成员. 在他留在乡村村庄期间,他的行为可能会受到注意,他可能有义务亲自去处理。 在这种情况下,而且只有在这种情况下,他可能拥有所谓的性格可以失去. 但一入大城,便沉没于阴暗之中. 他的行为受到任何人的观察和照顾;因此,他极有可能自己忽视了这种行为,并抛弃了一切卑劣的放荡和恶行。 他从未从这种蒙昧中如此有效地出现,他的行为从未像他成为一个小教派的成员那样,如此激起任何受人尊敬的社会的注意. 从那时起,他得到了他从未有过的某种程度的考虑。 他的所有兄弟教派都有意观察他的行为,这是该教派的功劳;如果他制造任何丑闻,如果他非常偏离他们几乎总是相互要求的严酷道德,那么,就应该用永远是十分严厉的惩罚来惩罚他,即使没有恶果发生,就驱逐或断绝该教派的通信。 因此,在很少的宗教派别中,普通人民的道德几乎总是非常正常和有序的;一般比在既定的教会中要多得多。 这些小教派的道德,的确经常相当严谨和不具有社会性。

p210.original: There are two very easy and effectual remedies, however, by whose joint operation the state might, without violence, correct whatever was unsocial or disagreeably rigorous in the morals of all the little sects into which the country was divided.
p210.zh: 然而,有两个非常容易和有效的补救办法,国家可以通过这些补救办法采取联合行动,在不使用暴力的情况下,纠正那些在分裂国家的所有小教派的道德上不合社会或令人不解的苛刻行为。

p211.original: The first of those remedies is the study of science and philosophy, which the state might render almost universal among all people of middling or more than middling rank and fortune; not by giving salaries to teachers in order to make them negligent and idle, but by instituting some sort of probation, even in the higher and more difficult sciences, to be undergone by every person before he was permitted to exercise any liberal profession, or before he could be received as a candidate for any honourable office, of trust or profit. If the state imposed upon this order of men the necessity of learning, it would have no occasion to give itself any trouble about providing them with proper teachers. They would soon find better teachers for themselves, than any whom the state could provide for them. Science is the great antidote to the poison of enthusiasm and superstition; and where all the superior ranks of people were secured from it, the inferior ranks could not be much exposed to it.
p211.zh: 其中第一种补救办法是研究科学和哲学,国家可能使科学和哲学在一切从事干涉工作的人中几乎普遍化,而不只是干涉排名和财富;不是通过向教师发放薪水,使他们失职和闲置,而是通过实行某种缓刑,甚至在较高和难度更高的科学中,在允许每个人从事任何自由职业之前,或在任何荣誉职务、信任或盈利之前,每个人都可以接受这种缓刑。 如果国家要求男子学习,那么它就没有机会为男子提供合适的教师。 他们很快会找到更好的教师,比任何国家能够为他们提供的教师还要好。科学是对热情和迷信的毒药的伟大解药;在从它中保住所有上层人的队伍的地方,低层的队伍也不可能受到太多的暴露.
